ch.zt: 第一篇 · 波希米亚丑闻
p: I.
我。
To Sherlock Holmes she is always the woman.
对于夏洛克·福尔摩斯，她总是那个女人。
I have seldom heard him mention her under any other name.
我很少听到他以她以外的任何名字提及她。
In his eyes she eclipses and predominates the whole of her sex.
在他的眼中，她超越了和主宰了整个女性。
It was not that he felt any emotion akin to love for Irene Adler.
他并不是对伊丽莎白·阿德勒有丝毫类似爱情的感情。
All emotions, and that one particularly, were abhorrent to his cold, precise but admirably balanced mind.
所有感情，尤其是这种感情，都对他冷漠、精确但非常平衡的理智是厌恶的。
He was, I take it, the most perfect reasoning and observing machine that the world has seen, but as a lover he would have placed himself in a false position.
他，我认为，是这个世界上见过的最完美的推理和观察机器，但作为一个情人，他将自己置于一个错误的位置。
He never spoke of the softer passions, save with a gibe and a sneer.
他从不提及那些更温柔的感情，除了用一个嘲弄和一个轻蔑的微笑。
They were admirable things for the observer—excellent for drawing the veil from men’s motives and actions.
它们对于观察者来说是极好的东西——对于揭开男人动机和行为的帷幕非常出色。

But for the trained reasoner to admit such intrusions into his own delicate and finely adjusted temperament was to introduce a distracting factor which might throw a doubt upon all his mental results.
但对于训练有素的推理者承认这些干扰因素进入他的极其精细和调整的气质，这将引入一个干扰因素，可能使所有他的精神结果产生怀疑。
Grit in a sensitive instrument, or a crack in one of his own high-power lenses, would not be more disturbing than a strong emotion in a nature such as his.
在一个敏感的仪器中，或者在自己高功率的镜头中，灰尘不会比强烈的情感对他的性格更打扰。
And yet there was but one woman to him, and that woman was the late Irene Adler, of dubious and questionable memory.
但对一个训练有素的推理者来说，承认这些干扰因素进入他的极其精细和调整的气质，这将引入一个干扰因素，可能使所有他的精神结果产生怀疑。
I had seen little of Holmes lately.
我最近见到福尔摩斯很少。
My marriage had drifted us away from each other.
我的婚姻使我们远离彼此。

My own complete happiness, and the home-centred interests which rise up around the man who first finds himself master of his own establishment, were sufficient to absorb all my attention, while Holmes, who loathed every form of society with his whole Bohemian soul, remained in our lodgings in Baker Street, buried among his old books, and alternating from week to week between cocaine and ambition, the drowsiness of the drug, and the fierce energy of his own keen nature.
我自己的完全幸福，以及围绕着那个首先发现自己掌握自己建立的事业中心的人，上升起来的家中心的个人利益，都是足够的，而福尔摩斯，他厌恶所有形式的社会，他整个的博尔梅安灵魂，仍然在我们贝尔街的旅馆里，埋在旧书里，交替从一周到一周，从卡因到野心，药物的困倦和他自己的敏锐的天性，狂热的能量。

He was still, as ever, deeply attracted by the study of crime, and occupied his immense faculties and extraordinary powers of observation in following out those clues, and clearing up those mysteries which had been abandoned as hopeless by the official police.
他仍然对犯罪研究深感兴趣，利用自己庞大的思维能力和非凡的观察力，追踪线索，解开那些被官方警察放弃的谜团。

From time to time I heard some vague account of his doings: of his summons to Odessa in the case of the Trepoff murder, of his clearing up of the singular tragedy of the Atkinson brothers at Trincomalee, and finally of the mission which he had accomplished so delicately and successfully for the reigning family of Holland.
不时地，我听到有关他的一些模糊的报道：在托普夫谋杀案中被召到敖德萨，他在特林科莱特的阿特金森兄弟的奇异悲剧中解决了问题，最后，他为荷兰王室完成了一项极其巧妙和成功的使命。
Beyond these signs of his activity, however, which I merely shared with all the readers of the daily press, I knew little of my former friend and companion.
除了这些活动的迹象，我只和所有每天报纸的读者一样知道我的旧友和同伴。
One night—it was on the twentieth of March, 1888—I was returning from a journey to a patient (for I had now returned to civil practice), when my way led me through Baker Street.
一个晚上——那是1888年3月20日——我从一个病人那里回来（因为我现在又回到了民事执业），当我走过贝克街那熟悉的门，它总是与我追求和暗黑的《红楼子》研究室的黑暗事件相关联，我被一种强烈的愿望抓住，想再次见到霍尔姆斯，并知道他如何利用他的非凡能力。

As I passed the well-remembered door, which must always be associated in my mind with my wooing, and with the dark incidents of the Study in Scarlet, I was seized with a keen desire to see Holmes again, and to know how he was employing his extraordinary powers.
当我经过那熟悉的门时，我看到他的高大、瘦削的身材两次在暗影中闪过。
His rooms were brilliantly lit, and, even as I looked up, I saw his tall, spare figure pass twice in a dark silhouette against the blind.
他快速地在房间里走动，急切地，头低垂在胸口，双手握在背后。
He was pacing the room swiftly, eagerly, with his head sunk upon his chest and his hands clasped behind him.
对我来说，我了解他的每一个情绪和习惯，他的态度和方式都讲述了自己的故事。
To me, who knew his every mood and habit, his attitude and manner told their own story.
他正在工作。
He was at work again.
他再次醒来。
He had risen out of his drug-created dreams and was hot upon the scent of some new problem.
他从药物创造的梦中醒来，对一个新问题在追索中。
I rang the bell and was shown up to the chamber which had formerly been in part my own.
我按响了门铃，被带到了以前部分是我的房间的房间。
His manner was not effusive.
他的态度并不热情。
It seldom was; but he was glad, I think, to see me.
他很少是不热情的，但我想，见到我，他很高兴。
With hardly a word spoken, but with a kindly eye, he waved me to an armchair, threw across his case of cigars, and indicated a spirit case and a gasogene in the corner.
他几乎不说什么，但用一个友好的眼神看着我，他把我带到一把椅子上，把他的烟斗放在一个烟斗架上，指示一个酒瓶和一个煤气灯在角落。
Then he stood before the fire and looked me over in his singular introspective fashion.
然后他站在火炉前，用他独特的反思方式看着我。
“Wedlock suits you,” he remarked.
“婚姻适合你。”他说道。
“I think, Watson, that you have put on seven and a half pounds since I saw you.”
“我猜想，华生，自从我上次见到你，你增重了七磅半。”
“Seven!”
I answered.
我答道。
“Indeed, I should have thought a little more.
“的确，我应该多想一些。”
Just a trifle more, I fancy, Watson.
“不过，我想，华生，你大概只多了一点。”
And in practice again, I observe.
“而且在实际生活中，我观察到。”
You did not tell me that you intended to go into harness.”
“你没有告诉我，你打算要上马。”
“Then, how do you know?”
“那么，你怎么知道的呢？”
“I see it, I deduce it.
“我看到的，我推断的。”
How do I know that you have been getting yourself very wet lately, and that you have a most clumsy and careless servant girl?”
我怎么知道你最近变得很湿，而且你有个最笨且粗心的女仆呢？”
“My dear Holmes,” said I, “this is too much.
“亲爱的华生，这太过了。”
You would certainly have been burned, had you lived a few centuries ago.
“如果你生活在几个世纪以前，你肯定会被烧死的。”
It is true that I had a country walk on Thursday and came home in a dreadful mess, but as I have changed my clothes I can’t imagine how you deduce it.
“确实，我星期四有了一次乡村散步，回来的时候弄得一团糟，不过因为我换了衣服，我不能想象你是怎么推断的。”
As to Mary Jane, she is incorrigible, and my wife has given her notice, but there, again, I fail to see how you work it out.”
“至于玛丽·简，她顽固不化，我妻子已经通知她了，不过，我又怎么推断出的呢？”
He chuckled to himself and rubbed his long, nervous hands together.
他自言自语地笑了，搓着他那长长的、紧张的手。
“It is simplicity itself,” said he; “my eyes tell me that on the inside of your left shoe, just where the firelight strikes it, the leather is scored by six almost parallel cuts.
“这很简单。”他说，“我的眼睛告诉我，你的左鞋内侧，就在火光照射的地方，皮革上被六条几乎平行的切痕划过。
Obviously they have been caused by someone who has very carelessly scraped round the edges of the sole in order to remove crusted mud from it.
显然，它们是被一个非常粗心地在鞋底边缘刮去泥垢的人造成的。
Hence, you see, my double deduction that you had been out in vile weather, and that you had a particularly malignant boot-slitting specimen of the London slavey.
因此，你看，我的双重推断，你曾出过门，在恶劣的天气里，你穿了一双特别恶毒的伦敦奴隶的靴子。

As to your practice, if a gentleman walks into my rooms smelling of iodoform, with a black mark of nitrate of silver upon his right forefinger, and a bulge on the right side of his top-hat to show where he has secreted his stethoscope, I must be dull, indeed, if I do not pronounce him to be an active member of the medical profession.”
关于你的习惯，如果一个绅士走进我的房间，身上带着碘酒的气味，右手指上有一块硝酸银的印记，帽子的右侧有一个肿胀的地方，显示他藏了听诊器，我必须是愚蠢透顶，否则我不会把这个人判定为医学界的活跃成员。
I could not help laughing at the ease with which he explained his process of deduction.
我忍不住笑他解释推理过程的轻松。

“When I hear you give your reasons,” I remarked, “the thing always appears to me to be so ridiculously simple that I could easily do it myself, though at each successive instance of your reasoning I am baffled until you explain your process.
“当你听到你给出理由时，事情总是看起来如此简单，以至于我很容易自己做，尽管每次你推理，我都被迷惑，直到你解释你的过程。
And yet I believe that my eyes are as good as yours.”
而且我相信，我的眼睛和你的眼睛一样好。
“Quite so,” he answered, lighting a cigarette, and throwing himself down into an armchair.
“完全正确。”他回答，点燃了一支雪茄，瘫坐在一把扶手椅上。
“You see, but you do not observe.
“你看，但你没有观察。
The distinction is clear.
区别是清楚的。
For example, you have frequently seen the steps which lead up from the hall to this room.”
例如，你经常看到从大厅到这个房间的楼梯。
“Frequently.”
“经常。”
“How often?”
“多少次？”
“Well, some hundreds of times.”
“嗯，几百次。”
“Then how many are there?”
那么一共有多少个？
“How many?
如何 many ？
I don’t know.”
我不知道。
“Quite so!
非常对!
You have not observed.
你并未察觉。
And yet you have seen.
然而你却看到了。
That is just my point.
那是我的意思。
Now, I know that there are seventeen steps, because I have both seen and observed.
现在，我知道有十七级台阶，因为我既见过也观察过。
By the way, since you are interested in these little problems, and since you are good enough to chronicle one or two of my trifling experiences, you may be interested in this.”
顺便说一下，既然您对这些小问题感兴趣，既然您愿意记录我一些琐碎经历中的一个或两个，您或许会对这一问题感兴趣。
He threw over a sheet of thick, pink-tinted notepaper which had been lying open upon the table.
他扔过一张厚纸片，纸片上摊开着，上面印着淡粉色的稿纸。
“It came by the last post,” said he.
“是最后邮包寄来的，”他说道。
“Read it aloud.”
读出来。
The note was undated, and without either signature or address.
那张字条没有写日期，也没有签名和地址。
“There will call upon you to-night, at a quarter to eight o’clock,” it said, “a gentleman who desires to consult you upon a matter of the very deepest moment.
“今晚八点一刻将会来拜访你，”它写道，“一个对一件极为重要的事情想向你咨询的先生。”
Your recent services to one of the royal houses of Europe have shown that you are one who may safely be trusted with matters which are of an importance which can hardly be exaggerated.
你最近为欧洲的一个皇家家庭服务，已表明你可以安全地被委托处理一些极其重要的事务，其重要性几乎无法夸大。
This account of you we have from all quarters received.
这是来自各方的关于你的报告。
Be in your chamber then at that hour, and do not take it amiss if your visitor wear a mask.”
到那时请到你的房间，如果你的访客戴面具，不要介意。
“This is indeed a mystery,” I remarked.
“这确实是一个谜。”我评论道。
“What do you imagine that it means?”
“你想象它意味着什么？”
“I have no data yet.
“我还没有数据。
It is a capital mistake to theorise before one has data.
理论先行，是资本的错误。
Insensibly one begins to twist facts to suit theories, instead of theories to suit facts.
不自觉地，一个人开始把事实扭曲以适应理论，而不是把理论扭曲以适应事实。
But the note itself.
但那张纸本身。
What do you deduce from it?”
你从它推导出什么？”
I carefully examined the writing, and the paper upon which it was written.
我仔细检查了书写，以及上面写的纸张。
“The man who wrote it was presumably well to do,” I remarked, endeavouring to imitate my companion’s processes.
“写这张纸的人似乎是很有钱的。”我评论道，试图模仿我的同伴的进程。
“Such paper could not be bought under half a crown a packet.
“这种纸不可能半镑钱一包买得到。
It is peculiarly strong and stiff.”
它特别强韧且挺直。
“Peculiar—that is the very word,” said Holmes.
“特别——这句话正是。”说霍尔姆斯。
“It is not an English paper at all.
“它不是英格兰纸张。
Hold it up to the light.”
请举起来看。
I did so, and saw a large “E” with a small “g,” a “P,” and a large “G” with a small “t” woven into the texture of the paper.
我照做了，发现一张纸上有“E”和“g”、“P”和“t”等符号交织在一起。
“What do you make of that?” asked Holmes.
“你对这个怎么看？”夏洛克问道。
“The name of the maker, no doubt; or his monogram, rather.”
“这个名字，当然；或者他的缩写。”
“Not at all.
“不，不。
The ‘G’ with the small ‘t’ stands for ‘Gesellschaft,’ which is the German for ‘Company.’
“‘G’ 小写 ‘t’ 表示 ‘Gesellschaft’，这是德语中的 ‘Company’。
It is a customary contraction like our ‘Co.’
这是一个类似我们“Co.”的缩写。
‘P,’ of course, stands for ‘Papier.’
“P”当然代表“Papier”。
Now for the ‘Eg.’
现在是“Eg”。
Let us glance at our Continental Gazetteer.”
让我们看看我们的《大陆报导》。
He took down a heavy brown volume from his shelves.
他从书架上取下一本厚棕色的书。
“Eglow, Eglonitz—here we are, Egria.
埃洛格，埃洛尼茨——找到了，埃莉亚。
It is in a German-speaking country—in Bohemia, not far from Carlsbad.
它位于一个德语区——在捷克，离卡尔萨布斯不远。
‘Remarkable as being the scene of the death of Wallenstein, and for its numerous glass-factories and paper-mills.’
“这是一个非常有趣的地方，因为它曾是瓦尔特林顿的所在地，而且这里有许多玻璃工厂和纸厂。”
Ha, ha, my boy, what do you make of that?”
哈，哈，我的孩子，你对这个怎么看？
His eyes sparkled, and he sent up a great blue triumphant cloud from his cigarette.
他的眼睛闪烁着，他从烟斗里吐出了一团巨大的蓝色胜利云。
“The paper was made in Bohemia,” I said.
“那张纸是用波希米亚纸做的，”我说。
“Precisely.
“准确。”
And the man who wrote the note is a German.
写这封信的人是德国人。
Do you note the peculiar construction of the sentence—‘This account of you we have from all quarters received.’
你注意到这句奇怪的句子结构——“我们从四面八方收到关于你的这番报道。”
A Frenchman or Russian could not have written that.
法国人或俄罗斯人不可能写这封信。
It is the German who is so uncourteous to his verbs.
这个德国人对他的动词太不礼貌了。
It only remains, therefore, to discover what is wanted by this German who writes upon Bohemian paper and prefers wearing a mask to showing his face.
因此，唯一要解决的问题就是这个德国人写在波希米亚纸上，喜欢戴面具而不愿意露面。
And here he comes, if I am not mistaken, to resolve all our doubts.”
他来了，如果我没猜错的话，要解决我们所有的疑问。
As he spoke there was the sharp sound of horses’ hoofs and grating wheels against the curb, followed by a sharp pull at the bell.
他说话时，传来马蹄声和马蹄与门槛摩擦的声音，随后是一声尖锐的铃铛拉响声。
Holmes whistled.
森德尔吹起了口哨。
“A pair, by the sound,” said he.
“两匹，根据声音。”他说。
“Yes,” he continued, glancing out of the window.
“是的，”他继续说，瞥了窗外一眼。
“A nice little brougham and a pair of beauties.
“一辆漂亮的双轮马车，两匹漂亮的马。”
A hundred and fifty guineas apiece.
两百五十英镑。
There’s money in this case, Watson, if there is nothing else.”
这里有钱，华生，除了别的。
“I think that I had better go, Holmes.”
“我觉得最好走了，华生。”
“Not a bit, Doctor.
“不，医生。
Stay where you are.
你待在这里。
I am lost without my Boswell.
我没有我的博尔伍德。
And this promises to be interesting.
这听起来很有趣。
It would be a pity to miss it.”
真可惜错过。
“But your client—”
“但是你的客户——”
“Never mind him.
“别管他。
I may want your help, and so may he.
我可能需要你的帮助，他可能也需要。
Here he comes.
他来了。
Sit down in that armchair, Doctor, and give us your best attention.”
坐在这把扶手椅上，医生，给我们最专注的注意。”
A slow and heavy step, which had been heard upon the stairs and in the passage, paused immediately outside the door.
一阵缓慢而沉重的脚步声，曾在楼梯和走廊里听到，立即停在了门外。
Then there was a loud and authoritative tap.
然后，一阵响亮而权威的敲门声。
“Come in!” said Holmes.
“进来吧！”说：“华生。”
A man entered who could hardly have been less than six feet six inches in height, with the chest and limbs of a Hercules.
一个身高六英尺六英寸的男子走进来，身材和四肢都像一个大力士。
His dress was rich with a richness which would, in England, be looked upon as akin to bad taste.
他的衣服是富丽堂皇的，这在英国会被看作是粗俗的品味。

Heavy bands of astrakhan were slashed across the sleeves and fronts of his double-breasted coat, while the deep blue cloak which was thrown over his shoulders was lined with flame-coloured silk and secured at the neck with a brooch which consisted of a single flaming beryl.
他的双排扣大衣袖口和前襟上用亚麻布条子割得稀里哗啦的，而他披在肩上的深蓝色大衣里里外外都用火红的丝绸镶边，还系着一个用一颗红宝石做成的扣子。
Boots which extended halfway up his calves, and which were trimmed at the tops with rich brown fur, completed the impression of barbaric opulence which was suggested by his whole appearance.
他的靴子延伸到膝盖一半的位置，靴子的顶部用棕色的皮毛装饰，完美地展现了他那粗犷奢华的外表。

He carried a broad-brimmed hat in his hand, while he wore across the upper part of his face, extending down past the cheekbones, a black vizard mask, which he had apparently adjusted that very moment, for his hand was still raised to it as he entered.
他手里拿着一顶宽边的帽子，脸上戴着一个黑色的面具，从下巴到脸颊，一直延伸到下巴，这个面具显然是刚刚调整好的，因为他的手还举着面具，似乎在等待着什么。
From the lower part of the face he appeared to be a man of strong character, with a thick, hanging lip, and a long, straight chin suggestive of resolution pushed to the length of obstinacy.
从下部看，他似乎是一个性格坚强的人，嘴唇厚实，下巴直挺，暗示着决断到了极点的顽固。
“You had my note?” he asked with a deep harsh voice and a strongly marked German accent.
“你有我的信吗？”他用深沉而带有明显德国口音的声音问道。
“I told you that I would call.”
“我告诉你我会来的。”
He looked from one to the other of us, as if uncertain which to address.
他从我们中间打量着，似乎不知道该向谁致意。
“Pray take a seat,” said Holmes.
“请坐吧。”说者为赫尔克里·波洛。
“This is my friend and colleague, Dr. Watson, who is occasionally good enough to help me in my cases.
“这是我的朋友和同事，我偶尔会帮助我的案件的，叫作约瑟夫·沃森的医生。”
Whom have I the honour to address?”
“我是要向谁致意呢？”
“You may address me as the Count Von Kramm, a Bohemian nobleman.
“你可以叫我作克劳姆伯爵，一个波希米亚的贵族。
I understand that this gentleman, your friend, is a man of honour and discretion, whom I may trust with a matter of the most extreme importance.

福斯特街挤满了红头发的人，普普巷看起来像小贩的橙子摊。
I should not have thought there were so many in the whole country as were brought together by that single advertisement.
我以为整个国家里聚集起来的，也不过如此之多，都因为那一条广告。
Every shade of colour they were—straw, lemon, orange, brick, Irish-setter, liver, clay; but, as Spaulding said, there were not many who had the real vivid flame-coloured tint.
每种颜色他们都有——草绿、柠檬黄、橙色、砖红、爱尔兰 Setter、肝脏色、土黄色；但正如斯帕林所说，拥有那种真正的鲜明火焰色的并不多。

How he did it I could not imagine, but he pushed and pulled and butted until he got me through the crowd, and right up to the steps which led to the office.

二楼楼梯上，有两条人流，有的怀着希望，有的沮丧地回来。但我们挤进去，尽量了，很快发现自己进了办公室。

我不愿轻易失去这样一个地方，因此，既然我听说你有能力给需要帮助的穷人提供建议，我就立刻来到这里。
“And you did very wisely,” said Holmes.
“你做得非常明智。”说的是一边。
“Your case is an exceedingly remarkable one, and I shall be happy to look into it.
"您的案子非常特别，我乐意一探究竟。"
From what you have told me I think that it is possible that graver issues hang from it than might at first sight appear.”
"根据你所讲，我认为这背后可能隐藏着比表面上看起来更严重的议题。"

"非常严重！" 朱巴先生说。
“Why, I have lost four pound a week.”
"我一周亏了四镑。"

"相反，你比我更富，而且在每一个涉及字母 A 的领域里，你都获得了微小的知识。你没有因为这些而损失什么。"
“No, sir.
"不，先生。
But I want to find out about them, and who they are, and what their object was in playing this prank—if it was a prank—upon me.
但我想要弄清楚这些，以及他们是谁，以及他们为什么对我搞这个恶作剧——如果这是恶作剧的话。"
It was a pretty expensive joke for them, for it cost them two and thirty pounds.”
"他们花了一笔不小的代价，因为这花了他们二十五镑。"
“We shall endeavour to clear up these points for you.
"我们将尽力澄清这些点。
And, first, one or two questions, Mr. Wilson.

This assistant of yours who first called your attention to the advertisement—how long had he been with you?”
你最初引起你注意的那个助手，他在这个人身上工作了多久？"
“About a month then.”
"大约一个月。"
“How did he come?”
"他是怎么来的？"
“In answer to an advertisement.”
"在回答一则广告。"
“Was he the only applicant?”
"他是唯一的申请者吗？"
“No, I had a dozen.”
"不，我有十几个。"
“Why did you pick him?”
"你为什么选他？"

“At half wages, in fact.”
"实际上，半薪。"
“Yes.”
"是的。"
“What is he like, this Vincent Spaulding?”
"他长什么样，维恩·斯帕尔丁？"
“Small, stout-built, very quick in his ways, no hair on his face, though he’s not short of thirty.
"个子不高，体型健壮，做事机灵，脸上没有胡须，虽然三十多岁了。"
Has a white splash of acid upon his forehead.”
他额头有块白色的酸渍。
Holmes sat up in his chair in considerable excitement.
森德尔坐起来，非常激动。
“I thought as much,” said he.

“Have you ever observed that his ears are pierced for earrings?”

“Yes, sir.
"是的，先生。"
He told me that a gipsy had done it for him when he was a lad.”
他说，他小时候，一个吉普赛人帮他把耳朵穿了耳钉。
“Hum!” said Holmes, sinking back in deep thought.

"你不在的时候，你的生意有处理吗？"
“Nothing to complain of, sir.
"没有什么可抱怨的，先生。"
There’s never very much to do of a morning.”
"早上没什么事要做。"
“That will do, Mr. Wilson.
"那就可以了，威尔逊先生。"
I shall be happy to give you an opinion upon the subject in the course of a day or two.
"我会在两天内给你一个关于这个问题的意见。"
To-day is Saturday, and I hope that by Monday we may come to a conclusion.”
"今天是星期六，我希望到星期一我们能得出结论。"
“Well, Watson,” said Holmes when our visitor had left us, “what do you make of it all?”
"好了，华生先生，"说时柯南道尔先生对我们来访者离开后，"你对这一切是怎么看的？"
“I make nothing of it,” I answered frankly.
"我对这一切没什么看法，"我坦率地回答。
“It is a most mysterious business.”
"这是一桩最神秘的业务。"
“As a rule,” said Holmes, “the more bizarre a thing is the less mysterious it proves to be.
"一般来说，越是怪异的事，就越不神秘。"
It is your commonplace, featureless crimes which are really puzzling, just as a commonplace face is the most difficult to identify.
"你的平凡的、无特征的犯罪，实际上是最令人费解的，就像平凡的面孔是最难辨认的。"
But I must be prompt over this matter.”
"但是我要快些。"
“What are you going to do, then?”
"你打算怎么办？"
I asked.
我问。
“To smoke,” he answered.
“抽烟。”他回答。
“It is quite a three pipe problem, and I beg that you won’t speak to me for fifty minutes.”
“这是一个三管烟的问题，我请求您不要和我交谈五十分钟。”
He curled himself up in his chair, with his thin knees drawn up to his hawk-like nose, and there he sat with his eyes closed and his black clay pipe thrusting out like the bill of some strange bird.
他蜷缩在椅子上，把瘦小的膝盖缩到鹰一样的鼻子下，闭上眼睛，他的黑色泥烟管像某种奇怪的鸟的喙一样挺立着。

I had come to the conclusion that he had dropped asleep, and indeed was nodding myself, when he suddenly sprang out of his chair with the gesture of a man who has made up his mind and put his pipe down upon the mantelpiece.
我已经得出结论，他睡着了，事实上我也在打盹，这时他突然从椅子上跳起来，像一个已经下定决心的人，把烟管放在壁炉台上。
“Sarasate plays at the St. James’s Hall this afternoon,” he remarked.
“萨拉萨特今天下午在圣詹姆斯大厅演奏。”他说道。
“What do you think, Watson?
“沃森先生，你觉得如何？”
Could your patients spare you for a few hours?”
你的病人可以让你休息几个小时吗？”
“I have nothing to do to-day.
“今天我没有事情可做。”
My practice is never very absorbing.”
我的诊所从不很吸引人。
“Then put on your hat and come.
“那么戴上帽子，来吧。
I am going through the City first, and we can have some lunch on the way.
我先要穿过城市，我们可以在路上吃点东西。
I observe that there is a good deal of German music on the programme, which is rather more to my taste than Italian or French.
我注意到节目单上有不少德国音乐，这对我来说比意大利或法国的要更合口味。
It is introspective, and I want to introspect.
它是内省的，我想要内省。
Come along!”
来吧！”
We travelled by the Underground as far as Aldersgate; and a short walk took us to Saxe-Coburg Square, the scene of the singular story which we had listened to in the morning.
我们乘坐地铁到了阿德尔格莱特，然后步行到萨克森-科堡广场，那里是我们在早上听过的奇异故事的地点。

It was a poky, little, shabby-genteel place, where four lines of dingy two-storied brick houses looked out into a small railed-in enclosure, where a lawn of weedy grass and a few clumps of faded laurel bushes made a hard fight against a smoke-laden and uncongenial atmosphere.
这是一个简陋、小气、绅士风格的地方，有四行灰暗的两层砖房，它们面向一个小围栏，围栏里有一块杂草丛生的草地和几丛褪色的紫罗兰，与烟熏和不舒适的气氛作斗争。
Three gilt balls and a brown board with “JABEZ WILSON” in white letters, upon a corner house, announced the place where our red-headed client carried on his business.
在一栋带有金色球体和棕色板子的角落房子上，写着“杰巴兹·威尔逊”，宣布了我们红发客户做生意的地方。
Sherlock Holmes stopped in front of it with his head on one side and looked it all over, with his eyes shining brightly between puckered lids.
森林·霍尔姆斯站在那里，头歪向一边，仔细打量着，眼睛在紧闭的睫毛间闪闪发光。
Then he walked slowly up the street, and then down again to the corner, still looking keenly at the houses.
然后他慢慢地沿着街道走，然后又走回来，仍然仔细地盯着房子。
Finally he returned to the pawnbroker’s, and, having thumped vigorously upon the pavement with his stick two or three times, he went up to the door and knocked.
最后他回到当铺，用拐杖猛击了几下地面，然后走近门口敲了两下。
It was instantly opened by a bright-looking, clean-shaven young fellow, who asked him to step in.
门立刻被一个明亮、干净的年轻男子打开，他问道他如何从这里到大英街。
“Thank you,” said Holmes, “I only wished to ask you how you would go from here to the Strand.”
“谢谢您，”说霍尔姆斯，“我只是想问您从这里到大英街如何走。”
“Third right, fourth left,” answered the assistant promptly, closing the door.
“第三右，第四左”，助手迅速回答，关门。
“Smart fellow, that,” observed Holmes as we walked away.
“聪明的家伙，”霍尔姆斯说，我们走着。
“He is, in my judgment, the fourth smartest man in London, and for daring I am not sure that he has not a claim to be third.
“他，在我的判断中，是伦敦第四聪明的人，而且我怀疑他是否没有资格是第三。
I have known something of him before.”
我之前知道一些他。”
“Evidently,” said I, “Mr. Wilson’s assistant counts for a good deal in this mystery of the Red-headed League.
“显然，”我说，“杰巴兹·威尔逊的助手在这一谜团中起着重要作用。”
I am sure that you inquired your way merely in order that you might see him.”
我确信你只是想知道怎么走，以便看到他。”
“Not him.”
“不是他。”
“What then?”
“那么呢？”
“The knees of his trousers.”
“他的裤子膝盖处。”
“And what did you see?”
“你看到什么了？”
“What I expected to see.”
“我所期待看到的。”
“Why did you beat the pavement?”
“你为什么踩碎了路面？”
“My dear doctor, this is a time for observation, not for talk.
“亲爱的医生，这是观察的时候，不是说话的时候。
We are spies in an enemy’s country.
我们是敌人国家的间谍。
We know something of Saxe-Coburg Square.
我们对萨克森-科堡广场有所了解。
Let us now explore the parts which lie behind it.”
现在我们来探索它后面的部分。
The road in which we found ourselves as we turned round the corner from the retired Saxe-Coburg Square presented as great a contrast to it as the front of a picture does to the back.
我们发现自己在拐角处，从萨克森-科堡广场退居的街道上，呈现出与它截然不同的景象，就像一幅画的前部与背面相比，前者更显生动。
It was one of the main arteries which conveyed the traffic of the City to the north and west.
它是连接城市北部和西部的主干道。
The roadway was blocked with the immense stream of commerce flowing in a double tide inward and outward, while the footpaths were black with the hurrying swarm of pedestrians.
道路被巨大的商业流注入双流，而行人路径则黑压压地涌动着匆匆的行人。

It was difficult to realise as we looked at the line of fine shops and stately business premises that they really abutted on the other side upon the faded and stagnant square which we had just quitted.
我们看着这条线上的店铺和宏伟的商业建筑，很难想象它们真的在另一边与我们刚刚离开的褪色和停滞的广场相邻。
“Let me see,” said Holmes, standing at the corner and glancing along the line, “I should like just to remember the order of the houses here.
“让我看看，”说霍尔姆斯，站在拐角处，凝视着这条线，“我希望能记住这些房子的顺序。”
It is a hobby of mine to have an exact knowledge of London.
这是我对伦敦的爱好，我有精确的了解。
There is Mortimer’s, the tobacconist, the little newspaper shop, the Coburg branch of the City and Suburban Bank, the Vegetarian Restaurant, and McFarlane’s carriage-building depot.
有莫特里姆的，烟草店，小报铺，柯伯格城郊银行分行，素食餐馆，麦克弗兰的车床制造店。
That carries us right on to the other block.
这就带我们到了另一块地。
And now, Doctor, we’ve done our work, so it’s time we had some play.
现在，医生，我们已经完成了工作，所以该是娱乐的时候了。
A sandwich and a cup of coffee, and then off to violin-land, where all is sweetness and delicacy and harmony, and there are no red-headed clients to vex us with their conundrums.”
一份三明治和一杯咖啡，然后去音乐之国，那里一切都是甜蜜、精致和和谐，没有红发客户会让我们头疼。
My friend was an enthusiastic musician, being himself not only a very capable performer but a composer of no ordinary merit.
我的朋友是个热心的音乐家，他自己不仅是一个非常出色的表演者，而且也是一个不凡的音乐家。

All the afternoon he sat in the stalls wrapped in the most perfect happiness, gently waving his long, thin fingers in time to the music, while his gently smiling face and his languid, dreamy eyes were as unlike those of Holmes the sleuth-hound, Holmes the relentless, keen-witted, ready-handed criminal agent, as it was possible to conceive.
全天他都坐在戏台里，裹着最完美的幸福，轻轻挥动着长长的、瘦削的手指，随着音乐节拍，他的脸上带着温柔的笑容，眼神迷离，像极了侦探猎犬霍尔姆斯，像极了那不那么机警、敏锐、反应迅速的犯罪分子。

In his singular character the dual nature alternately asserted itself, and his extreme exactness and astuteness represented, as I have often thought, the reaction against the poetic and contemplative mood which occasionally predominated in him.
他独特的性格，双面性交替出现，他的极端精确和机敏代表了他偶尔出现的诗性和沉思的反面。

The swing of his nature took him from extreme languor to devouring energy; and, as I knew well, he was never so truly formidable as when, for days on end, he had been lounging in his armchair amid his improvisations and his black-letter editions.
他的性格起伏不定，从极度的慵懒到吞噬的精力；我知道，他从长时间的弹奏和黑体书籍中，变得异常可怕。

Then it was that the lust of the chase would suddenly come upon him, and that his brilliant reasoning power would rise to the level of intuition, until those who were unacquainted with his methods would look askance at him as on a man whose knowledge was not that of other mortals.
然后，猎奇的欲望就会突然降临，他的卓越的推理能力就会达到直觉的水平，那些不认识他的人都会对他感到奇怪，就像一个非人类的智者。
When I saw him that afternoon so enwrapped in the music at St. James’s Hall I felt that an evil time might be coming upon those whom he had set himself to hunt down.
当我那天下午看到他在圣詹姆斯大厅里裹着音乐时，我感觉，要找他的人可能会遇到麻烦。
“You want to go home, no doubt, Doctor,” he remarked as we emerged.
“你打算回家，对吧，医生？”他说道，我们出来时。
“Yes, it would be as well.”
“是的，最好。”
“And I have some business to do which will take some hours.
“还有些事情要处理，需要一些时间。”
This business at Coburg Square is serious.”
这些事情在柯伯格广场是严肃的。
“Why serious?”
“为什么严肃？”
“A considerable crime is in contemplation.
有重大犯罪在策划中。
I have every reason to believe that we shall be in time to stop it.
我确信我们今天晚上能够阻止它。
But to-day being Saturday rather complicates matters.
但今天是星期六，这使得事情复杂化了。
I shall want your help to-night.”
我需要你的帮助今晚。
“At what time?”
“几点了？”
“Ten will be early enough.”
“十点应该来得及。”
“I shall be at Baker Street at ten.”
“我十点到贝克街。”
“Very well.
“好的。
And, I say, Doctor, there may be some little danger, so kindly put your army revolver in your pocket.”
我说，医生，也许会有点危险，你把你的军用手枪藏在口袋里。”
He waved his hand, turned on his heel, and disappeared in an instant among the crowd.
他挥了挥手，转身消失在人群之中。
I trust that I am not more dense than my neighbours, but I was always oppressed with a sense of my own stupidity in my dealings with Sherlock Holmes.
我希望我不是比邻居们更愚蠢，但我总觉得自己在处理与夏洛克·福尔摩斯的关系上总是愚蠢的。

Here I had heard what he had heard, I had seen what he had seen, and yet from his words it was evident that he saw clearly not only what had happened but what was about to happen, while to me the whole business was still confused and grotesque.
我在这里听到的，我看到的，但他的话语表明，他不仅看到了已经发生的事情，而且看到了即将发生的，而对我来说，整个事情仍然混乱和荒诞。

As I drove home to my house in Kensington I thought over it all, from the extraordinary story of the red-headed copier of the Encyclopædia down to the visit to Saxe-Coburg Square, and the ominous words with which he had parted from me.
当我驾车回家，在肯辛顿，我思考了从红发复印百科全书的故事到拜访萨克森-科堡广场，以及他离开我的那句令人不安的话。
What was this nocturnal expedition, and why should I go armed?
这个夜间探险，为什么我要武装自己？
Where were we going, and what were we to do?
我们要去哪里，我们要做什么？
I had the hint from Holmes that this smooth-faced pawnbroker’s assistant was a formidable man—a man who might play a deep game.
我从福尔摩斯那里得到一个暗示，这个圆脸的鞋匠助手是个厉害人物——一个可能玩深棋的大人物。
I tried to puzzle it out, but gave it up in despair and set the matter aside until night should bring an explanation.
我试图琢磨，但绝望了，把这件事搁置起来，直到夜晚能给出解释。
It was a quarter-past nine when I started from home and made my way across the Park, and so through Oxford Street to Baker Street.
当我从家出发，穿过公园，再穿过牛津街到贝克街时，九点半了。
Two hansoms were standing at the door, and as I entered the passage I heard the sound of voices from above.
门边站着两辆马车，我走进过道时，听到楼上有人说话的声音。

On entering his room, I found Holmes in animated conversation with two men, one of whom I recognised as Peter Jones, the official police agent, while the other was a long, thin, sad-faced man, with a very shiny hat and oppressively respectable frock-coat.
进入他的房间，我发现福尔摩斯和两位男子在交谈，其中一位我认出是彼得·琼斯，官方警察局的官员，另一位是长而瘦，脸色阴郁的男子，戴着非常亮的帽子，穿着一副非常整洁的长袍。
“Ha!
Our party is complete,” said Holmes, buttoning up his pea-jacket and taking his heavy hunting crop from the rack.
我们的队伍已经齐全了，”福尔摩斯说，扣好他的大衣领子，从架子上取下他的沉重猎捕用的枪套。
“Watson, I think you know Mr. Jones, of Scotland Yard?
“沃森先生，你知道彼得·琼斯吗？他是伦敦警察局的。
Let me introduce you to Mr. Merryweather, who is to be our companion in to-night’s adventure.”
让我介绍你认识我们的同伴，今晚的冒险。
“We’re hunting in couples again, Doctor, you see,” said Jones in his consequential way.
“我们又是一对一对地行动，医生，你看，”杰森用他那惯常的腔调说。
“Our friend here is a wonderful man for starting a chase.
“我们的朋友在这里是个起跑点。
All he wants is an old dog to help him to do the running down.”
他只想要一只老狗来帮助他追捕。”
“I hope a wild goose may not prove to be the end of our chase,” observed Mr. Merryweather gloomily.
“我希望一只野鸭不会成为我们追捕的终点，”莫里韦特先生忧郁地说。
“You may place considerable confidence in Mr. Holmes, sir,” said the police agent loftily.
“你对福尔摩斯先生很有信心，先生，”警察局的官员高傲地说。
“He has his own little methods, which are, if he won’t mind my saying so, just a little too theoretical and fantastic, but he has the makings of a detective in him.
“他有自己的方法，如果他不介意我这么说，就是有点理论化和荒诞，但他有侦探的天性。
It is not too much to say that once or twice, as in that business of the Sholto murder and the Agra treasure, he has been more nearly correct than the official force.”
他说，这不夸张，他曾经不止一次，比如在索尔托谋杀案和阿加拉宝藏案中，比官方力量更接近正确。
“Oh, if you say so, Mr. Jones, it is all right,” said the stranger with deference.
“哦，如果你说对了，琼斯先生，那一切就都对了。”陌生人恭敬地说道。
“Still, I confess that I miss my rubber.
“不过，我承认我缺少我的橡胶。
It is the first Saturday night for seven-and-twenty years that I have not had my rubber.”
这是七十七年来我第一次没有橡胶的周六晚上。
“I think you will find,” said Sherlock Holmes, “that you will play for a higher stake to-night than you have ever done yet, and that the play will be more exciting.
“我认为，”说斯克鲁奇霍尔姆先生，“你今晚会比你以前做过的任何一次玩得更高赌注，而且玩得更刺激。
For you, Mr. Merryweather, the stake will be some £ 30,000; and for you, Jones, it will be the man upon whom you wish to lay your hands.”
对于您，马米特韦特先生，赌注是30000英镑；对于您，琼斯先生，是您想抓的人。
“John Clay, the murderer, thief, smasher, and forger.
“约翰克莱，谋杀犯、窃贼、破坏者和伪造者。
He’s a young man, Mr. Merryweather, but he is at the head of his profession, and I would rather have my bracelets on him than on any criminal in London.
他是个年轻人，马米特韦特先生，但他在这个行当里是头号人物，我宁愿戴我的手镯在约翰克莱身上，也不愿在伦敦任何一个罪犯身上。
He’s a remarkable man, is young John Clay.
他是个了不起的人，约翰克莱是个年轻人。
His grandfather was a royal duke, and he himself has been to Eton and Oxford.
他的祖父是皇家公爵，他自己是去伊顿和牛津的。
His brain is as cunning as his fingers, and though we meet signs of him at every turn, we never know where to find the man himself.
他的大脑和手指一样机灵，尽管我们处处都能看到他的痕迹，但我们永远不知道在哪里能找到这个人。
He’ll crack a crib in Scotland one week, and be raising money to build an orphanage in Cornwall the next.
他会在苏格兰破译一个密码，然后在康沃尔筹集资金建立孤儿院。
I’ve been on his track for years and have never set eyes on him yet.”
我跟踪约翰克莱已经多年，但至今还没有见过他。
“I hope that I may have the pleasure of introducing you to-night.
“我希望今晚能有幸介绍您。
I’ve had one or two little turns also with Mr. John Clay, and I agree with you that he is at the head of his profession.
我也有过一次或两次和约翰克莱先生的小圈子，我同意你，他在这个行当里是头号人物。
It is past ten, however, and quite time that we started.
已经十点了，我们该出发了。
If you two will take the first hansom, Watson and I will follow in the second.”
你俩先坐第一辆出租车，我和你二位再坐第二辆。
Sherlock Holmes was not very communicative during the long drive and lay back in the cab humming the tunes which he had heard in the afternoon.
福尔摩斯在漫长的车程中并不怎么说话，只躺在车厢里哼着下午听到的曲子。
We rattled through an endless labyrinth of gas-lit streets until we emerged into Farrington Street.
我们在昏暗的街道上颠簸着，穿过无尽的迷宫，直到我们来到弗拉根顿街。
“We are close there now,” my friend remarked.
“我们现在离那里很近了，”我的朋友说。
“This fellow Merryweather is a bank director, and personally interested in the matter.
这位梅里韦瑟先生是银行家，而且对这件事个人有所利害。
I thought it as well to have Jones with us also.
我觉得最好也带上 Jones。
He is not a bad fellow, though an absolute imbecile in his profession.
他虽然不聪明，但是个不错的家伙。
He has one positive virtue.
他有一个优点。
He is as brave as a bulldog and as tenacious as a lobster if he gets his claws upon anyone.
他勇敢如斗牛犬，如果抓到谁，他就会死死咬住不放。
Here we are, and they are waiting for us.”
我们到了，他们也在等着我们。
We had reached the same crowded thoroughfare in which we had found ourselves in the morning.
我们来到的那条拥挤的街道，和我们早上遇到的那条一模一样。
Our cabs were dismissed, and, following the guidance of Mr. Merryweather, we passed down a narrow passage and through a side door, which he opened for us.
我们的马车被送走了，按照梅瑞瑟先生的指引，我们通过一条狭窄的通道，然后从侧门进去，他为我们打开了门。
Within there was a small corridor, which ended in a very massive iron gate.
在这里有一条小走廊，走廊尽头有一扇非常巨大的铁门。
This also was opened, and led down a flight of winding stone steps, which terminated at another formidable gate.
这扇门也被打开，沿着石阶下了一段蜿蜒的楼梯，楼梯尽头是另一扇巨大的铁门。

Mr. Merryweather stopped to light a lantern, and then conducted us down a dark, earth-smelling passage, and so, after opening a third door, into a huge vault or cellar, which was piled all round with crates and massive boxes.
梅瑞威瑟先生停下来点燃一支灯笼，然后领我们走进一条黑暗潮湿的通道，接着打开第三道门，走进一个巨大的储藏室或地窖，里面堆满了木箱和厚重的箱子。
“You are not very vulnerable from above,” Holmes remarked as he held up the lantern and gazed about him.
“从上面你并不很脆弱。”霍尔姆斯先生说道，他举起了灯笼，环顾四周。
“Nor from below,” said Mr. Merryweather, striking his stick upon the flags which lined the floor.
“从下面也不脆弱。”马尔里奇先生敲了敲地板上排列的木板。
“Why, dear me, it sounds quite hollow!” he remarked, looking up in surprise.
“哦，亲爱的，听起来很空洞！”他惊讶地说道。
“I must really ask you to be a little more quiet!” said Holmes severely.
“我必须很严厉地要求你，不要那么大声！”霍尔姆斯先生说道。
“You have already imperilled the whole success of our expedition.
“你已经严重地危及了我们的探险成功。”
Might I beg that you would have the goodness to sit down upon one of those boxes, and not to interfere?”
“我恳求你，坐到这些箱子上，不要干涉。”

The solemn Mr. Merryweather perched himself upon a crate, with a very injured expression upon his face, while Holmes fell upon his knees upon the floor and, with the lantern and a magnifying lens, began to examine minutely the cracks between the stones.
神圣的马尔里奇先生坐在一个箱子上，脸上带着非常受伤的表情，霍尔姆斯先生跪在地板上，用灯笼和放大镜仔细检查石缝。
A few seconds sufficed to satisfy him, for he sprang to his feet again and put his glass in his pocket.
仅仅几秒钟就让他满意了，他再次站起来，把玻璃放进口袋。
“We have at least an hour before us,” he remarked, “for they can hardly take any steps until the good pawnbroker is safely in bed.
我们至少还有一个小时的时间，”他说道，“因为他们至少要等那个好杂货商安全地睡到床上去。
Then they will not lose a minute, for the sooner they do their work the longer time they will have for their escape.
然后他们不会浪费时间，因为越早他们开始工作，他们越有时间逃脱。
We are at present, Doctor—as no doubt you have divined—in the cellar of the City branch of one of the principal London banks.
我们现在，医生——正如你一定猜到的，在伦敦市中心一家主要银行的地下室。

Mr. Merryweather is the chairman of directors, and he will explain to you that there are reasons why the more daring criminals of London should take a considerable interest in this cellar at present.”
马尔里奇先生是董事会主席，他将向你解释，为什么伦敦胆大的罪犯现在对这个地下室感兴趣。
“It is our French gold,” whispered the director.
“这是我们的法国黄金。”秘书低声说道。
“We have had several warnings that an attempt might be made upon it.”
“我们已经收到几次警告，说可能会有人试图袭击它。”
“Your French gold?”
"你的法国黄金？"
“Yes.
"是的。
We had occasion some months ago to strengthen our resources and borrowed for that purpose 30,000 napoleons from the Bank of France.
有些时候，我们曾借了30,000法郎给法国银行。
It has become known that we have never had occasion to unpack the money, and that it is still lying in our cellar.
这些钱一直没打开过，还一直放在地下室里。
The crate upon which I sit contains 2,000 napoleons packed between layers of lead foil.
我坐的箱子里有2,000法郎，用一层层铅箔包起来的。
Our reserve of bullion is much larger at present than is usually kept in a single branch office, and the directors have had misgivings upon the subject.”
目前我们的黄金储备比通常在单个分行存放的要多，董事会对此有所顾虑。
“Which were very well justified,” observed Holmes.
"这是很合理的，" 森林先生观察到。
“And now it is time that we arranged our little plans.
"现在是时候安排我们的计划了。
I expect that within an hour matters will come to a head.
我预计在半小时内事情会发展到高潮。
In the meantime Mr. Merryweather, we must put the screen over that dark lantern.”
在这段时间里，我们必须把那盏暗灯罩起来。
“And sit in the dark?”
"而且坐在黑暗里？"
“I am afraid so.
"恐怕是这样。
I had brought a pack of cards in my pocket, and I thought that, as we were a partie carrée, you might have your rubber after all.
我带了一包牌，想既然我们是局里人，你也可以抽一副牌。
But I see that the enemy’s preparations have gone so far that we cannot risk the presence of a light.
但看来敌人已经准备得这么远，我们不能冒着有光的风险。
And, first of all, we must choose our positions.
首先，我们必须选择我们的位置。
These are daring men, and though we shall take them at a disadvantage, they may do us some harm unless we are careful.
这些人是胆大的，尽管我们可能对他们不利，但若我们不谨慎小心，他们可能会对我们造成伤害。
I shall stand behind this crate, and do you conceal yourselves behind those.
我将站在这个箱子后面，你则藏在那些后面。
Then, when I flash a light upon them, close in swiftly.
然后，当我在他们身上闪灯时，迅速靠近。
If they fire, Watson, have no compunction about shooting them down.”
如果他们开枪，沃森先生，你不必犹豫，把他们打死。
I placed my revolver, cocked, upon the top of the wooden case behind which I crouched.
我将我的手枪，上膛，放在木箱后面我蹲伏的地方。
Holmes shot the slide across the front of his lantern and left us in pitch darkness—such an absolute darkness as I have never before experienced.
森德森先生，我将滑动门关上，然后我们陷入一片漆黑——这是我以前从未体验过的绝对黑暗。
The smell of hot metal remained to assure us that the light was still there, ready to flash out at a moment’s notice.
金属的气味仍然存在，以证明灯仍然在那里，随时准备在需要时闪亮。
To me, with my nerves worked up to a pitch of expectancy, there was something depressing and subduing in the sudden gloom, and in the cold dank air of the vault.
对我来说，我的神经已经绷紧到无法忍受的程度，突然的黑暗和阴冷的空气地下室里有一种压抑和窒息的感觉。
“They have but one retreat,” whispered Holmes.
“他们只有一个退路，”霍尔姆斯低声说道。
“That is back through the house into Saxe-Coburg Square.
“那就是回到房子的萨塞-科伯格广场。
I hope that you have done what I asked you, Jones?”
我希望你已经做了我要求你的事情，琼斯先生？
“I have an inspector and two officers waiting at the front door.”
“我有一个检查员和两个门卫在前门等着。”
“Then we have stopped all the holes.
“然后我们已经堵住了所有的洞口。”
And now we must be silent and wait.”
现在我们必须保持沉默，等待。
What a time it seemed!
真是太糟糕了！
From comparing notes afterwards it was but an hour and a quarter, yet it appeared to me that the night must have almost gone, and the dawn be breaking above us.
从对比笔记后得知，不过一个小时四十五分钟，但我觉得夜色已经差不多过去了，曙光也快要照到我们头顶了。

My limbs were weary and stiff, for I feared to change my position; yet my nerves were worked up to the highest pitch of tension, and my hearing was so acute that I could not only hear the gentle breathing of my companions, but I could distinguish the deeper, heavier in-breath of the bulky Jones from the thin, sighing note of the bank director.
我的四肢疲惫僵硬，因为害怕改变姿势；但我的神经绷得紧紧的，听觉也到了极限，我能听到同伴的轻柔呼吸，也能分辨出胖子琼斯的深沉、沉重的呼吸声，而银行家的叹息声则很轻。
From my position I could look over the case in the direction of the floor.
从我的位置，我可以望向地板的那边。
Suddenly my eyes caught the glint of a light.
突然，我的眼睛捕捉到一丝光亮。
At first it was but a lurid spark upon the stone pavement.
首先，是一块石板上的一道光斑。

Then it lengthened out until it became a yellow line, and then, without any warning or sound, a gash seemed to open and a hand appeared, a white, almost womanly hand, which felt about in the centre of the little area of light.
然后它延伸出来，变成一条黄色的线，接着，没有任何警告或声音，一个伤口似乎打开了，一个白皙、几乎女性的手出现在小光亮的中心。
For a minute or more the hand, with its writhing fingers, protruded out of the floor.
一只手，带着扭曲的指头，伸出地板。
Then it was withdrawn as suddenly as it appeared, and all was dark again save the single lurid spark which marked a chink between the stones.
然后它突然消失，就像它出现一样，一切都又陷入黑暗，除了那块石板上的一个光斑。
Its disappearance, however, was but momentary.
但它的消失只是短暂的。
With a rending, tearing sound, one of the broad, white stones turned over upon its side and left a square, gaping hole, through which streamed the light of a lantern.
一声撕裂、撕扯的声音，一块宽大的白石板翻转在它的侧边，留下一个正方形、大口的洞，从洞中流出了灯笼的光。

Over the edge there peeped a clean-cut, boyish face, which looked keenly about it, and then, with a hand on either side of the aperture, drew itself shoulder-high and waist-high, until one knee rested upon the edge.
从边缘处，一个干净的、男孩般的脸孔露了出来，它仔细打量着四周，然后，用一只手按在洞口的两侧，身体高高抬起，直到一只膝盖搭在边缘。
In another instant he stood at the side of the hole and was hauling after him a companion, lithe and small like himself, with a pale face and a shock of very red hair.
另外一个瞬间，他站在洞口的旁边，拉着同伴，一个苗条、像他一样的人，面色苍白，一头红发。
“It’s all clear,” he whispered.
“一切清了。”他轻声说。
“Have you the chisel and the bags?
“你有凿子和袋子吗？
Great Scott!
大声的“斯科特！”
Jump, Archie, jump, and I’ll swing for it!”
Archie，跳起来，跳起来，我这就跳下来！”
Sherlock Holmes had sprung out and seized the intruder by the collar.
福尔摩斯纵身跳出，抓住了闯入者衣领。
The other dived down the hole, and I heard the sound of rending cloth as Jones clutched at his skirts.
另一个跳进了洞里，我听到乔伊斯抓着裙子撕裂布料的声音。
The light flashed upon the barrel of a revolver, but Holmes’ hunting crop came down on the man’s wrist, and the pistol clinked upon the stone floor.
灯光照在手枪的枪口上，但华生的猎枪打在那人手腕上，手枪落在石板地上。
“It’s no use, John Clay,” said Holmes blandly.
“没用了，乔纳森·克莱，” Holmes 非常平静地说。
“You have no chance at all.”
你根本就没有一丝一毫的希望。
“So I see,” the other answered with the utmost coolness.
如此看来，”另一个人以 utmost coolness 回答道。
“I fancy that my pal is all right, though I see you have got his coat-tails.”
我 fancy 那 我 的 老弟 还 好 着 呢 ， 虽然 我 看 见 你 把 他的 领带 拿 了 去 。
“There are three men waiting for him at the door,” said Holmes.
Holmes 说道：“门边有三个人在等着他。”
“Oh, indeed!
哦，是吗！
You seem to have done the thing very completely.
你似乎把那件事做得非常彻底。
I must compliment you.”
我要 compliment 你。“
“And I you,” Holmes answered.
“Your red-headed idea was very new and effective.”
你的红发子的主意非常新而且有效。
“You’ll see your pal again presently,” said Jones.
琼斯说：“你一会儿就会见到你的朋友了。”
“He’s quicker at climbing down holes than I am.
他比我还快，能爬出洞来。
Just hold out while I fix the derbies.”
请等我一下，我来处理你的皮靴。
“I beg that you will not touch me with your filthy hands,” remarked our prisoner as the handcuffs clattered upon his wrists.
我恳求你不要用手脏脏的来触碰我，”我们的囚犯说道，当手铐叮叮当当地落在他的手腕上时。
“You may not be aware that I have royal blood in my veins.
你可能不知道我体内流淌着皇室的血液。
Have the goodness, also, when you address me always to say ‘sir’ and ‘please.’”
你说话时，也请务必称呼我为先生，称呼我为请。
“All right,” said Jones with a stare and a snigger.
约翰，你笑眯眯地说道，你瞪了我一眼。
“Well, would you please, sir, march upstairs, where we can get a cab to carry your Highness to the police-station?”
“好吧，先生，你请上楼，我们有车可以载你去警察局。”
“That is better,” said John Clay serenely.
“很好，”约翰，他平静地说道。
He made a sweeping bow to the three of us and walked quietly off in the custody of the detective.
他向我们做了个大礼，然后在侦探的监护下悄悄地离开了。
“Really, Mr. Holmes,” said Mr. Merryweather as we followed them from the cellar, “I do not know how the bank can thank you or repay you.
“真的，先生，”米勒先生说道，当我们跟随他们从地下室出来时，“我也不知道银行怎么感谢你，怎么报答你。
There is no doubt that you have detected and defeated in the most complete manner one of the most determined attempts at bank robbery that have ever come within my experience.”
你没有怀疑，你已经用最彻底的方式，成功地破获了最坚决的银行抢劫案，你在我经验中从未遇到过。
“I have had one or two little scores of my own to settle with Mr. John Clay,” said Holmes.
“我有一些和约翰·克莱先生的私事要处理，”说霍尔姆斯先生。

“I have been at some small expense over this matter, which I shall expect the bank to refund, but beyond that I am amply repaid by having had an experience which is in many ways unique, and by hearing the very remarkable narrative of the Red-headed League.”
我在这事上花了一些小钱，我期望银行会退款，但除此之外，我得到了一个非常独特的经验，还有听到非常惊人的红头帽的叙述。

“You see, Watson,” he explained in the early hours of the morning as we sat over a glass of whisky and soda in Baker Street, “it was perfectly obvious from the first that the only possible object of this rather fantastic business of the advertisement of the League, and the copying of the Encyclopædia, must be to get this not over-bright pawnbroker out of the way for a number of hours every day.
你看，华生，”他早上早些时候，在贝克街我们坐在威士忌和苏打水旁边解释道，“从一开始，这则广告联盟以及复制百科全书的这一相当离奇的生意的唯一可能目的就很明显，就是要把这有点过早的金匠每天几个小时都清除出去。
It was a curious way of managing it, but, really, it would be difficult to suggest a better.
这是一种巧妙的方式，但，真的，这很难建议更好的方式。
The method was no doubt suggested to Clay’s ingenious mind by the colour of his accomplice’s hair.
这种方法当然出自克莱机智的头脑，是他的同伙头发颜色启发的。
The £ 4 a week was a lure which must draw him, and what was it to them, who were playing for thousands?
4镑/周是个诱饵，一定吸引他，对谁来说，他们玩的是千金的把戏？
They put in the advertisement, one rogue has the temporary office, the other rogue incites the man to apply for it, and together they manage to secure his absence every morning in the week.
他们刊登了广告，一个贼有临时办公室，另一个贼煽动人申请，他们一起成功地在一周的每一天早上把人赶出办公室。
From the time that I heard of the assistant having come for half wages, it was obvious to me that he had some strong motive for securing the situation.”
自从我听说助手拿到了半薪，我就知道他有强烈的动机要获得这个职位。
“But how could you guess what the motive was?”
“但是你怎么知道动机是什么？”
“Had there been women in the house, I should have suspected a mere vulgar intrigue.
“如果有女人在屋里，我就会怀疑只是个简单的勾当。
That, however, was out of the question.
但是这不可能。
The man’s business was a small one, and there was nothing in his house which could account for such elaborate preparations, and such an expenditure as they were at.
这人的生意很小，他的房子没有什么可以解释这种精心的准备和这种耗费。
It must, then, be something out of the house.
那么，一定是房子外面的东西。
What could it be?
什么？
I thought of the assistant’s fondness for photography, and his trick of vanishing into the cellar.
我想到了助手对摄影的爱好，以及他进入地下室的诡计。
The cellar!
地下室！
There was the end of this tangled clue.
这是这个纠缠不清线索的终点。
Then I made inquiries as to this mysterious assistant and found that I had to deal with one of the coolest and most daring criminals in London.
然后我询问了这个神秘助手，发现我必须与伦敦最冷静、最大胆的罪犯打交道。
He was doing something in the cellar—something which took many hours a day for months on end.
他在地下室做了些什么——一项每天需要好几个小时，几个月时间才能完成的工作。
What could it be, once more?
这又是什么？
I could think of nothing save that he was running a tunnel to some other building.
我只想到他正在挖一条隧道，去别的建筑。
“So far I had got when we went to visit the scene of action.
我们去现场的时候，我已知道。
I surprised you by beating upon the pavement with my stick.
我用棍子敲打路面。
I was ascertaining whether the cellar stretched out in front or behind.
我正在检查地下室是否在前面还是后面。
It was not in front.
不在前面。
Then I rang the bell, and, as I hoped, the assistant answered it.
然后我按了门铃，希望助手会接电话。
We have had some skirmishes, but we had never set eyes upon each other before.
我们曾有过一些小冲突，但从未见过对方。
I hardly looked at his face.
我几乎没看他的脸。
His knees were what I wished to see.
他的膝盖让我看到了。
You must yourself have remarked how worn, wrinkled, and stained they were.
你一定注意到它们很脏、很皱、很脏。
They spoke of those hours of burrowing.
他们谈论着那些挖掘的时光。
The only remaining point was what they were burrowing for.
剩下的问题是他们挖掘的是什么。
I walked round the corner, saw the City and Suburban Bank abutted on our friend’s premises, and felt that I had solved my problem.
我绕过拐角，看到城和郊区银行与我们朋友的建筑相邻，感觉我已经解决了问题。
When you drove home after the concert I called upon Scotland Yard and upon the chairman of the bank directors, with the result that you have seen.”
在你音乐会结束后回家时，我去了苏格兰场和银行董事的主席，结果你已经见到了。
“And how could you tell that they would make their attempt to-night?”
“你怎么知道他们会今晚来呢？”
I asked.
我问。
“Well, when they closed their League offices that was a sign that they cared no longer about Mr. Jabez Wilson’s presence—in other words, that they had completed their tunnel.
“他们关闭了联盟办公室，那是一个信号，他们不再关心杰abez·威尔逊的出席——换句话说，他们已经完成了他们的地道。
But it was essential that they should use it soon, as it might be discovered, or the bullion might be removed.
但是必须尽快使用，因为可能会被发现，或者黄金会被移走。
Saturday would suit them better than any other day, as it would give them two days for their escape.
周六会更适合他们，因为可以给他们两天的时间逃脱。
For all these reasons I expected them to come to-night.”
因为这些原因，我预计他们今晚会来。
“You reasoned it out beautifully,” I exclaimed in unfeigned admiration.
“你很聪明地推理出来了。”我赞叹道。
“It is so long a chain, and yet every link rings true.”
“它是一个长链，但是每一个环都真实可信。”
“It saved me from ennui,” he answered, yawning.
“它让我免于无聊。”他答道，打了个哈欠。
“Alas!
I already feel it closing in upon me.
我已经感到它在逼近我。
My life is spent in one long effort to escape from the commonplaces of existence.
我的生活是为逃脱平凡的生活而努力。
These little problems help me to do so.”
这些小问题帮助我逃脱。
“And you are a benefactor of the race,” said I.
“你是一个种族的恩人。”我说。
He shrugged his shoulders.
他耸耸肩。
“Well, perhaps, after all, it is of some little use,” he remarked. “‘L’homme c’est rien—l’œuvre c’est tout,’ as Gustave Flaubert wrote to George Sand.”
“嗯，也许，毕竟还是有一点用处吧，”他 remarks。“‘人是无足轻重的，唯有作品才重要，’”如 Gustave Flaubert 曾写给乔治·桑说。
“My dear fellow,” said Sherlock Holmes as we sat on either side of the fire in his lodgings at Baker Street, “life is infinitely stranger than anything which the mind of man could invent.
“亲爱的，”说来，我们坐在壁炉旁的霍尔登街的霍尔登先生的住所里， “生活比人类所能发明的任何东西都要更古怪。
We would not dare to conceive the things which are really mere commonplaces of existence.
我们不会去设想那些只是日常事物。

If we could fly out of that window hand in hand, hover over this great city, gently remove the roofs, and peep in at the queer things which are going on, the strange coincidences, the plannings, the cross-purposes, the wonderful chains of events, working through generations, and leading to the most outré results, it would make all fiction with its conventionalities and foreseen conclusions most stale and unprofitable.”
如果我们能从那个窗户手拉手飞出去，轻飘飘地在大城里飘荡，轻轻掀开屋顶，看看那些奇怪的事情正在发生，那些奇怪的巧合，那些计划，那些交叉的意图，那些奇妙的事件，通过几代人，导致最离奇的结果，那就会使所有的虚构都变得乏味而无价值。

There is as much sense in Hafiz as in Horace, and as much knowledge of the world.”
有如哈菲兹和霍雷肖，也有对世界的了解。

ch.zt: 第四篇 · 博斯科姆比溪谷秘案
p: We were seated at breakfast one morning, my wife and I, when the maid brought in a telegram.
我们在早餐时正坐着，我的妻子和我，这时女仆送来了一封电报。
It was from Sherlock Holmes and ran in this way:
这是来自夏洛克·福尔摩斯的电报，内容如下：
“Have you a couple of days to spare?
“你有几天空闲吗？
Have just been wired for from the west of England in connection with Boscombe Valley tragedy.
从英格兰西部来了一封电报，与博斯科姆比山谷的悲剧有关。
Shall be glad if you will come with me.
如果你愿意的话，我会很高兴的。
Air and scenery perfect.
空气和风景都很好。
Leave Paddington by the 11:15.”
请乘坐11:15离开帕丁顿。
“What do you say, dear?” said my wife, looking across at me.
“亲爱的，你有什么意见吗？”我的妻子看着我。
“Will you go?”
“你愿意去吗？”
“I really don’t know what to say.
“我实在不知道说什么好。
I have a fairly long list at present.”
我现在有一份很长的名单。
“Oh, Anstruther would do your work for you.
“哦，安斯特鲁特先生会替你处理的。
You have been looking a little pale lately.
近来你有点儿脸色苍白。
I think that the change would do you good, and you are always so interested in Mr. Sherlock Holmes’ cases.”
我认为这种变化对你有好处，而且你总是对福尔摩斯先生的案件很感兴趣。
“I should be ungrateful if I were not, seeing what I gained through one of them,” I answered.
“如果我没有从中得到好处，我就不感谢你了。”我回答。
“But if I am to go, I must pack at once, for I have only half an hour.”
“但是我必须马上打包，因为我只有半小时的时间。”
My experience of camp life in Afghanistan had at least had the effect of making me a prompt and ready traveller.
我在阿富汗的营地生活经验至少让我变得一个迅速和准备好的旅行者。
My wants were few and simple, so that in less than the time stated I was in a cab with my valise, rattling away to Paddington Station.
我的需要很少也很简单，所以我不到说的时间我就坐上了出租车，带着我的行李，嘎嘎地颠簸着前往帕丁顿车站。
Sherlock Holmes was pacing up and down the platform, his tall, gaunt figure made even gaunter and taller by his long grey travelling-cloak and close-fitting cloth cap.
森林·霍尔姆斯在站台上来回踱步，他的高大瘦削的身材因为他的长灰色旅行外套和紧身帽而更加高大。
“It is really very good of you to come, Watson,” said he.
“谢谢你来，沃森先生，”他说。
“It makes a considerable difference to me, having someone with me on whom I can thoroughly rely.
“这对我来说很重要，因为我可以依靠的人。
Local aid is always either worthless or else biassed.
当地援助总是要么毫无价值要么偏见。
If you will keep the two corner seats I shall get the tickets.”
如果你愿意，我将给你两个角落的座位，我会买票。
We had the carriage to ourselves save for an immense litter of papers which Holmes had brought with him.
我们只有自己一个，除了一个巨大的堆叠的文件，霍尔姆斯带来的，我们没有别人。
Among these he rummaged and read, with intervals of note-taking and of meditation, until we were past Reading.
他翻阅着这些文件，间歇着记笔记和沉思，直到我们过了读取。
Then he suddenly rolled them all into a gigantic ball and tossed them up onto the rack.
然后他突然把它们都揉成一个巨大的球，扔到架子上。
“Have you heard anything of the case?” he asked.
“你听说这个案子了吗？”他问道。
“Not a word.
“没有一个字。
I have not seen a paper for some days.”
我几天没有看到过一张纸。
“The London press has not had very full accounts.
“伦敦的报纸没有提供很详细的报道。”
I have just been looking through all the recent papers in order to master the particulars.
我刚刚翻阅了所有最近的文件，以便掌握详情。
It seems, from what I gather, to be one of those simple cases which are so extremely difficult.”
从我所了解的情况来看，这似乎是一个非常简单但极其困难的案件。
“That sounds a little paradoxical.”
“这听起来有点矛盾。”
“But it is profoundly true.
“但这是非常正确的。”
Singularity is almost invariably a clue.
特立独行的东西几乎总是线索。
The more featureless and commonplace a crime is, the more difficult it is to bring it home.
当犯罪行为越简单、越平凡时，就越难将其归咎于某人。
In this case, however, they have established a very serious case against the son of the murdered man.”
在这个案件中，他们已经对谋杀者的儿子建立了非常严重的指控。
“It is a murder, then?”
“这是一起谋杀案吗？”
“Well, it is conjectured to be so.
“嗯，它被推测为如此。
I shall take nothing for granted until I have the opportunity of looking personally into it.
我将在有机会亲自调查的情况下，对它的情况进行解释。
I will explain the state of things to you, as far as I have been able to understand it, in a very few words.
我将向你解释我所理解的情况，用非常简短的话。
“Boscombe Valley is a country district not very far from Ross, in Herefordshire.
“布什莫谷是一个距离罗斯不远的乡村地区。
The largest landed proprietor in that part is a Mr. John Turner, who made his money in Australia and returned some years ago to the old country.
在那里，最大的土地所有者是约翰·特纳先生，他在澳大利亚赚了钱，然后回到旧国家。
One of the farms which he held, that of Hatherley, was let to Mr. Charles McCarthy, who was also an ex-Australian.
他所持有的最大的农场，即霍特莱农场，被让给了查尔斯·麦克查姆先生，他也曾是澳大利亚人。
The men had known each other in the colonies, so that it was not unnatural that when they came to settle down they should do so as near each other as possible.
他们知道彼此，所以在他们定居时，尽可能接近。
Turner was apparently the richer man, so McCarthy became his tenant but still remained, it seems, upon terms of perfect equality, as they were frequently together.
蒂蒙斯似乎是富翁，所以麦卡希成了他的佃户，但似乎仍然保持着平等的条件，因为他们经常在一起。
McCarthy had one son, a lad of eighteen, and Turner had an only daughter of the same age, but neither of them had wives living.
麦卡希有一个儿子，十八岁，蒂蒙斯有一个女儿，十八岁，但她们都没有活着结婚。

They appear to have avoided the society of the neighbouring English families and to have led retired lives, though both the McCarthys were fond of sport and were frequently seen at the race-meetings of the neighbourhood.
他们似乎避免了邻近的英国家庭的社交，过着隐居的生活，尽管麦卡希和蒂蒙斯都喜欢运动，并经常在附近举行赛马的聚会中出现。
McCarthy kept two servants—a man and a girl.
麦卡希有两个仆人——一个男人和一个女孩。
Turner had a considerable household, some half-dozen at the least.
蒂蒙斯有一个相当大的家庭，至少有半打人。
That is as much as I have been able to gather about the families.
这就是我所能收集到的关于这两个家庭的事实。
Now for the facts.
现在是事实。

“On June 3rd, that is, on Monday last, McCarthy left his house at Hatherley about three in the afternoon and walked down to the Boscombe Pool, which is a small lake formed by the spreading out of the stream which runs down the Boscombe Valley.
“在六月三日，也就是上星期一，麦卡希从他家的霍特勒里走了大约下午三点，然后步行到博斯科姆湖，这是一个由博斯科姆山谷的水流扩散形成的湖泊。
He had been out with his serving-man in the morning at Ross, and he had told the man that he must hurry, as he had an appointment of importance to keep at three.
他和他的仆人早上在罗斯走了一趟，告诉他必须加快，因为他在三点有一项重要的约会。
From that appointment he never came back alive.
从那之后，他再没有回来。
“From Hatherley Farmhouse to the Boscombe Pool is a quarter of a mile, and two people saw him as he passed over this ground.
“从霍特勒农场到博斯科姆湖有四分之一英里，有两个人看到他经过这个地方。
One was an old woman, whose name is not mentioned, and the other was William Crowder, a game-keeper in the employ of Mr. Turner.
一个是未提及的老人，另一个是威廉·库德，是蒂蒙斯先生的猎场工人。
Both these witnesses depose that Mr. McCarthy was walking alone.
两个证人证言说，先生麦卡希正在行走。
The game-keeper adds that within a few minutes of his seeing Mr. McCarthy pass he had seen his son, Mr. James McCarthy, going the same way with a gun under his arm.
猎场工人补充说，他看到麦卡希父亲，即迈克尔·詹姆斯·麦卡希，带着枪在同一条路上走。
To the best of his belief, the father was actually in sight at the time, and the son was following him.
根据他的信念，父亲当时确实可见，儿子则跟随他。
He thought no more of the matter until he heard in the evening of the tragedy that had occurred.
他直到晚上才想起这件事。
“The two McCarthys were seen after the time when William Crowder, the game-keeper, lost sight of them.
“在威廉·克劳德猎手看不见他们的时候，麦卡特夫妇俩被看见了。”
The Boscombe Pool is thickly wooded round, with just a fringe of grass and of reeds round the edge.
贝斯考姆湖四周被茂密的树林环绕，湖边只有一圈草和芦苇。
A girl of fourteen, Patience Moran, who is the daughter of the lodge-keeper of the Boscombe Valley estate, was in one of the woods picking flowers.
一个十四岁的女孩，帕蒂尼尔·莫兰，是贝斯考姆山谷庄园的看林员的女儿，在湖边的树林里摘花。
She states that while she was there she saw, at the border of the wood and close by the lake, Mr. McCarthy and his son, and that they appeared to be having a violent quarrel.
她说，当她在那儿的时候，她看到，在树林的边界和靠近湖边的地方，麦卡特先生和他的儿子，似乎在激烈地争吵。
She heard Mr. McCarthy the elder using very strong language to his son, and she saw the latter raise up his hand as if to strike his father.
她听到麦卡特先生用非常粗鲁的语言责骂他的儿子，她看到他的儿子举起手来，好像要打他的父亲。

She was so frightened by their violence that she ran away and told her mother when she reached home that she had left the two McCarthys quarrelling near Boscombe Pool, and that she was afraid that they were going to fight.
她被他们的暴力吓坏了，跑走了，告诉她的妈妈，她刚到家就说她离开麦卡特夫妇在贝斯考姆湖边争吵，她害怕他们要打架。
She had hardly said the words when young Mr. McCarthy came running up to the lodge to say that he had found his father dead in the wood, and to ask for the help of the lodge-keeper.
她刚说完这些话，年轻的麦卡特先生就跑来告诉看林员，说他在树林里发现他父亲死在树林里，要他帮忙。
He was much excited, without either his gun or his hat, and his right hand and sleeve were observed to be stained with fresh blood.
他非常激动，没有他的枪和帽子，他的右手和袖子被新鲜的血迹染红了。
On following him they found the dead body stretched out upon the grass beside the pool.
他们跟着他，发现死尸躺在湖边的草地上。
The head had been beaten in by repeated blows of some heavy and blunt weapon.
头部被用重物钝器多次击打。
The injuries were such as might very well have been inflicted by the butt-end of his son’s gun, which was found lying on the grass within a few paces of the body.
伤势如此严重，可能是因为他儿子的枪的枪管的末端被击中。

Under these circumstances the young man was instantly arrested, and a verdict of ‘wilful murder’ having been returned at the inquest on Tuesday, he was on Wednesday brought before the magistrates at Ross, who have referred the case to the next Assizes.
在这些情况下，年轻人立刻被逮捕，陪审团在星期二裁定“谋杀”，他于星期三被带到罗斯的法官面前，法官将此案转交给下一次巡回法庭。
Those are the main facts of the case as they came out before the coroner and the police-court.”
这就是案件的主要事实，它们在验尸官和警察法庭上被宣布出来。
“I could hardly imagine a more damning case,” I remarked.
“我简直无法想象一个更令人震惊的案子了。”我评论道。
“If ever circumstantial evidence pointed to a criminal it does so here.”
如果任何可疑的证据指向罪犯，它在这里就指向了罪犯。
“Circumstantial evidence is a very tricky thing,” answered Holmes thoughtfully.
可疑的证据是一个非常棘手的东西，”霍尔姆斯认真地说。
“It may seem to point very straight to one thing, but if you shift your own point of view a little, you may find it pointing in an equally uncompromising manner to something entirely different.
它可能看起来指向非常明确的东西，但如果你稍微改变一下自己的观点，你会发现它指向的东西同样坚定地指向完全不同的东西。
It must be confessed, however, that the case looks exceedingly grave against the young man, and it is very possible that he is indeed the culprit.
无论如何，这个案子看起来对年轻人非常严重，而且很有可能他是罪犯。

There are several people in the neighbourhood, however, and among them Miss Turner, the daughter of the neighbouring landowner, who believe in his innocence, and who have retained Lestrade, whom you may recollect in connection with the Study in Scarlet, to work out the case in his interest.
附近有几个地方，其中有一个邻居的小姐，即特纳小姐，相信他的无辜，并且保留了莱斯特德，你可能还记得在《红房子》中与他合作的莱斯特德，来处理这个案子以他的利益。

Lestrade, being rather puzzled, has referred the case to me, and hence it is that two middle-aged gentlemen are flying westward at fifty miles an hour instead of quietly digesting their breakfasts at home.”
莱斯特德因为有些困惑，把案子交给了我，因此，两个中年男子以每小时五十英里的速度向西飞行，而不是安静地在家里吃早餐。
“I am afraid,” said I, “that the facts are so obvious that you will find little credit to be gained out of this case.”
“我恐怕，”我说，“事实是如此明显，你将发现从这个案子中获得很少的信用。”
“There is nothing more deceptive than an obvious fact,” he answered, laughing.
“没有什么比明显的事实更欺骗人了，”他笑着回答。
“Besides, we may chance to hit upon some other obvious facts which may have been by no means obvious to Mr. Lestrade.
“此外，我们可能会偶然发现一些其他明显的事实，这些事实对于莱斯特德来说是完全不明显的。
You know me too well to think that I am boasting when I say that I shall either confirm or destroy his theory by means which he is quite incapable of employing, or even of understanding.
你太了解我了，以为我是在吹牛，当我说我会通过我无法使用或理解的方法来证实或摧毁他的理论，或者甚至理解。

To take the first example to hand, I very clearly perceive that in your bedroom the window is upon the right-hand side, and yet I question whether Mr. Lestrade would have noted even so self-evident a thing as that.”
以第一个例子为例，我非常清楚地看到，在你的卧室窗户在右边，但我怀疑莱斯特德是否注意到这样一个显而易见的东西。
“How on earth—”
“My dear fellow, I know you well.
“亲爱的小伙子，我知道你很熟悉。
I know the military neatness which characterises you.
我知道你的军事整洁，你的早晨剃须，这个季节你早晨剃须依靠阳光；但因为你的剃须越来越少，直到它变得完全不整洁，当我们在左面的角上，它显然比右边更不被照亮。

You shave every morning, and in this season you shave by the sunlight; but since your shaving is less and less complete as we get farther back on the left side, until it becomes positively slovenly as we get round the angle of the jaw, it is surely very clear that that side is less illuminated than the other.
你每天早晨刮胡子，而在这个季节你是在阳光下刮的；但是随着我们离左边的侧脸越来越远，你的刮胡子就变得越来越不彻底，直到变得完全不成样子，就像我们绕过下巴的角度一样，很明显，那一侧比另一侧更不被照亮。
I could not imagine a man of your habits looking at himself in an equal light and being satisfied with such a result.
我无法想象你这样的习惯的人，能够对自己的相貌有如此公正的评价，而且对自己满意。
I only quote this as a trivial example of observation and inference.
我只是举这个例子来说明观察和推论。
Therein lies my métier, and it is just possible that it may be of some service in the investigation which lies before us.
这就是我的职业，也许在我们面前的调查中，它可能会有所帮助。
There are one or two minor points which were brought out in the inquest, and which are worth considering.”
有些细节在听证会上被提出来，值得考虑。
“What are they?”
“它们是什么？”
“It appears that his arrest did not take place at once, but after the return to Hatherley Farm.
“看起来，他的逮捕并不是立刻进行的，而是回到霍特勒农场之后。
On the inspector of constabulary informing him that he was a prisoner, he remarked that he was not surprised to hear it, and that it was no more than his deserts.
检察官告诉他他是囚犯，他说道：“我并不感到惊讶，因为这不过是他应得的。”
This observation of his had the natural effect of removing any traces of doubt which might have remained in the minds of the coroner’s jury.”
他对他的观察自然地消除了听证会中可能存在的任何怀疑。
“It was a confession,” I ejaculated.
“这是一份供词。”我惊呼道。
“No, for it was followed by a protestation of innocence.”
“不，因为这被一个声明所推翻。”
“Coming on the top of such a damning series of events, it was at least a most suspicious remark.”
“在这样令人震惊的一系列事件之后，这真是一个非常可疑的评论。”
“On the contrary,” said Holmes, “it is the brightest rift which I can at present see in the clouds.
“相反，”说霍尔姆斯，“这是一条最亮的裂隙，我目前能看到的。”
However innocent he might be, he could not be such an absolute imbecile as not to see that the circumstances were very black against him.
即使他再无辜，他也不能是一个绝对的傻瓜，因为他不会看不到这些情况对他非常不利。

Had he appeared surprised at his own arrest, or feigned indignation at it, I should have looked upon it as highly suspicious, because such surprise or anger would not be natural under the circumstances, and yet might appear to be the best policy to a scheming man.
如果他显得惊讶于自己的逮捕，或者假装愤怒于它，我就会认为这非常可疑，因为这种惊讶或愤怒并不自然，而且在这些情况下，它可能表明一个狡猾的人的最佳策略。
His frank acceptance of the situation marks him as either an innocent man, or else as a man of considerable self-restraint and firmness.
他的坦率接受现状，表明他要么是一个无辜的人，要么是一个相当克制和坚定的人。

As to his remark about his deserts, it was also not unnatural if you consider that he stood beside the dead body of his father, and that there is no doubt that he had that very day so far forgotten his filial duty as to bandy words with him, and even, according to the little girl whose evidence is so important, to raise his hand as if to strike him.
关于他所说的“坟地”，也并非不可理解，因为他在父亲的坟前站了很久，而且毫无疑问，那天他已经忘记了孝顺父亲的义务，甚至，根据那个重要女孩的证词，甚至举起手来好像要打他。
The self-reproach and contrition which are displayed in his remark appear to me to be the signs of a healthy mind rather than of a guilty one.”
他所说的自责和悔恨在我看来，更像是健康的大脑的标志，而不是罪恶的标志。
I shook my head.
我摇了摇头。
“Many men have been hanged on far slighter evidence,” I remarked.
“许多人在轻微的证据下被绞死。”我评论道。
“So they have.
“是的。”
And many men have been wrongfully hanged.”
许多人在错误的证据下被绞死。”
“What is the young man’s own account of the matter?”
“年轻人自己对这件事的描述是什么？”我问道。
“It is, I am afraid, not very encouraging to his supporters, though there are one or two points in it which are suggestive.
“恐怕对支持者来说，这并不是非常令人鼓舞的，尽管其中有一些是暗示性的。”
You will find it here, and may read it for yourself.”
你会在这里找到它，并可以自己阅读。

He picked out from his bundle a copy of the local Herefordshire paper, and having turned down the sheet he pointed out the paragraph in which the unfortunate young man had given his own statement of what had occurred.
他从包裹里取出一份当地赫里福德郡的报纸，翻过那页后，指出了那份不幸的年轻人所作的陈述，他在其中详细说明了所发生的事情的那段文字。
I settled myself down in the corner of the carriage and read it very carefully.
我坐在车厢角落里，仔细阅读。
It ran in this way:
这样写道：

“Mr. James McCarthy, the only son of the deceased, was then called and gave evidence as follows: ‘I had been away from home for three days at Bristol, and had only just returned upon the morning of last Monday, the 3rd.
“詹姆斯·麦卡锡先生，唯一儿子，当时被叫来作证，如下所述：‘我在家外停留了三天，在星期一的3日才回来。’
My father was absent from home at the time of my arrival, and I was informed by the maid that he had driven over to Ross with John Cobb, the groom.
我的父亲当时不在家，我从女仆那里得知他去了罗斯，和约翰·科布，马夫一起。

Shortly after my return I heard the wheels of his trap in the yard, and, looking out of my window, I saw him get out and walk rapidly out of the yard, though I was not aware in which direction he was going.
在我回来后不久，我听到他的马车在院子里的轮子声，从窗口看过去，我看到他出来，快速走出院子，尽管我不知道他要去哪个方向。
I then took my gun and strolled out in the direction of the Boscombe Pool, with the intention of visiting the rabbit warren which is upon the other side.
