“他们一定是狡猾的魔鬼。”
“How could they have decoyed him down there?
“他们怎么把人引到那里去？
The Embankment is not on the direct line to the station.
埃姆布顿街不是直通车站的。
The bridge, no doubt, was too crowded, even on such a night, for their purpose.
桥，毫无疑问，也太拥挤，即使在这样的夜晚，也是为了他们的目的。
Well, Watson, we shall see who will win in the long run.
哈士奇，我们会看到谁会最终获胜。
I am going out now!”
我现在要出去了！”
“To the police?”
“去警察局？””
“No; I shall be my own police.
“不，我要自己当警察。”
When I have spun the web they may take the flies, but not before.”
当我编织好网，他们或许能捉到苍蝇，但在此之前，他们不能。”
All day I was engaged in my professional work, and it was late in the evening before I returned to Baker Street.
整天我都在从事我的专业工作，直到晚上才回到贝克街。
Sherlock Holmes had not come back yet.
哈士奇还没有回来。
It was nearly ten o’clock before he entered, looking pale and worn.
大约十点钟他才回来，脸色苍白，疲惫不堪。
He walked up to the sideboard, and tearing a piece from the loaf he devoured it voraciously, washing it down with a long draught of water.
他走到酒柜边，撕下一块面包，狼吞虎咽地吃了起来，喝了一大口水。
“You are hungry,” I remarked.
“你饿了。”我说道。
“Starving.
“饿得要死。
It had escaped my memory.
我记不起这件事了。
I have had nothing since breakfast.”
我从早饭后就没有吃东西了。
“Nothing?”
“没有？”
“Not a bite.
“没有咬一口。
I had no time to think of it.”
我没有时间去想这件事。
“And how have you succeeded?”
“你是怎么成功的？”
“Well.”
“You have a clue?”
“你有一个线索？”
“I have them in the hollow of my hand.
“我手上有线索。
Young Openshaw shall not long remain unavenged.
小开思霍夫不会久受欺凌。
Why, Watson, let us put their own devilish trade-mark upon them.
为什么，沃森，让我们把他们的恶习标记在他们身上。
It is well thought of!”
这做得很好！”
“What do you mean?”
你是什么意思？
He took an orange from the cupboard, and tearing it to pieces he squeezed out the pips upon the table.
他从橱柜中取了一个橙子，撕开后把果核挤在桌上。
Of these he took five and thrust them into an envelope.
其中他取了五颗，塞进一个信封里。
On the inside of the flap he wrote “S. H. for J. O.” Then he sealed it and addressed it to “Captain James Calhoun, Barque Lone Star, Savannah, Georgia.”
里面他写上“S. H. for J. O.”然后封好，写上“詹姆斯·卡伦上尉，萨凡纳，佐治亚州‘圣塔尔马特’号”。
“That will await him when he enters port,” said he, chuckling.
那将等待他到他进入港口时，他笑着说。
“It may give him a sleepless night.
它可能会让他彻夜难眠。
He will find it as sure a precursor of his fate as Openshaw did before him.”
他会发现它对自己命运的预示，就像欧普沙威在他之前对自己的命运一样确定。
“And who is this Captain Calhoun?”
“And这是谁这个卡莱恩上校？”
“The leader of the gang.
这个小队的头目。
I shall have the others, but he first.”
我要将其他人拿下，但先拿下他。
“How did you trace it, then?”
你怎么追踪到它的？
He took a large sheet of paper from his pocket, all covered with dates and names.
他从口袋里取出一张大纸，上面密密麻麻地写着日期和名字。
“I have spent the whole day,” said he, “over Lloyd’s registers and files of the old papers, following the future career of every vessel which touched at Pondicherry in January and February in ’83.
他说：“我整整一天都在查洛伊的登记册和旧报纸上的文件，追踪1883年1月和2月在浦昂其里停靠的每艘船只的未来航程。”
There were thirty-six ships of fair tonnage which were reported there during those months.
共有三十六艘货轮在那几个月里被报告过。
Of these, one, the Lone Star, instantly attracted my attention, since, although it was reported as having cleared from London, the name is that which is given to one of the states of the Union.”
在这其中，有一艘，利星号，立刻吸引了我的注意，虽然它被报告为已经从伦敦出发，但这个名字是美国的一个州所用。”
“Texas, I think.”
Texas, 我想。
“I was not and am not sure which; but I knew that the ship must have an American origin.”
我不太确定是哪一艘，但我知道那艘船必定有美国的起源。
“What then?”
那又怎样？
“I searched the Dundee records, and when I found that the barque Lone Star was there in January, ’85, my suspicion became a certainty.
我查了邓布雷的记录，当我发现巴克利星号在1885年1月那裡时，我的怀疑便成了定论。
I then inquired as to the vessels which lay at present in the port of London.”
然后我 inquiry 了现时停泊在伦敦港的船只。
“Yes?”
是吗？
“The Lone Star had arrived here last week.
“来星州上一周就到了这里。”
I went down to the Albert Dock and found that she had been taken down the river by the early tide this morning, homeward bound to Savannah.
我下到阿尔伯特码头，发现她今天早上的早潮时已被运往河里，朝萨凡纳方向而去。
I wired to Gravesend and learned that she had passed some time ago, and as the wind is easterly I have no doubt that she is now past the Goodwins and not very far from the Isle of Wight.”
我电告格雷森，得知她已经驶过一些时间，由于风向偏东，我毫不怀疑她现在已经驶过好望角，离伊丽莎白岛不远。
“What will you do, then?”
你将怎么办？
“Oh, I have my hand upon him.
哦，我已经抓住他了。
He and the two mates, are as I learn, the only native-born Americans in the ship.
他和他的两个同伴，据我所知，都是船上唯一的美国人。
The others are Finns and Germans.
其他人是芬兰人和德国人。
I know, also, that they were all three away from the ship last night.
我知道，此外，他们昨晚都离开了那艘船。
I had it from the stevedore who has been loading their cargo.
我是从负责装货的装卸工那里听说的。

By the time that their sailing-ship reaches Savannah the mail-boat will have carried this letter, and the cable will have informed the police of Savannah that these three gentlemen are badly wanted here upon a charge of murder.”
当他们的帆船到达佐治亚州的萨凡纳时，这封信已经邮递出去，而萨凡纳的警察也已经通知他们，这三个人因谋杀罪被悬赏通缉。

There is ever a flaw, however, in the best laid of human plans, and the murderers of John Openshaw were never to receive the orange pips which would show them that another, as cunning and as resolute as themselves, was upon their track.
尽管人类计划再完美，也总会有漏洞，约翰·开普什沃斯的凶手们永远也不会收到那些橘子皮，显示他们被追踪的人，比他们自己更加狡猾和坚定。
Very long and very severe were the equinoctial gales that year.
那一年的春分和秋分大风都是极长且极严酷的。
We waited long for news of the Lone Star of Savannah, but none ever reached us.
我们等待了很久，但一直没有收到萨凡纳的“星”号的消息。

We did at last hear that somewhere far out in the Atlantic a shattered stern-post of a boat was seen swinging in the trough of a wave, with the letters “L. S.” carved upon it, and that is all which we shall ever know of the fate of the Lone Star.
最后我们终于听说，一艘船的残破船尾在大西洋的某个地方被波浪拍打着，上面刻着“L. S.”，这就是我们对“星”号的最后知道的结局。

ch.et: VI. The Man with the Twisted Lip
p: Isa Whitney, brother of the late Elias Whitney, D.D., Principal of the Theological College of St. George’s, was much addicted to opium.
艾萨·惠特尼，是已故爱德华·惠特尼（D. D.）主教的儿子，圣乔治神学院的校长，对鸦片成瘾非常严重。

The habit grew upon him, as I understand, from some foolish freak when he was at college; for having read De Quincey’s description of his dreams and sensations, he had drenched his tobacco with laudanum in an attempt to produce the same effects.
这习惯是从他大学时期的一个愚蠢的怪癖开始的，因为他读了德克西的梦境和感觉描述，试图产生同样的效果。

He found, as so many more have done, that the practice is easier to attain than to get rid of, and for many years he continued to be a slave to the drug, an object of mingled horror and pity to his friends and relatives.
他发现，像许多其他人一样，习惯更容易获得而不是摆脱，多年以来他一直是一个鸦片的奴隶，他的朋友和亲人对他感到既恐怖又可怜。
I can see him now, with yellow, pasty face, drooping lids, and pin-point pupils, all huddled in a chair, the wreck and ruin of a noble man.
我现在可以看见他，黄色的、苍白的脸，垂下的眼皮，小点的瞳孔，蜷缩在一把椅子上，一个伟大的人变成废墟。
One night—it was in June, ’89—there came a ring to my bell, about the hour when a man gives his first yawn and glances at the clock.
有一天——是1889年六月，我听到铃声，大约是男人第一次打哈欠的时候，瞥了一眼钟。
I sat up in my chair, and my wife laid her needle-work down in her lap and made a little face of disappointment.
我坐在椅子上，妻子放下她的针线活，脸上露出失望的表情。
“A patient!” said she.
“一个病人！”她说。
“You’ll have to go out.”
“你必须出去。”
I groaned, for I was newly come back from a weary day.
我呻吟，因为我刚刚从一个疲惫的一天回来。
We heard the door open, a few hurried words, and then quick steps upon the linoleum.
我们听到门打开，几句话，然后快速的脚步在地毯上。
Our own door flew open, and a lady, clad in some dark-coloured stuff, with a black veil, entered the room.
我们的门飞快打开，一位女士，穿着某种暗色的衣服，戴着黑纱，进入房间。
“You will excuse my calling so late,” she began, and then, suddenly losing her self-control, she ran forward, threw her arms about my wife’s neck, and sobbed upon her shoulder.
“你为我这么晚打电话，”她开始说，然后突然失去控制，她跑过来，抱住我妻子的脖子，哭在她的肩膀上。
“Oh, I’m in such trouble!” she cried; “I do so want a little help.”
“哦，我多么需要帮助！”她说，“我多么需要帮助。”
“Why,” said my wife, pulling up her veil, “it is Kate Whitney.
“为什么，”我妻子拉起她的纱巾，“这是凯特·惠特尼。”
How you startled me, Kate!
你怎么惊吓了我，凯特！
I had not an idea who you were when you came in.”
当你进来时，我完全不知道你是谁。
“I didn’t know what to do, so I came straight to you.”
“我也不知道该怎么办，所以直接来找你。”
That was always the way.
这就是我一贯的做法。
Folk who were in grief came to my wife like birds to a lighthouse.
悲伤的人总是像鸟儿一样飞向我的妻子。
“It was very sweet of you to come.
“你真是太好了，能来。”
Now, you must have some wine and water, and sit here comfortably and tell us all about it.
现在，你必须喝点酒和水，然后在这里舒服地坐下来，把一切都告诉我们。
Or should you rather that I sent James off to bed?”
或者你更愿意让我派人去叫詹姆斯睡觉？
“Oh, no, no!
I want the doctor’s advice and help, too.
我也需要医生的建议和帮助。
It’s about Isa.
这事是关于伊萨的。
He has not been home for two days.
他已经两天没有回家了。
I am so frightened about him!”
我非常担心他！
It was not the first time that she had spoken to us of her husband’s trouble, to me as a doctor, to my wife as an old friend and school companion.
这并不是第一次她对我们说起她丈夫的困难，她对我作为医生，对我妻子作为老朋友和同学的描述。
We soothed and comforted her by such words as we could find.
通过我们能找到的那些话语，我们安慰和安慰了她。
Did she know where her husband was?
她知道她丈夫在哪里吗？
Was it possible that we could bring him back to her?
是否可能将他带回去？
It seems that it was.
看来是这样。
She had the surest information that of late he had, when the fit was on him, made use of an opium den in the farthest east of the City.
她确信，近来他使用鸦片馆的次数最多，当发作时，他会在城的最远东边使用鸦片馆。
Hitherto his orgies had always been confined to one day, and he had come back, twitching and shattered, in the evening.
他以前的狂欢总是局限于一天，晚上回来时，抽搐和破碎，显得疲惫不堪。
But now the spell had been upon him eight-and-forty hours, and he lay there, doubtless among the dregs of the docks, breathing in the poison or sleeping off the effects.
现在，他被魔咒笼罩了八十四小时，躺在那里，很可能在码头的泥潭里，呼吸着毒气，或者睡着了药的副作用。
There he was to be found, she was sure of it, at the Bar of Gold, in Upper Swandam Lane.
她肯定能找到他，他在黄金酒吧，上斯旺达巷。
But what was she to do?
她要做什么？
How could she, a young and timid woman, make her way into such a place and pluck her husband out from among the ruffians who surrounded him?
如何让一个年轻而胆小的女人，找到这样一个地方，从一群围绕着他的粗鄙之徒中，把她的丈夫拉出来？
There was the case, and of course there was but one way out of it.
这是案件，当然只有一个出路。
Might I not escort her to this place?
我是否可以带她去这个地方？
And then, as a second thought, why should she come at all?
然而，作为第二考虑，她为什么要去？
I was Isa Whitney’s medical adviser, and as such I had influence over him.
我是伊萨·惠特尼的医疗顾问，作为这样的人，我有影响。
I could manage it better if I were alone.
如果我独自一人，我可以做得更好。
I promised her on my word that I would send him home in a cab within two hours if he were indeed at the address which she had given me.
我承诺她，以我的话，如果他真的在她给我提供的地址，我会在两小时内把他送到。

And so in ten minutes I had left my armchair and cheery sitting-room behind me, and was speeding eastward in a hansom on a strange errand, as it seemed to me at the time, though the future only could show how strange it was to be.
然而，十分钟后，我离开了我的椅子和愉快的客厅，向东疾驰，好像当时看来，似乎是一个奇怪的使命，尽管未来只有才能显示，这多么奇怪，要被带去一个陌生的地方。
But there was no great difficulty in the first stage of my adventure.
但第一阶段的冒险并没有什么困难。
Upper Swandam Lane is a vile alley lurking behind the high wharves which line the north side of the river to the east of London Bridge.
上沃斯丹姆巷是一条肮脏的巷子，隐藏在伦敦桥东面河岸北侧高码头后面。
Between a slop-shop and a gin-shop, approached by a steep flight of steps leading down to a black gap like the mouth of a cave, I found the den of which I was in search.
在一个杂货店和酒吧之间，我找到了我正在寻找的洞穴。

Ordering my cab to wait, I passed down the steps, worn hollow in the centre by the ceaseless tread of drunken feet; and by the light of a flickering oil-lamp above the door I found the latch and made my way into a long, low room, thick and heavy with the brown opium smoke, and terraced with wooden berths, like the forecastle of an emigrant ship.
我让马车停下，顺着楼梯往下走，楼梯中央被醉鬼的脚踏磨损得凹陷。在门上方的油灯下，我找到了锁，然后进入了长而低的房间，里面弥漫着棕色的鸦片烟雾，木质的床铺排列得像船员的舱室。

Through the gloom one could dimly catch a glimpse of bodies lying in strange fantastic poses, bowed shoulders, bent knees, heads thrown back, and chins pointing upward, with here and there a dark, lack-lustre eye turned upon the newcomer.
在黑暗中，可以看到一些身体躺在奇怪的姿势，弯曲的肩膀，弯曲的膝盖，头仰起，下巴朝上，有时还有一双黯淡无光的眼睛盯着新来的客人。
Out of the black shadows there glimmered little red circles of light, now bright, now faint, as the burning poison waxed or waned in the bowls of the metal pipes.
从黑暗中闪烁着一些小红点，它们时而明亮，时而暗淡，就像金属壶里的燃烧的毒药在膨胀或收缩。

The most lay silent, but some muttered to themselves, and others talked together in a strange, low, monotonous voice, their conversation coming in gushes, and then suddenly tailing off into silence, each mumbling out his own thoughts and paying little heed to the words of his neighbour.
大部分沉默，但有些人低声自言自语，其他人低声交谈，他们的对话像流水一样涌出，然后突然沉默，每个人都在讲述自己的想法，几乎不注意邻居的话。

At the farther end was a small brazier of burning charcoal, beside which on a three-legged wooden stool there sat a tall, thin old man, with his jaw resting upon his two fists, and his elbows upon his knees, staring into the fire.
在远处，有一个小炭火炉，旁边有一个三脚木凳上坐着一个高瘦的老先生，下巴放在两手中，肘放在膝盖上，盯着火。
As I entered, a sallow Malay attendant had hurried up with a pipe for me and a supply of the drug, beckoning me to an empty berth.
当我进来时，一个黄褐色的马来侍者匆匆赶来，给我递上了一支烟和一种药物，叫我坐空铺。
“Thank you.
“谢谢。
I have not come to stay,” said I. “There is a friend of mine here, Mr. Isa Whitney, and I wish to speak with him.”
我不是来逗留的。”我说，“我有个朋友叫西奥，我想和他说话。”
There was a movement and an exclamation from my right, and peering through the gloom, I saw Whitney, pale, haggard, and unkempt, staring out at me.
我右方有动静，黑暗中看到西奥，脸色苍白，憔悴，不整洁，盯着我。
“My God!
“我的天啊！
It’s Watson,” said he.
是沃森。”他说。
He was in a pitiable state of reaction, with every nerve in a twitter.
他处于极度反应状态，每根神经都在颤抖。
“I say, Watson, what o’clock is it?”
"嘿，华生，几点了？"
“Nearly eleven.”
"快十一点了。"
“Of what day?”
"是哪一天？"
“Of Friday, June 19th.”
"是星期五，六月十九日。"
“Good heavens!
"天啊！
I thought it was Wednesday.
我以为是星期三。
It is Wednesday.
星期三。
What d’you want to frighten a chap for?”
你吓唬一个人干什么？"
He sank his face onto his arms and began to sob in a high treble key.
他把脸埋在臂弯里，开始在高音调里号啕大哭。
“I tell you that it is Friday, man.
"我告诉你，今天是星期五。
Your wife has been waiting this two days for you.
你妻子已经等了两天了。
You should be ashamed of yourself!”
你应该为自己的行为感到羞耻！"
“So I am.
"是的。
But you’ve got mixed, Watson, for I have only been here a few hours, three pipes, four pipes—I forget how many.
但是你搞错了，华生，因为我来这儿的时间只有几个小时，三支烟，四支烟——我记不清了。
But I’ll go home with you.
但是我要和你一起去。
I wouldn’t frighten Kate—poor little Kate.
我不会吓到凯特——可怜的凯特。
Give me your hand!
给我手！
Have you a cab?”
你有出租车吗？
“Yes, I have one waiting.”
“是的，我有一辆正在等待。”
“Then I shall go in it.
“那我就坐它。
But I must owe something.
但我必须欠点什么。
Find what I owe, Watson.
找出我欠的，华生。
I am all off colour.
我浑身不适。
I can do nothing for myself.”
我什么也帮不了自己。
I walked down the narrow passage between the double row of sleepers, holding my breath to keep out the vile, stupefying fumes of the drug, and looking about for the manager.
我沿着双层枕木之间的小巷走过去，屏住呼吸，尽量不让那恶臭的麻醉药熏倒，四处张望，寻找经理。
As I passed the tall man who sat by the brazier I felt a sudden pluck at my skirt, and a low voice whispered, “Walk past me, and then look back at me.”
当我经过炉火旁坐着的那位高个子男人时，突然一阵轻微的触碰我的裙摆，低语道：“走过我身边，然后回头看我。”
The words fell quite distinctly upon my ear.
这句话清晰地落在我的耳中。
I glanced down.
我低头一看。

They could only have come from the old man at my side, and yet he sat now as absorbed as ever, very thin, very wrinkled, bent with age, an opium pipe dangling down from between his knees, as though it had dropped in sheer lassitude from his fingers.
只能是从我身边那位老人那里来的，他现在坐得和以前一样专注，瘦削，皱纹满面，佝偻着身子，一根鸦片烟管从膝盖间垂下来，仿佛是出于懒散从手指间滑落。
I took two steps forward and looked back.
我走了两步，回头一看。
It took all my self-control to prevent me from breaking out into a cry of astonishment.
我竭力克制住自己，不让惊讶的叫声从喉咙里冒出来。

He had turned his back so that none could see him but I. His form had filled out, his wrinkles were gone, the dull eyes had regained their fire, and there, sitting by the fire and grinning at my surprise, was none other than Sherlock Holmes.
他转过身去，让我不再能看到他，他的身材丰满了，皱纹消失了，呆滞的眼睛又恢复了活力，坐在火炉旁，咧着嘴对我惊讶的样子，正是我所认识的夏洛克·福尔摩斯。
He made a slight motion to me to approach him, and instantly, as he turned his face half round to the company once more, subsided into a doddering, loose-lipped senility.
他向我做出一个轻微的动作，示意我靠近他，然后他转过脸去，再次面向公司，瞬间变得痴痴呆呆，口齿不清。
“Holmes!”
“福尔摩斯！”
I whispered, “what on earth are you doing in this den?”
我轻声问道：“你在什么地方，你到底在干什么？”
“As low as you can,” he answered; “I have excellent ears.
“低到你所能达到的最低限度，”他回答，“我的耳朵很好。”
If you would have the great kindness to get rid of that sottish friend of yours I should be exceedingly glad to have a little talk with you.”
如果你愿意的话，把那个愚蠢的朋友送走，我非常乐意和你谈谈。”
“I have a cab outside.”
“我有一辆出租车在外面。”
“Then pray send him home in it.
“那么，请你把出租车送他回家。”
You may safely trust him, for he appears to be too limp to get into any mischief.
你完全放心，因为他看起来太软弱，无法干出什么坏事。
I should recommend you also to send a note by the cabman to your wife to say that you have thrown in your lot with me.
我建议你也把信通过出租车司机寄给你的妻子，告诉她你已经和我在一起了。
If you will wait outside, I shall be with you in five minutes.”
如果你愿意，我将在五分钟内到你身边。
It was difficult to refuse any of Sherlock Holmes’ requests, for they were always so exceedingly definite, and put forward with such a quiet air of mastery.
夏洛克·福尔摩斯的任何要求对我来说都很难拒绝，因为它们总是非常明确，而且带着一种平静的气概，显示出他无所不能的掌控。

I felt, however, that when Whitney was once confined in the cab my mission was practically accomplished; and for the rest, I could not wish anything better than to be associated with my friend in one of those singular adventures which were the normal condition of his existence.
我觉得，当韦恩被送进出租车后，我的使命基本上完成了，剩下的事情，我只能希望和我的朋友一起参与那些奇异的冒险，这些冒险是他的正常状态。
In a few minutes I had written my note, paid Whitney’s bill, led him out to the cab, and seen him driven through the darkness.
几分钟后，我写好了信，付清了韦恩的账，把他送出了出租车，看着他被黑暗中驶走。
In a very short time a decrepit figure had emerged from the opium den, and I was walking down the street with Sherlock Holmes.
很短的时间，一个破败的身影从鸦片馆里走出，我和夏洛克·霍尔正沿着街道走着。
For two streets he shuffled along with a bent back and an uncertain foot.
他两步一挪，弯腰驼背，脚也摇晃不定。
Then, glancing quickly round, he straightened himself out and burst into a hearty fit of laughter.
然后，他瞥了一眼四周，挺直了腰，放声大笑起来。
“I suppose, Watson,” said he, “that you imagine that I have added opium-smoking to cocaine injections, and all the other little weaknesses on which you have favoured me with your medical views.”
“我猜想，沃森先生，你认为我除了吸鸦片，还有其他小毛病，你都向我提供过医学见解。”
“I was certainly surprised to find you there.”
“我确实很惊讶，发现你在这里。”
“But not more so than I to find you.”
“但和我一样惊讶，发现你在这里。”
“I came to find a friend.”
“我是来找朋友的。”
“And I to find an enemy.”
“而我来找的，是敌人。”
“An enemy?”
“敌人？”
“Yes; one of my natural enemies, or, shall I say, my natural prey.
“是的，我自然的敌人，或者，我该说，我自然的猎物。
Briefly, Watson, I am in the midst of a very remarkable inquiry, and I have hoped to find a clue in the incoherent ramblings of these sots, as I have done before now.
简短地说，沃森先生，我正处在一件非常奇特的调查之中，我希望能在这些混混的胡言乱语中找到线索，正如我之前所做。

Had I been recognised in that den my life would not have been worth an hour’s purchase; for I have used it before now for my own purposes, and the rascally Lascar who runs it has sworn to have vengeance upon me.
如果我在那个地方被认出来，我的生命价值连城，因为我之前用它来满足自己的需要，而那里的小混混也发誓要报复我。
There is a trap-door at the back of that building, near the corner of Paul’s Wharf, which could tell some strange tales of what has passed through it upon the moonless nights.”
建筑后面有一扇后门，靠近保罗码头的拐角，那里可能藏着一些关于月夜发生的事情的奇怪故事。
“What!
“什么！”
You do not mean bodies?”
你不是说尸体吗？
“Ay, bodies, Watson.
“哎呀，尸体，华生。
We should be rich men if we had £ 1000 for every poor devil who has been done to death in that den.
如果我们有1000英镑，每杀死一个穷人，我们就能成为富人。
It is the vilest murder-trap on the whole riverside, and I fear that Neville St. Clair has entered it never to leave it more.
那里是整个河边最恶劣的谋杀陷阱，我担心内维尔·斯克莱尔先生已经进入并不会再离开。
But our trap should be here.”
但我们的陷阱应该在这里。

He put his two forefingers between his teeth and whistled shrilly—a signal which was answered by a similar whistle from the distance, followed shortly by the rattle of wheels and the clink of horses’ hoofs.
他把两根前牙夹在牙齿之间，尖声吹哨——信号被从远处传来的类似哨声所回答，随后是车轮的咔嚓声和马蹄的叮当声。
“Now, Watson,” said Holmes, as a tall dog-cart dashed up through the gloom, throwing out two golden tunnels of yellow light from its side lanterns.
“现在，华生，”说霍尔姆斯，一辆高大的狗车在黑暗中疾驰，从侧灯中射出两束金色的隧道黄色的光。
“You’ll come with me, won’t you?”
“你愿意跟我一起去吗？”
“If I can be of use.”
“如果我有用的话。”
“Oh, a trusty comrade is always of use; and a chronicler still more so.
“哦，一个忠实的同伴总是有用的，而一个记录者更是如此。
My room at The Cedars is a double-bedded one.”
我在泰德斯德的房间是一张双人床。
“The Cedars?”
“泰德斯德？”
“Yes; that is Mr. St. Clair’s house.
“是的；那是斯克莱尔先生的房子。
I am staying there while I conduct the inquiry.”
我在那里停留，以便进行调查。”
“Where is it, then?”
“那么它在哪里？”
“Near Lee, in Kent.
“在肯特的莱林附近。
We have a seven-mile drive before us.”
我们还有七英里的路要走。
“But I am all in the dark.”
“但我是全然蒙昧的。”
“Of course you are.
“当然你也是。”
You’ll know all about it presently.
你很快就会知道的。
Jump up here.
走上来。
All right, John; we shall not need you.
好吧，约翰；我们不需要你了。
Here’s half a crown.
这是半枚金币。
Look out for me to-morrow, about eleven.
你明天晚上九点要留意一下。
Give her her head.
给她一个头。
So long, then!”
再见！”

He flicked the horse with his whip, and we dashed away through the endless succession of sombre and deserted streets, which widened gradually, until we were flying across a broad balustraded bridge, with the murky river flowing sluggishly beneath us.
他挥动马鞭，我们疾驰穿过无尽的阴暗和荒凉的街道，街道逐渐变宽，直到我们飞驰过一座宽阔的栏杆桥，桥下是浑浊的河水缓慢地流淌。
Beyond lay another dull wilderness of bricks and mortar, its silence broken only by the heavy, regular footfall of the policeman, or the songs and shouts of some belated party of revellers.
超越那里是另一片灰暗的荒野，砖墙和灰泥，只有警察的脚步声和一些晚来聚会的喧闹声打破沉默。
A dull wrack was drifting slowly across the sky, and a star or two twinkled dimly here and there through the rifts of the clouds.
一架暗淡的帆船缓缓地漂浮在天空中，星星或两颗星星在云缝中闪烁。

Holmes drove in silence, with his head sunk upon his breast, and the air of a man who is lost in thought, while I sat beside him, curious to learn what this new quest might be which seemed to tax his powers so sorely, and yet afraid to break in upon the current of his thoughts.
森林侦探在沉默中驾驶，头低垂在胸前，像一个陷入思考的人，而我坐在他旁边，好奇于这个新探求，似乎耗尽了他力量，又害怕打断他的思绪。

We had driven several miles, and were beginning to get to the fringe of the belt of suburban villas, when he shook himself, shrugged his shoulders, and lit up his pipe with the air of a man who has satisfied himself that he is acting for the best.
我们已经行驶了几个英里，正接近郊区别墅的边缘，这时他振作起来，耸耸肩，用烟斗的空气像一个满足的人一样，而我坐在他旁边，好奇于这个新探求，似乎耗尽了他力量，又害怕打断他的思绪。
“You have a grand gift of silence, Watson,” said he.
“你有沉默的天赋，沃森先生。”
“It makes you quite invaluable as a companion. ’Pon my word, it is a great thing for me to have someone to talk to, for my own thoughts are not over-pleasant.
“这使你成为我的同伴非常有用。我保证，和我交谈是一件好事，因为我的想法并不愉快。
I was wondering what I should say to this dear little woman to-night when she meets me at the door.”
我在门边遇见她时，正想知道该对她说些什么。”
“You forget that I know nothing about it.”
“你忘记了，我什么都不知道。”
“I shall just have time to tell you the facts of the case before we get to Lee.
“我们到莱恩之前，就该把案件的经过告诉你了。”
It seems absurdly simple, and yet, somehow I can get nothing to go upon.
“看起来简单，但又好像毫无头绪。”
There’s plenty of thread, no doubt, but I can’t get the end of it into my hand.
“当然有线，但拿不到手。”
Now, I’ll state the case clearly and concisely to you, Watson, and maybe you can see a spark where all is dark to me.”
“现在，我将清楚而简洁地向你说明案件，沃森先生，也许你能看到我所不知道的东西的火花。”
“Proceed, then.”
“继续吧。”
“Some years ago—to be definite, in May, 1884—there came to Lee a gentleman, Neville St. Clair by name, who appeared to have plenty of money.
“许多年前——确切地说，是在1884年5月——有个名叫诺维尔·斯克莱尔的先生来到莱恩，他似乎有很多钱。
He took a large villa, laid out the grounds very nicely, and lived generally in good style.
他租了一栋大别墅，把花园布置得很漂亮，并且过着体面的生活。
By degrees he made friends in the neighbourhood, and in 1887 he married the daughter of a local brewer, by whom he now has two children.
他渐渐地在附近交了朋友，并在1887年娶了当地酿酒厂主的女儿，现在他有两个孩子。
He had no occupation, but was interested in several companies and went into town as a rule in the morning, returning by the 5:14 from Cannon Street every night.
他没有职业，但对一些公司很感兴趣，每天早上进城，晚上从坎农街5:14出发返回。
Mr. St. Clair is now thirty-seven years of age, is a man of temperate habits, a good husband, a very affectionate father, and a man who is popular with all who know him.
斯克莱尔先生现在37岁，是一个有节制的人，是个好丈夫，是个非常爱他的父亲，是个所有认识他的人都喜欢的人。
I may add that his whole debts at the present moment, as far as we have been able to ascertain, amount to £ 88 10s., while he has £ 220 standing to his credit in the Capital and Counties Bank.
我可以补充说，目前他的所有债务，根据我们所知道的，总共是88英镑10先令，而他在资本和县银行有220英镑的信用。
There is no reason, therefore, to think that money troubles have been weighing upon his mind.
因此，他没有理由认为金钱问题困扰了他的心。

“Last Monday Mr. Neville St. Clair went into town rather earlier than usual, remarking before he started that he had two important commissions to perform, and that he would bring his little boy home a box of bricks.
“上个星期一，南希·斯克里尔先生进城时比平时早了一些，他出发前说他有两个重要的任务要完成，还说他要带他的小儿子回家一箱砖头。

Now, by the merest chance, his wife received a telegram upon this same Monday, very shortly after his departure, to the effect that a small parcel of considerable value which she had been expecting was waiting for her at the offices of the Aberdeen Shipping Company.
现在，只是偶然的机会，他的妻子在这一星期一收到了一封电报，她出发前不久，电报说她所期待的小包裹在爱丁堡航运公司的工作处等着她。
Now, if you are well up in your London, you will know that the office of the company is in Fresno Street, which branches out of Upper Swandam Lane, where you found me to-night.
现在，如果你在伦敦很有经验，你就会知道这家公司的工作处位于弗雷斯诺街，它从上斯旺德姆街分出，你今天晚上在这里遇到的。

Mrs. St. Clair had her lunch, started for the City, did some shopping, proceeded to the company’s office, got her packet, and found herself at exactly 4:35 walking through Swandam Lane on her way back to the station.
斯克里尔太太吃午饭，去城里购物，然后去公司的工作处，取了包裹，发现自己在4:35时，沿着斯旺德姆街走着，准备回家。
Have you followed me so far?”
你一直跟着我了吗？
“It is very clear.”
“很清楚。
“If you remember, Monday was an exceedingly hot day, and Mrs. St. Clair walked slowly, glancing about in the hope of seeing a cab, as she did not like the neighbourhood in which she found herself.
“如果你记得，星期一是个非常炎热的日子，斯克里尔太太慢慢地走着，希望看到一辆出租车，因为她不喜欢她所发现的地区。

While she was walking in this way down Swandam Lane, she suddenly heard an ejaculation or cry, and was struck cold to see her husband looking down at her and, as it seemed to her, beckoning to her from a second-floor window.
当她沿着斯旺德姆街走着时，她突然听到一声叫喊，她被突然看到丈夫在二楼窗口向下指，好像被某种不可抗拒的力量从后面拉走。
The window was open, and she distinctly saw his face, which she describes as being terribly agitated.
窗口是开着的，她清楚地看到他的脸，她描述他的脸非常激动。
He waved his hands frantically to her, and then vanished from the window so suddenly that it seemed to her that he had been plucked back by some irresistible force from behind.
他挥动他的手，疯狂地向她挥动，然后从窗口消失，好像被某种不可抗拒的力量从后面拉走。
One singular point which struck her quick feminine eye was that although he wore some dark coat, such as he had started to town in, he had on neither collar nor necktie.
一个使她敏锐的女性眼睛特别注意到的一个奇异点是，尽管他穿了一件黑色的外套，像他出发时穿的，他没有领带或领带。

“Convinced that something was amiss with him, she rushed down the steps—for the house was none other than the opium den in which you found me to-night—and running through the front room she attempted to ascend the stairs which led to the first floor.
“相信他出了什么事，她冲下楼梯，因为这房子不是今晚你遇到的那家鸦片馆，她穿过前厅，试图登上通往一楼的楼梯。
At the foot of the stairs, however, she met this Lascar scoundrel of whom I have spoken, who thrust her back and, aided by a Dane, who acts as assistant there, pushed her out into the street.
在楼梯的脚下，她遇到了我提到的这个印度水手，他把她推了回去，由一个丹麦人，他在那里起着助手的作用，推她出去到街上。
Filled with the most maddening doubts and fears, she rushed down the lane and, by rare good-fortune, met in Fresno Street a number of constables with an inspector, all on their way to their beat.
她充满了最令人发狂的怀疑和恐惧，冲下这条巷子，幸运的是，在弗雷斯诺街，她遇到了一群警察，一个检查员，他们去巡逻，她遇到了他们。
The inspector and two men accompanied her back, and in spite of the continued resistance of the proprietor, they made their way to the room in which Mr. St. Clair had last been seen.
检察官和两名男子陪她回去了，尽管店主一直极力反抗，他们还是找到了 Mr. St. Clair 最后出现的房间。
There was no sign of him there.
那里没有他的踪迹。
In fact, in the whole of that floor there was no one to be found save a crippled wretch of hideous aspect, who, it seems, made his home there.
实际上，在整层楼里，除了一个瘸子，样子丑陋不堪，他似乎在那里住着。
Both he and the Lascar stoutly swore that no one else had been in the front room during the afternoon.
他和水手坚决声称下午没有人在前厅。

So determined was their denial that the inspector was staggered, and had almost come to believe that Mrs. St. Clair had been deluded when, with a cry, she sprang at a small deal box which lay upon the table and tore the lid from it.
他们拒绝得如此坚决，以至于检察官几乎相信，斯蒂尔夫人被欺骗了，当她尖叫着冲向桌上的一个小盒子，撕开了盒子的盖子时，盒子的盖子被撕开了。
Out there fell a cascade of children’s bricks.
那里掉下来一串孩子的砖块。
It was the toy which he had promised to bring home.
这是他答应要带回家的玩具。
“This discovery, and the evident confusion which the cripple showed, made the inspector realise that the matter was serious.
“这个发现和瘸子明显表现出的混乱，使检察官意识到事情很严重。
The rooms were carefully examined, and results all pointed to an abominable crime.
房间仔细检查过，所有迹象都指向了极其恶劣的犯罪。
The front room was plainly furnished as a sitting-room and led into a small bedroom, which looked out upon the back of one of the wharves.
前厅显然被布置成一个客厅，通向一个小卧室，这个卧室面向码头的一个角落。
Between the wharf and the bedroom window is a narrow strip, which is dry at low tide but is covered at high tide with at least four and a half feet of water.
从码头和卧室窗户之间有一条狭窄的通道，低潮时是干的，但高潮时至少有四英尺五英寸的水。
The bedroom window was a broad one and opened from below.
卧室窗户是一个宽的窗户，从下面打开。
On examination traces of blood were to be seen upon the windowsill, and several scattered drops were visible upon the wooden floor of the bedroom.
仔细检查后，在窗户台上可以看到血迹，在卧室的木板地板上可以看到几滴血迹。
Thrust away behind a curtain in the front room were all the clothes of Mr. Neville St. Clair, with the exception of his coat.
推到前面房间的一幅窗帘后面去的，都是 Neville 霍斯特先生的衣服，除了他的大衣以外。
His boots, his socks, his hat, and his watch—all were there.
他的靴子、袜子、帽子和手表——都在那里。
There were no signs of violence upon any of these garments, and there were no other traces of Mr. Neville St. Clair.
这些衣物上没有暴力的痕迹，也没有其他迹象表明南希先生已经离开。

Out of the window he must apparently have gone for no other exit could be discovered, and the ominous bloodstains upon the sill gave little promise that he could save himself by swimming, for the tide was at its very highest at the moment of the tragedy.
从窗口出去似乎是他唯一的选择，因为从窗户看到的血迹表明，他无法通过游泳逃脱，因为此时正是大潮的最高潮。
“And now as to the villains who seemed to be immediately implicated in the matter.
“现在，关于那些似乎立即与案件有关的罪犯。

The Lascar was known to be a man of the vilest antecedents, but as, by Mrs. St. Clair’s story, he was known to have been at the foot of the stair within a very few seconds of her husband’s appearance at the window, he could hardly have been more than an accessory to the crime.
这个水手的背景非常恶劣，但根据斯蒂尔夫人讲述的情况，他在丈夫出现时，就在楼梯的脚边，不可能比他更接近犯罪。

His defence was one of absolute ignorance, and he protested that he had no knowledge as to the doings of Hugh Boone, his lodger, and that he could not account in any way for the presence of the missing gentleman’s clothes.
他的辩护是完全的无知，他坚称他不知道约书亚·布恩的所作所为，也无法解释为什么失踪的绅士的衣物出现在那里。
“So much for the Lascar manager.
“所以，水手经理的事就这样了。
Now for the sinister cripple who lives upon the second floor of the opium den, and who was certainly the last human being whose eyes rested upon Neville St. Clair.
现在，对于住在二楼鸦片馆的阴险瘸子，我们来看看。
His name is Hugh Boone, and his hideous face is one which is familiar to every man who goes much to the City.
他的名字叫约书亚·布恩，他的丑陋的面孔是每个去城里的人都知道的。
He is a professional beggar, though in order to avoid the police regulations he pretends to a small trade in wax vestas.
他是一个专业的乞丐，尽管为了避开警察的规定，他假装从事小贸易。
Some little distance down Threadneedle Street, upon the left-hand side, there is, as you may have remarked, a small angle in the wall.
在泰德纳街的某个地方，左转，你会看到墙角。

Then with a red head of hair, and an appropriate dress, I took my station in the business part of the city, ostensibly as a match-seller but really as a beggar.
然后，我用红色头发，穿着合适的服装，站在商业区，假装卖火柴，实际上是一个乞丐。
For seven hours I plied my trade, and when I returned home in the evening I found to my surprise that I had received no less than 26s.
我在街上卖了七个小时，晚上回家时发现我收到了26先令4便士。
4便士。
“I wrote my articles and thought little more of the matter until, some time later, I backed a bill for a friend and had a writ served upon me for £ 25.
我写了一些文章，只关心这件事，直到某段时间后，我为朋友开了一张欠款25英镑的欠条。
I was at my wit’s end where to get the money, but a sudden idea came to me.
我在为钱发愁，突然想到一个办法。
I begged a fortnight’s grace from the creditor, asked for a holiday from my employers, and spent the time in begging in the City under my disguise.
我向债权人请求宽限两个月，向雇主请假，花时间在伦敦的街头乞讨，以化装身份。
In ten days I had the money and had paid the debt.
十天后，我有了钱，还清了债务。

“Well, you can imagine how hard it was to settle down to arduous work at £ 2 a week when I knew that I could earn as much in a day by smearing my face with a little paint, laying my cap on the ground, and sitting still.
“嗯，你想想，要安下心来每周挣2英镑的工作，我却知道一天可以赚2英镑，靠涂脸、把帽子丢在地上、坐在那里。

It was a long fight between my pride and the money, but the dollars won at last, and I threw up reporting and sat day after day in the corner which I had first chosen, inspiring pity by my ghastly face and filling my pockets with coppers.
这是一场与骄傲和钱的斗争，但最后美元赢了，我放弃了报道，每天坐在角落里，用丑陋的脸和铜钱装钱。
Only one man knew my secret.
只有一个知道我的秘密。

He was the keeper of a low den in which I used to lodge in Swandam Lane, where I could every morning emerge as a squalid beggar and in the evenings transform myself into a well-dressed man about town.
他是斯旺德姆巷一个肮脏窝点的看守，在那里我曾住过，我可以每天早上化身为一个肮脏的乞丐，晚上又变成一个街坊常客。
This fellow, a Lascar, was well paid by me for his rooms, so that I knew that my secret was safe in his possession.
这个船长，我为他的房间付了钱，所以我知道我的秘密在他手中。
“Well, very soon I found that I was saving considerable sums of money.
“嗯，很快我发现自己在节省钱。

I do not mean that any beggar in the streets of London could earn £ 700 a year—which is less than my average takings—but I had exceptional advantages in my power of making up, and also in a facility of repartee, which improved by practice and made me quite a recognised character in the City.
我并不是说伦敦街头的乞丐一年能赚700英镑——这比我的平均收入少得多——但我有特殊的优势，我善于算计，也善于言辞，这些都因练习而变得熟练，使我成了伦敦城中一个很受人欢迎的人物。
All day a stream of pennies, varied by silver, poured in upon me, and it was a very bad day in which I failed to take £ 2.
一天来了一条条铜钱，有时还有银币，我每天都很糟糕，没有取到2英镑。
“As I grew richer I grew more ambitious, took a house in the country, and eventually married, without anyone having a suspicion as to my real occupation.
“随着我变得富有，我变得更有野心，买了一间乡间房子，最终结婚，没有人怀疑我的真实职业。
My dear wife knew that I had business in the City.
我亲爱的妻子知道我在伦敦城有业务。
She little knew what.
她不知道什么。

“Last Monday I had finished for the day and was dressing in my room above the opium den when I looked out of my window and saw, to my horror and astonishment, that my wife was standing in the street, with her eyes fixed full upon me.
上个星期一，我下班后正准备换衣服，在我房间的楼上，我透过窗户看到，我的妻子站在街上，眼睛盯着我。
I gave a cry of surprise, threw up my arms to cover my face, and, rushing to my confidant, the Lascar, entreated him to prevent anyone from coming up to me.
我大吃一惊，双手捂住脸，冲向我的密友——水手，恳求他阻止任何人靠近我。
I heard her voice downstairs, but I knew that she could not ascend.
我听到楼下有人声，但我知道她无法上楼。
Swiftly I threw off my clothes, pulled on those of a beggar, and put on my pigments and wig.
我迅速脱掉衣服，穿上乞丐的衣服，戴上我的假发。
Even a wife’s eyes could not pierce so complete a disguise.
我迅速打开窗户，用暴力重新修复了我早上卧室里自己留下的小伤口。
But then it occurred to me that there might be a search in the room, and that the clothes might betray me.
然后我抓起我的外套，这外套是用铜钱加固的，我刚从皮包里转移到外套里的。
I threw open the window, reopening by my violence a small cut which I had inflicted upon myself in the bedroom that morning.
我用力扔出外套，它消失在泰晤士河里。
Then I seized my coat, which was weighted by the coppers which I had just transferred to it from the leather bag in which I carried my takings.
然后我抓住我的大衣，大衣上挂着我刚才从皮夹克袋中转移到它上面的几枚铜币。
I hurled it out of the window, and it disappeared into the Thames.
“我不知道还有什么需要解释的。”

The other clothes would have followed, but at that moment there was a rush of constables up the stair, and a few minutes after I found, rather, I confess, to my relief, that instead of being identified as Mr. Neville St. Clair, I was arrested as his murderer.
我决心尽可能长时间地保持我的伪装，因此我更喜欢脏脸。
“I do not know that there is anything else for me to explain.
知道妻子会非常担心，我摘下戒指，告诉水手，一个匆忙的潦草字条，告诉她她不必担心。
I was determined to preserve my disguise as long as possible, and hence my preference for a dirty face.
“那条字条只送到昨天。”说霍尔姆斯。

Knowing that my wife would be terribly anxious, I slipped off my ring and confided it to the Lascar at a moment when no constable was watching me, together with a hurried scrawl, telling her that she had no cause to fear.”
“天啊！”
“That note only reached her yesterday,” said Holmes.
“那张便条只是昨天才到达她的。”说的是一字一句。
“Good God!
“天啊！”
What a week she must have spent!”
她这一周肯定过得非常辛苦！
“The police have watched this Lascar,” said Inspector Bradstreet, “and I can quite understand that he might find it difficult to post a letter unobserved.
“警察已经盯上了这个水手，”布拉德斯特路警官说，“我能完全理解他可能难以不被注意到就寄信。
Probably he handed it to some sailor customer of his, who forgot all about it for some days.”
他大概把信交给了一个水手顾客，那人几天里都忘了这件事。
“That was it,” said Holmes, nodding approvingly; “I have no doubt of it.
“没错，”霍尔姆斯点点头，“我肯定。
But have you never been prosecuted for begging?”
但你从来没有因为乞讨被起诉过吗？
“Many times; but what was a fine to me?”
“很多次，但我对罚款有什么感觉呢？
“It must stop here, however,” said Bradstreet.
“无论如何，”布拉德斯特路说，“必须在这里结束。
“If the police are to hush this thing up, there must be no more of Hugh Boone.”
“如果警察要掩盖这件事，那么休·布恩不能再继续下去了。
“I have sworn it by the most solemn oaths which a man can take.”
“我发誓，我用了一个男人可以发誓的最庄严的誓言。
“In that case I think that it is probable that no further steps may be taken.
“如果这样的话，我认为，再没有什么可以进一步采取的了。
But if you are found again, then all must come out.
但如果你再被发现，那么一切都将揭开。
I am sure, Mr. Holmes, that we are very much indebted to you for having cleared the matter up.
我确信，先生霍尔姆斯，我们对你的帮助非常感激。
I wish I knew how you reach your results.”
我想知道你是怎么得出结论的。
“I reached this one,” said my friend, “by sitting upon five pillows and consuming an ounce of shag.
“我朋友说，我通过坐在五把椅子上和吃了一盎司的松毛虫，得出这个结论。
I think, Watson, that if we drive to Baker Street we shall just be in time for breakfast.”
我认为，沃森先生，如果我们开车去贝克街，我们刚好赶得上早餐。

ch.et: VII. The Adventure of the Blue Carbuncle
p: I had called upon my friend Sherlock Holmes upon the second morning after Christmas, with the intention of wishing him the compliments of the season.
我在圣诞节后的第二天早晨拜访了我朋友夏洛克·福尔摩斯，打算祝他节日快乐。
He was lounging upon the sofa in a purple dressing-gown, a pipe-rack within his reach upon the right, and a pile of crumpled morning papers, evidently newly studied, near at hand.
他正坐在沙发上，穿着紫色的睡衣，右手边放着一个烟灰缸，旁边放着一堆刚读过的晨报，显然刚刚研读过。
Beside the couch was a wooden chair, and on the angle of the back hung a very seedy and disreputable hard-felt hat, much the worse for wear, and cracked in several places.
舒服的木椅靠背角上挂着一个破旧不堪的硬毛毡帽子，破烂不堪，裂开好几个地方。
A lens and a forceps lying upon the seat of the chair suggested that the hat had been suspended in this manner for the purpose of examination.
椅子上的显微镜和镊子暗示，帽子是用这种方式悬挂起来进行检查的。
“You are engaged,” said I; “perhaps I interrupt you.”
“你有约会。”我说，“也许我打扰了你。”
“Not at all.
“不，不。
I am glad to have a friend with whom I can discuss my results.
我很高兴有一个朋友，可以讨论我的结果。

The matter is a perfectly trivial one”—he jerked his thumb in the direction of the old hat—“but there are points in connection with it which are not entirely devoid of interest and even of instruction.”
这事很轻微——”他用拇指指着那顶旧帽子——“但与它有关的点，有些不完全无趣，甚至有些有趣和值得学习。”
I seated myself in his armchair and warmed my hands before his crackling fire, for a sharp frost had set in, and the windows were thick with the ice crystals.
我坐在他的扶手椅上，暖和了暖和手，因为寒霜降临了，窗户上结满了冰晶。

“I suppose,” I remarked, “that, homely as it looks, this thing has some deadly story linked on to it—that it is the clue which will guide you in the solution of some mystery and the punishment of some crime.”
“我猜，”我说，“这东西看起来很普通，但一定有一个致命的故事跟它有关——那是一个线索，会引导你解决某个谜团，惩治某个犯罪。”
“No, no.
“不，不。
No crime,” said Sherlock Holmes, laughing.
没有犯罪。”夏洛克·福尔摩斯笑着说。
“Only one of those whimsical little incidents which will happen when you have four million human beings all jostling each other within the space of a few square miles.
“只有那些发生在四百万人类拥挤在几平方英里内时的荒诞小事件。”

Amid the action and reaction of so dense a swarm of humanity, every possible combination of events may be expected to take place, and many a little problem will be presented which may be striking and bizarre without being criminal.
在如此密集的人群中，各种各样的事件可能会发生，许多个小小的难题可能会出现，这些难题虽然不犯罪，但很有趣，甚至很值得学习。
We have already had experience of such.”
我们已经体验过这样的事情了。”
“So much so,” I remarked, “that of the last six cases which I have added to my notes, three have been entirely free of any legal crime.”
如此之多，”我 remark，“以致于在我笔记中最后六起案件中，有三起完全没有任何法律犯罪。”
“Precisely.
“正是如此。
You allude to my attempt to recover the Irene Adler papers, to the singular case of Miss Mary Sutherland, and to the adventure of the man with the twisted lip.
你指的是我试图找回伊丽莎白·阿德勒的文件，还有玛丽·斯图尔特小姐的奇异案件，以及那位唇形扭曲男子的冒险。
Well, I have no doubt that this small matter will fall into the same innocent category.
好吧，我肯定这小事情会落入同一种无辜的类别。
You know Peterson, the commissionaire?”
你知道佩特森吗？
“Yes.”
“是的。”
“It is to him that this trophy belongs.”
“这是属于他的奖品。
“It is his hat.”
“这是他的帽子。”
“No, no, he found it.
“不，不，他发现的。”
Its owner is unknown.
“它的主人是未知的。”
I beg that you will look upon it not as a battered billycock but as an intellectual problem.
我恳求你不要把它看作一个破旧的帽子，而是把它看作一个智力问题。
And, first, as to how it came here.
首先，关于它怎么来到这里。
It arrived upon Christmas morning, in company with a good fat goose, which is, I have no doubt, roasting at this moment in front of Peterson’s fire.
它在圣诞节早上到达的，带着一只大肥鹅，我肯定此刻它正在彼得森的火炉前烤着。

The facts are these: about four o’clock on Christmas morning, Peterson, who, as you know, is a very honest fellow, was returning from some small jollification and was making his way homeward down Tottenham Court Road.
事实是这样的：大约四点钟的圣诞节早上，彼得森，你知道的，是一个非常诚实的人，正在回家的路上，他正沿着特温特公园大道返回。
In front of him he saw, in the gaslight, a tallish man, walking with a slight stagger, and carrying a white goose slung over his shoulder.
他前面看见，在煤气灯下，一个高个子的人，步履蹒跚，手里提着一只白鹅。
As he reached the corner of Goodge Street, a row broke out between this stranger and a little knot of roughs.
当他走到Goodge街拐角处时，一个群体与一群粗人之间爆发了冲突。
One of the latter knocked off the man’s hat, on which he raised his stick to defend himself and, swinging it over his head, smashed the shop window behind him.
一个粗人敲掉了那人帽子，他举起棍子来保护自己，挥舞着棍子，砸破了他身后的一扇窗户。

Peterson had rushed forward to protect the stranger from his assailants; but the man, shocked at having broken the window, and seeing an official-looking person in uniform rushing towards him, dropped his goose, took to his heels, and vanished amid the labyrinth of small streets which lie at the back of Tottenham Court Road.
Peterson冲上前去保护那个陌生人，但那人被砸破的窗户吓到了，看到穿着制服的官员向他走来，就扔掉了他的鹅，跑了起来，消失在通往特温斯特街路的巷子中。

The roughs had also fled at the appearance of Peterson, so that he was left in possession of the field of battle, and also of the spoils of victory in the shape of this battered hat and a most unimpeachable Christmas goose.”
粗人也跟着跑开了，所以只剩下Peterson在战场上，也保留了这个破帽和一只非常可靠的圣诞节鹅。
“Which surely he restored to their owner?”
“那么，他把帽子和鹅都送回来了吗？”
“My dear fellow, there lies the problem.
“亲爱的先生，这确实是个问题。
It is true that ‘For Mrs. Henry Baker’ was printed upon a small card which was tied to the bird’s left leg, and it is also true that the initials ‘H.
那是真的，‘对于亨利·贝aker夫人’这几个字印在一张小卡片上，这张卡片系在那只鸟的左腿上，而且亨利·H的 initials 也确实印在那里。

B.’ are legible upon the lining of this hat, but as there are some thousands of Bakers, and some hundreds of Henry Bakers in this city of ours, it is not easy to restore lost property to any one of them.”
B.’ 是这顶帽子 lining 上可以辨认的，但这个城市中有上千个 Baker，也有几百个 Henry Baker，要归还遗失的财产给其中任何一个都颇不容易。”
“What, then, did Peterson do?”
“那么，Peterson做了什么？”
“He brought round both hat and goose to me on Christmas morning, knowing that even the smallest problems are of interest to me.
“他把帽子和鹅都送到了我的面前，知道即使是最小的问题对我来说也是有趣的。
The goose we retained until this morning, when there were signs that, in spite of the slight frost, it would be well that it should be eaten without unnecessary delay.
我们保留了这只鹅，直到今天早上，因为尽管有轻微的霜冻，我们还是希望在不延迟的情况下把它吃掉。
Its finder has carried it off, therefore, to fulfil the ultimate destiny of a goose, while I continue to retain the hat of the unknown gentleman who lost his Christmas dinner.”
它的发现者把它带走了，因此，它完成了一只鹅的最终命运，而我仍然保留着这个陌生人丢失的圣诞节晚餐的破帽。
“Did he not advertise?”
“他没有广告吗？”
“No.”
“没有。”
“Then, what clue could you have as to his identity?”
“那么，你有什么线索可以确定他的身份？”
“Only as much as we can deduce.”
只能推断出我们能推断的那么多了。
“From his hat?”
“从他的帽子？”
“Precisely.”
“正是。”
“But you are joking.
“但你是在开玩笑。
What can you gather from this old battered felt?”
从这顶破旧的旧旧的呢帽能推断出什么来？
“Here is my lens.
“这是我的望远镜。
You know my methods.
你知道我的方法。
What can you gather yourself as to the individuality of the man who has worn this article?”
你自己能推断出这个人穿这顶帽子的个性吗？
I took the tattered object in my hands and turned it over rather ruefully.
我接过这破破烂烂的东西，有些不情愿地翻了翻。
It was a very ordinary black hat of the usual round shape, hard and much the worse for wear.
它是一顶普通的黑色帽子，圆头，硬邦邦的，已经破旧不堪。
The lining had been of red silk, but was a good deal discoloured.
衬里是红色的丝绒，但已经有些褪色。
There was no maker’s name; but, as Holmes had remarked, the initials “H. B.” were scrawled upon one side.
没有制造商的名称；但，正如霍尔姆斯所说的，帽子上的“H. B.”字样是潦草写的。
It was pierced in the brim for a hat-securer, but the elastic was missing.
它在帽檐上有一个洞，用来固定帽子，但弹性绳已经不见了。
For the rest, it was cracked, exceedingly dusty, and spotted in several places, although there seemed to have been some attempt to hide the discoloured patches by smearing them with ink.
其余的，它已经裂开，非常尘土飞扬，有些地方还被涂上墨水，似乎有人试图掩盖褪色的斑点。
“I can see nothing,” said I, handing it back to my friend.
“我看不出什么。”我说着，把帽子还给了我朋友。
“On the contrary, Watson, you can see everything.
"恰恰相反，沃森先生，你什么都看不见。
You fail, however, to reason from what you see.
但是你却不能从你所看到的推导出结论。
You are too timid in drawing your inferences.”
你太胆小了，不能从你的推论中得出结论。
“Then, pray tell me what it is that you can infer from this hat?”
那么，告诉我，你从这顶帽子中能推导出什么结论？
He picked it up and gazed at it in the peculiar introspective fashion which was characteristic of him.
他捡起来，用他特有的 introspective 观察方式 peculiar 地凝视着那顶帽子。

“It is perhaps less suggestive than it might have been,” he remarked, “and yet there are a few inferences which are very distinct, and a few others which represent at least a strong balance of probability.
"这顶帽子也许不如它看起来那么有暗示性，然而却有一些非常明确的推论，还有一些推论则代表了相当的概率平衡。
That the man was highly intellectual is of course obvious upon the face of it, and also that he was fairly well-to-do within the last three years, although he has now fallen upon evil days.
这个人显然是个非常聪明的人，而且他最近三年来还算过得不错，尽管现在他陷入了困境。

He had foresight, but has less now than formerly, pointing to a moral retrogression, which, when taken with the decline of his fortunes, seems to indicate some evil influence, probably drink, at work upon him.
他有预见能力，但现在已经不如以前了，这暗示着一种道德的退步，当这种退步与他的经济状况的下降结合起来时，似乎暗示着某种邪恶的影响，可能是酒。
This may account also for the obvious fact that his wife has ceased to love him.”
这也可能解释为什么他的妻子不再爱他。
“My dear Holmes!”
"亲爱的华生先生！"
“He has, however, retained some degree of self-respect,” he continued, disregarding my remonstrance.
"然而，他仍然保留了一些自尊，"他继续说道，无视我的劝阻。

“He is a man who leads a sedentary life, goes out little, is out of training entirely, is middle-aged, has grizzled hair which he has had cut within the last few days, and which he anoints with lime-cream.
"他是个安于现状的人，很少外出，完全缺乏训练，中年，最近几天他剪了头发，用石灰奶油抹了头发。
These are the more patent facts which are to be deduced from his hat.
这些是帽子中可以推导出来的更明显的事实。
Also, by the way, that it is extremely improbable that he has gas laid on in his house.”
顺便说一句，这顶帽子非常不可能在房子里安装煤气。
“You are certainly joking, Holmes.”
"你肯定是开玩笑的，华生先生。"
“Not in the least.
一点也不。
Is it possible that even now, when I give you these results, you are unable to see how they are attained?”
是否可能现在，当我把这些结果给你时，你仍然无法看到它们是如何得到的？
“I have no doubt that I am very stupid, but I must confess that I am unable to follow you.
我确信 myself 定是 stupid ，但必须 confess 必须 必须 必须  confess  that 我是 unable to follow you 难以 跟上 你 的 解析和注释已经给出，无需重复。
For example, how did you deduce that this man was intellectual?”
例如，你怎么推断出这个男人是有才智的？
For answer Holmes clapped the hat upon his head.
福尔摩斯搔搔头回答道。
It came right over the forehead and settled upon the bridge of his nose.
正好盖在前额上，落在鼻梁上。

“既然如此，我们最好在安静的房间里讨论，而不是在这风沙肆虐的集市广场上。”
“But pray tell me, before we go farther, who it is that I have the pleasure of assisting.”
“不过，在我们继续前行之前，请告诉我，是谁让我感到荣幸。”
The man hesitated for an instant.
这人犹豫了一下。
“My name is John Robinson,” he answered with a sidelong glance.
“我的名字叫约翰·罗宾逊。”他以斜眼瞥了一眼后回答。
“No, no; the real name,” said Holmes sweetly.
“不，不，是真名。”说来时，莫格里奇先生甜美地说道。
“It is always awkward doing business with an alias.”
“做买卖总得小心，别用假名。”
A flush sprang to the white cheeks of the stranger.
这陌生人的脸颊泛起了红晕。
“Well then,” said he, “my real name is James Ryder.”
“好吧，”他说，“我的真名是詹姆斯·瑞德。”
“Precisely so.
“正是这样。”
Head attendant at the Hotel Cosmopolitan.
酒店科姆朋顿的头侍者。
Pray step into the cab, and I shall soon be able to tell you everything which you would wish to know.”
请进车里，我很快就能告诉你你想知道的一切。”
The little man stood glancing from one to the other of us with half-frightened, half-hopeful eyes, as one who is not sure whether he is on the verge of a windfall or of a catastrophe.
这个小个子站在我们中间，用半惊恐半希望的眼神打量着我们，仿佛不知道自己是处在好运还是灾难的边缘。
Then he stepped into the cab, and in half an hour we were back in the sitting-room at Baker Street.
然后他进了车，半个小时后，我们回到了贝克街的客厅。
Nothing had been said during our drive, but the high, thin breathing of our new companion, and the claspings and unclaspings of his hands, spoke of the nervous tension within him.
在我们驾车的过程中，什么也没有说，但这个新同伴的高声细语和手的扣动和松开，透露了他内心的紧张。
“Here we are!” said Holmes cheerily as we filed into the room.
"我们到了！" 海默高兴地说道，我们一行人走进房间。
“The fire looks very seasonable in this weather.
"这天气看来很合适，" 海默说。
You look cold, Mr. Ryder.
"你看起来很冷，" 雷德先生说。
Pray take the basket-chair.
"请坐到那张椅子上。
I will just put on my slippers before we settle this little matter of yours.
"我先穿上拖鞋，然后我们来解决一下这个问题。
Now, then!
"好了，好了！
You want to know what became of those geese?”
"你想知道那些鹅的下落吗？
“Yes, sir.”
"是的，先生。
“Or rather, I fancy, of that goose.
"或者，我想，是那只鹅。
It was one bird, I imagine in which you were interested—white, with a black bar across the tail.”
"我想，你感兴趣的那只鹅，应该是白色的，尾部有一道黑色的条纹。
Ryder quivered with emotion.
雷德先生激动地颤抖起来。
“Oh, sir,” he cried, “can you tell me where it went to?”
"哦，先生，" 他喊道，"你能告诉我它去了哪里吗？
“It came here.”
"它来了。
“Here?”
"来了？
“Yes, and a most remarkable bird it proved.
"是的，而且它证明了它是一只非常特别的鸟。"
I don’t wonder that you should take an interest in it.
我不明白你为什么会对它感兴趣。
It laid an egg after it was dead—the bonniest, brightest little blue egg that ever was seen.
它在死掉后产了一个蛋——那是一个蓝蛋，蓝得像宝石一样，亮得像星星，点点闪耀。
I have it here in my museum.”
它在我的博物馆里。
Our visitor staggered to his feet and clutched the mantelpiece with his right hand.
我们的访客踉踉跄跄地站起身，右手抓住了壁炉架。
Holmes unlocked his strong-box and held up the blue carbuncle, which shone out like a star, with a cold, brilliant, many-pointed radiance.
棕油把他的保险箱打开，举起那颗蓝宝石，它像一颗星星一样闪闪发光，散发着冷冽的、明亮的、多点的光芒。
Ryder stood glaring with a drawn face, uncertain whether to claim or to disown it.
雷德曼瞪着眼睛，脸绷得紧紧的，不知道是认领还是放弃。
“The game’s up, Ryder,” said Holmes quietly.
“游戏结束了，雷德曼。”说时，霍尔姆斯平静地说道。
“Hold up, man, or you’ll be into the fire!
“站住，小子，否则你会掉进火里的！
Give him an arm back into his chair, Watson.
给他一个胳膊回到他的椅子上，华生。
He’s not got blood enough to go in for felony with impunity.
他没有足够的血去犯下罪行而无惧。
Give him a dash of brandy.
给他一杯杜松子酒。
So!
好了！
Now he looks a little more human.
现在他看起来有些像人了。
What a shrimp it is, to be sure!”
真是个小虾！”
For a moment he had staggered and nearly fallen, but the brandy brought a tinge of colour into his cheeks, and he sat staring with frightened eyes at his accuser.
他一时之间踉踉跄跄地跌倒，差点儿摔下，但杜松子酒使他的脸颊泛起了一点红晕，他呆呆地瞪着眼睛看着他的指控者。
“I have almost every link in my hands, and all the proofs which I could possibly need, so there is little which you need tell me.
我手里几乎都有了，所有的证明我也需要，所以你不需要告诉我太多。
Still, that little may as well be cleared up to make the case complete.
但那点小事情也最好弄清楚，以便整个案件完美无缺。
You had heard, Ryder, of this blue stone of the Countess of Morcar’s?”
雷德，你听说过这个摩卡罗公爵的蓝色宝石吗？
“It was Catherine Cusack who told me of it,” said he in a crackling voice.
他说：“是的，是凯瑟琳·库斯克告诉我的。”
“I see—her ladyship’s waiting-maid.
“我看到——她的女仆。
Well, the temptation of sudden wealth so easily acquired was too much for you, as it has been for better men before you; but you were not very scrupulous in the means you used.
哦，诱惑突然获得的财富太容易了，你也不例外，以前的那些人也一样；但你对手段的谨慎不够。
It seems to me, Ryder, that there is the making of a very pretty villain in you.
雷德，我觉得你身上有一种很漂亮的坏蛋。
You knew that this man Horner, the plumber, had been concerned in some such matter before, and that suspicion would rest the more readily upon him.
你知道这个叫霍恩的水管工以前曾经干过什么，而且这种怀疑会更轻易地落在他身上。
What did you do, then?
你做了什么？
You made some small job in my lady’s room—you and your confederate Cusack—and you managed that he should be the man sent for.
你做了些小工活儿，在我的房间里，你和你的同伙库斯克，然后你让他被派去。
Then, when he had left, you rifled the jewel-case, raised the alarm, and had this unfortunate man arrested.
等他离开后，你翻了珠宝盒，引起了警报，把这个不幸的人逮捕了。
You then—”
你然后——
Ryder threw himself down suddenly upon the rug and clutched at my companion’s knees.
雷德突然倒在地毯上，抓住我的同伴膝盖。
“For God’s sake, have mercy!” he shrieked.
“求求你，可怜我吧！”他尖叫道。
“Think of my father!
“想想我的父亲！”
Of my mother!
关于我的母亲！
It would break their hearts.
它会伤透他们的心。
I never went wrong before!
我从来没错过！
I never will again.
我再也不会错了。
I swear it.
我发誓。
I’ll swear it on a Bible.
我会在圣经上发誓。
Oh, don’t bring it into court!
哦，别把这事带到法庭！
For Christ’s sake, don’t!”
真的，别了！
“Get back into your chair!” said Holmes sternly.
“回到你的椅子上！”斯普林顿严厉地说。
“It is very well to cringe and crawl now, but you thought little enough of this poor Horner in the dock for a crime of which he knew nothing.”
“现在你蜷缩、匍匐的样子很好，但你对这个可怜的霍恩纳在法庭上所犯的罪行所知甚少。”
“I will fly, Mr. Holmes.
“我会飞，先生。
I will leave the country, sir.
我要离开这个国家，先生。
Then the charge against him will break down.”
那么，对他的指控就会瓦解。”
“Hum!
We will talk about that.
我们再谈。
And now let us hear a true account of the next act.
现在，让我们听一听下一个场景的实情。
How came the stone into the goose, and how came the goose into the open market?
石头怎么会掉进鹅的嘴里，鹅又怎么会出现在公开的市场？
Tell us the truth, for there lies your only hope of safety.”
告诉我们实情吧，因为这正是你唯一的生还希望。
Ryder passed his tongue over his parched lips.
雷德利用舌头舔舔干裂的嘴唇。
“I will tell you it just as it happened, sir,” said he.
“我会告诉你，就是按照我所经历的，先生，”他说。

“When Horner had been arrested, it seemed to me that it would be best for me to get away with the stone at once, for I did not know at what moment the police might not take it into their heads to search me and my room.
“当霍恩被逮捕的时候，我觉得最好是我立刻离开酒店，把石头带走，因为我不知道警察什么时候可能不会想到搜查我房间和我的房间。
There was no place about the hotel where it would be safe.
酒店里没有一个地方是安全的。
I went out, as if on some commission, and I made for my sister’s house.
我出去，好像有某种委托似的，我走向我姐姐的家。
She had married a man named Oakshott, and lived in Brixton Road, where she fattened fowls for the market.
她嫁给了一名叫奥克肖特的人，住在布里顿路，她养鸡以供市场出售。
All the way there every man I met seemed to me to be a policeman or a detective; and, for all that it was a cold night, the sweat was pouring down my face before I came to the Brixton Road.
路上，我遇见的每一个人都像是警察或侦探；即使是在一个寒冷的晚上，我脸上的汗水还是在来到布里顿路之前就流了下来。
My sister asked me what was the matter, and why I was so pale; but I told her that I had been upset by the jewel robbery at the hotel.
我姐姐问我有什么事情，为什么脸色苍白；但我告诉她，我被酒店的珠宝盗窃事件所困扰。
Then I went into the back yard and smoked a pipe and wondered what it would be best to do.
然后我走进后院，抽了一根烟，想做什么才好。
“I had a friend once called Maudsley, who went to the bad, and has just been serving his time in Pentonville.
“我曾经有一个朋友叫慕斯莱，他去做了坏事，现在正在皮特尼维监狱服刑。
One day he had met me, and fell into talk about the ways of thieves, and how they could get rid of what they stole.
有一天，他遇见了我，和我谈了关于贼的手段，如何可以摆脱所偷的东西。
I knew that he would be true to me, for I knew one or two things about him; so I made up my mind to go right on to Kilburn, where he lived, and take him into my confidence.
我知道他会对我诚实，因为我知道一些关于他的事情；所以我决定去到凯尔文，他住在那儿，把他的事情告诉给他。
He would show me how to turn the stone into money.
他教我如何把石头变成钱。
But how to get to him in safety?
但如何安全地找到他？
I thought of the agonies I had gone through in coming from the hotel.
我想到从旅馆出来时的痛苦。
I might at any moment be seized and searched, and there would be the stone in my waistcoat pocket.
我随时可能被抓住并搜身，腰带口袋里有石头。

I was leaning against the wall at the time and looking at the geese which were waddling about round my feet, and suddenly an idea came into my head which showed me how I could beat the best detective that ever lived.
我靠着墙，看着脚边踱步的鹅，突然间脑袋里闪过一个想法，让我知道如何打败世上最好的侦探。
“My sister had told me some weeks before that I might have the pick of her geese for a Christmas present, and I knew that she was always as good as her word.
“我姐姐几个月前告诉我，我可以选她家的鹅作为圣诞礼物，我知道她总是说到做到。
I would take my goose now, and in it I would carry my stone to Kilburn.
我现在要拿我的鹅，把石头藏在凯尔布伦。
There was a little shed in the yard, and behind this I drove one of the birds—a fine big one, white, with a barred tail.
厅里有一间小棚子，我用一只鹅把石头藏在棚子后面。
I caught it, and prying its bill open, I thrust the stone down its throat as far as my finger could reach.
我捉住它，把它的嘴打开，把石头塞进它的喉咙，直到我的手指能伸到为止。
The bird gave a gulp, and I felt the stone pass along its gullet and down into its crop.
鸭子吞咽了，我感觉石头从它的食道滑到它的胃里。
But the creature flapped and struggled, and out came my sister to know what was the matter.
但这个家伙拍打挣扎，我姐姐过来知道怎么回事。
As I turned to speak to her the brute broke loose and fluttered off among the others.
我转身对她说，那家伙挣脱了，飞走了。
“‘Whatever were you doing with that bird, Jem?’ says she.
“‘你做了什么，杰姆？’她问。
“‘Well,’ said I, ‘you said you’d give me one for Christmas, and I was feeling which was the fattest.’
“‘嗯，’我说，‘你说了你会给我一只鹅作为圣诞礼物，我感觉哪只是最肥的。’
“‘Oh,’ says she, ‘we’ve set yours aside for you—Jem’s bird, we call it.
“‘哦，’她说，‘我们已经把你的鹅放在你那里的——杰姆的鹅，我们叫它。’
It’s the big white one over yonder.
远处有一只白色的。
There’s twenty-six of them, which makes one for you, and one for us, and two dozen for the market.’
有二十六个，正好一个给你，一个给我们，还有两打市场用的。
“‘Thank you, Maggie,’ says I; ‘but if it is all the same to you, I’d rather have that one I was handling just now.’
“‘谢谢你，玛吉，’我说，‘不过如果你觉得无所谓，我更愿意现在这个我正在处理的那只。’
“‘The other is a good three pound heavier,’ said she, ‘and we fattened it expressly for you.’
“‘另一只重三磅多，’她说，‘我们特意为它喂肥了。’
“‘Never mind.
“‘没关系。
I’ll have the other, and I’ll take it now,’ said I.
我要另一只，现在就拿走，’我说。
“‘Oh, just as you like,’ said she, a little huffed.
“‘哦，随你便，’她说，有点生气。
‘Which is it you want, then?’
‘你想要哪一只呢？’
“‘That white one with the barred tail, right in the middle of the flock.’
“‘那只有条带尾巴的白色的一只，正中间的那只。’
“‘Oh, very well.
“‘哦，好吧。
Kill it and take it with you.’
杀了它，带回去。’
“Well, I did what she said, Mr. Holmes, and I carried the bird all the way to Kilburn.
“好吧，先生，像你说的那样办，我把它一路带到金伯林。
I told my pal what I had done, for he was a man that it was easy to tell a thing like that to.
我把事情告诉了我朋友，因为他是很容易看出那种事的。
He laughed until he choked, and we got a knife and opened the goose.
他笑得喘不过气来，我们拿刀打开鹅。
My heart turned to water, for there was no sign of the stone, and I knew that some terrible mistake had occurred.
我的心像水一样凉了，因为没有石头的痕迹，我知道发生了可怕的错误。
I left the bird, rushed back to my sister’s, and hurried into the back yard.
我把鸟放了，急匆匆回到姐姐家，又急急忙忙跑到后院。
There was not a bird to be seen there.
那里根本就没有鸟。
“‘Where are they all, Maggie?’
“‘它们都去哪儿了， Maggie？’
I cried.
我哭了起来。
“‘Gone to the dealer’s, Jem.’
“‘都去卖鸟的了， Jem。’
“‘Which dealer’s?’
“‘哪一家的？’
“‘Breckinridge, of Covent Garden.’
“‘布莱克林，牛津街上的。’
“‘But was there another with a barred tail?’
“‘可是，有尾巴上带钩的吗？’
I asked, ‘the same as the one I chose?’
我问道：“那两个尾巴上带钩的，我怎么分得清呢？’
“‘Yes, Jem; there were two barred-tailed ones, and I could never tell them apart.’
“‘是的， Jem，有两个尾巴上带钩的，我从来也分不清。’

“Well, then, of course I saw it all, and I ran off as hard as my feet would carry me to this man Breckinridge; but he had sold the lot at once, and not one word would he tell me as to where they had gone.
“那么，当然我全看见了，我跑得像我的脚能带我多远就跑多远，跑到布莱克林先生那里去了，可是他立刻就把那批卖掉了，而且不说一个字告诉我它们去了哪里。
You heard him yourselves to-night.
你们自己也听到了。
Well, he has always answered me like that.
哦，他总是这样回答我的。
My sister thinks that I am going mad.
我姐姐认为我精神失常。
Sometimes I think that I am myself.
有时我觉得我自己。
And now—and now I am myself a branded thief, without ever having touched the wealth for which I sold my character.
现在——现在我是一个被标记的窃贼，从未拿过一分钱，只为卖了我的名声。
God help me!
神啊，求你帮助我！
God help me!”
神啊，求你帮助我！
He burst into convulsive sobbing, with his face buried in his hands.
他突然抽泣起来，双手捂着脸。
There was a long silence, broken only by his heavy breathing and by the measured tapping of Sherlock Holmes’ finger-tips upon the edge of the table.
那里有一阵长时间的沉默，只有他沉重的呼吸声和小指头在桌子边缘轻轻敲击的声音。
Then my friend rose and threw open the door.
然后我的朋友站起身，把门打开。
“Get out!” said he.
“出去！”他说。
“What, sir!
“什么，先生！”
Oh, Heaven bless you!”
哦，天啊！
“No more words.
“再无言语。
Get out!”
请出去！”
And no more words were needed.
再无言语是必要的。
There was a rush, a clatter upon the stairs, the bang of a door, and the crisp rattle of running footfalls from the street.
一阵急促的脚步声，门的砰的一声，还有从街上跑来的脚步的清脆的响声。
“After all, Watson,” said Holmes, reaching up his hand for his clay pipe, “I am not retained by the police to supply their deficiencies.
“无论如何，沃森先生，”说霍尔姆斯先生，伸手拿起了他的烟管， “我不是被警察雇来提供他们的不足。
If Horner were in danger it would be another thing; but this fellow will not appear against him, and the case must collapse.
如果霍尔姆斯先生处于危险之中，那另当别论；但是这个家伙不会来对付霍尔姆斯先生，而且这个案子必然要失败。
I suppose that I am commuting a felony, but it is just possible that I am saving a soul.
我以为我正犯下重罪，但也许我是在拯救灵魂。
This fellow will not go wrong again; he is too terribly frightened.
这个人不会再次犯错；他太害怕了。
Send him to gaol now, and you make him a gaol-bird for life.
现在把他送到监狱，你就让他成为终身的囚鸟。
Besides, it is the season of forgiveness.
除此之外，这是感恩的季节。
Chance has put in our way a most singular and whimsical problem, and its solution is its own reward.
遇到我们身前的奇奇怪怪的问题，它的解决就是它的奖赏。
If you will have the goodness to touch the bell, Doctor, we will begin another investigation, in which, also a bird will be the chief feature.”
如果你愿意轻轻按一下铃，医生，我们将开始一个新的调查，其中，鸟将成为主要特征。”

ch.et: VIII. The Adventure of the Speckled Band
ch.zt: 第八篇 · 花斑带探案
p: On glancing over my notes of the seventy odd cases in which I have during the last eight years studied the methods of my friend Sherlock Holmes, I find many tragic, some comic, a large number merely strange, but none commonplace; for, working as he did rather for the love of his art than for the acquirement of wealth, he refused to associate himself with any investigation which did not tend towards the unusual, and even the fantastic.
在翻阅我近八年来研究的七十多个案件笔记时，我发现其中许多案件是悲剧性的，有些是喜剧性的，有些则显得奇异，但没有一个案件是平凡的。因为，他研究艺术而不是追求财富，他拒绝与任何不趋向奇异或奇幻的调查结盟，即使那些调查是荒诞的。
Of all these varied cases, however, I cannot recall any which presented more singular features than that which was associated with the well-known Surrey family of the Roylotts of Stoke Moran.
从这些各种各样的案件中，我却无法回忆起任何具有更奇异特征的案件，那与著名的索谢家族的罗伊洛特家族有关。
The events in question occurred in the early days of my association with Holmes, when we were sharing rooms as bachelors in Baker Street.
这些事件发生在我和霍尔姆斯结识的早期，那时我们住在贝克街的单身汉房子里。

It is possible that I might have placed them upon record before, but a promise of secrecy was made at the time, from which I have only been freed during the last month by the untimely death of the lady to whom the pledge was given.
我或许在某个时候已经记录过这些事实，但当时有一个保密的承诺，我是在一个月前被解除的，因为那位承诺人去世了。

It is perhaps as well that the facts should now come to light, for I have reasons to know that there are widespread rumours as to the death of Dr. Grimesby Roylott which tend to make the matter even more terrible than the truth.
现在事实终于公之于众，因为我知道，关于格里米斯·罗伊洛特医生的死亡的谣言，使得事情更加可怕。
It was early in April in the year ’83 that I woke one morning to find Sherlock Holmes standing, fully dressed, by the side of my bed.
在1833年四月早些时候，我醒来时发现，霍尔姆斯先生正穿着整齐地站在我的床边。

He was a late riser, as a rule, and as the clock on the mantelpiece showed me that it was only a quarter-past seven, I blinked up at him in some surprise, and perhaps just a little resentment, for I was myself regular in my habits.
他通常是个晚起的人，钟表显示现在是七点半，我眨了眨眼，有些惊讶，也许还有一点儿怨恨，因为我自己习惯于早起。
“Very sorry to knock you up, Watson,” said he, “but it’s the common lot this morning.
“很抱歉让你惊醒了，沃森先生，”他说，“但这是今天早上很常见的事。”
Mrs. Hudson has been knocked up, she retorted upon me, and I on you.”
莱佛太太被惊醒了，她反驳说：“你被惊醒了，我被你惊醒了。”
“What is it, then—a fire?”
“这是什么——起火？”
“No; a client.
“不；一个客户。
It seems that a young lady has arrived in a considerable state of excitement, who insists upon seeing me.
似乎一个年轻女士到了这个早上，带着极大的激动，要求见我。
She is waiting now in the sitting-room.
她现在正在客厅里等待。

Now, when young ladies wander about the metropolis at this hour of the morning, and knock sleepy people up out of their beds, I presume that it is something very pressing which they have to communicate.
当年轻女士在凌晨这个时间四处游荡，敲醒睡着的人，我推测，他们一定有什么非常紧急的事情要传达。
Should it prove to be an interesting case, you would, I am sure, wish to follow it from the outset.
如果这成为有趣的一案，你一定会希望从一开始就跟随它。
I thought, at any rate, that I should call you and give you the chance.”
我认为，至少我应该给你打电话，给你机会。
“My dear fellow, I would not miss it for anything.”
“亲爱的兄弟，我不会错过任何事情的。”

I had no keener pleasure than in following Holmes in his professional investigations, and in admiring the rapid deductions, as swift as intuitions, and yet always founded on a logical basis with which he unravelled the problems which were submitted to him.
我在跟随霍尔姆斯进行专业调查时，感到最愉快的莫过于，欣赏他快速的推论，这些推论就像直觉一样迅速，但又始终建立在逻辑的基础上，从而解开他被提交给他的问题。
I rapidly threw on my clothes and was ready in a few minutes to accompany my friend down to the sitting-room.
我迅速穿上衣服，几分钟后，我准备好陪我的朋友下到客厅。
A lady dressed in black and heavily veiled, who had been sitting in the window, rose as we entered.
一位穿着黑色衣服，戴着沉重的面纱的女士，坐在窗口旁，一进屋就站了起来。
“Good-morning, madam,” said Holmes cheerily.
“早上好，夫人。”霍尔姆斯愉快地说。
“My name is Sherlock Holmes.
“我的名字是夏洛克·霍尔姆斯。”
This is my intimate friend and associate, Dr. Watson, before whom you can speak as freely as before myself.
这是我的亲密朋友和同事，我的医生沃森，在他面前你可以像在面对我时一样自由地讲话。
Ha!
哈！
I am glad to see that Mrs. Hudson has had the good sense to light the fire.
我很高兴看到，夫人霍尔姆斯已经明智地点火。
Pray draw up to it, and I shall order you a cup of hot coffee, for I observe that you are shivering.”
好的，请您坐到火炉旁，我将为您端一杯热咖啡，因为我注意到您在发抖。
“It is not cold which makes me shiver,” said the woman in a low voice, changing her seat as requested.
“它并不冷才让我发抖。”女士低声说，按照要求换了个座位。
“What, then?”
“那么，是吗？”
“It is fear, Mr. Holmes.
“是恐惧，先生霍尔姆斯。”
It is terror.”
“是恐怖。”
She raised her veil as she spoke, and we could see that she was indeed in a pitiable state of agitation, her face all drawn and grey, with restless frightened eyes, like those of some hunted animal.
她一边说话，一边举起面纱，我们看得出她确实处于极度不安的状态，脸色憔悴，眼眸里充满了惊恐，就像猎物般的眼睛。
Her features and figure were those of a woman of thirty, but her hair was shot with premature grey, and her expression was weary and haggard.
她的容貌和身材都像是三十岁的女人，但头发上却染上了早生的白发，表情疲惫憔悴。
Sherlock Holmes ran her over with one of his quick, all-comprehensive glances.
森林霍尔姆先生用他那敏捷而全面的目光扫过她。
“You must not fear,” said he soothingly, bending forward and patting her forearm.
“你不必害怕，”他温和地说，弯下身子，轻抚她的手臂。
“We shall soon set matters right, I have no doubt.
“我们很快就会把事情处理好，我肯定。”
You have come in by train this morning, I see.”
你今天是坐火车来的，我看出来了。”
“You know me, then?”
“你认识我吗？”
“No, but I observe the second half of a return ticket in the palm of your left glove.
“不，但我注意到你左手手套上有一张返程车票。”
You must have started early, and yet you had a good drive in a dog-cart, along heavy roads, before you reached the station.”
你一定是早早就出发了，而且在狗车上的驾驶座上坐了很长时间，经过了重路，才到达车站。”
The lady gave a violent start and stared in bewilderment at my companion.
女人猛地一惊，瞪大眼睛，看着我的同伴。
“There is no mystery, my dear madam,” said he, smiling.
“没有什么秘密，亲爱的女士，”他笑着说。
“The left arm of your jacket is spattered with mud in no less than seven places.
“你的左袖上沾满了泥，至少有七处。”
The marks are perfectly fresh.
标记非常新鲜。
There is no vehicle save a dog-cart which throws up mud in that way, and then only when you sit on the left-hand side of the driver.”
只有狗车才能在那样方式上溅泥，而且只有在驾驶座的左侧。”
“Whatever your reasons may be, you are perfectly correct,” said she.
“无论你的理由是什么，你完全正确。”她说。
“I started from home before six, reached Leatherhead at twenty past, and came in by the first train to Waterloo.
我从家出发早六点，到勒沃库姆二十分钟后，坐第一班火车到沃伦敦。
Sir, I can stand this strain no longer; I shall go mad if it continues.
老爷，我再也受不了这种折磨了；如果继续下去，我恐怕会发疯。
I have no one to turn to—none, save only one, who cares for me, and he, poor fellow, can be of little aid.
我没有可以依靠的人——除了只有一个，他对我关心，他，可怜的人，对我的帮助很小。
I have heard of you, Mr. Holmes; I have heard of you from Mrs. Farintosh, whom you helped in the hour of her sore need.
我听说过你，先生；我从福斯蒂安夫人那里听说过你，她帮助过你，是在你最需要的时候。
It was from her that I had your address.
是她给了我地址。
Oh, sir, do you not think that you could help me, too, and at least throw a little light through the dense darkness which surrounds me?
哦，先生，你难道不认为你也需要帮助，至少能给我一点光亮，穿过笼罩我的黑暗的浓雾吗？

At present it is out of my power to reward you for your services, but in a month or six weeks I shall be married, with the control of my own income, and then at least you shall not find me ungrateful.”
目前，我无法对你表示感谢，但我一个月或六周后，我将结婚，拥有自己的收入，那时至少你不会觉得我对你不感激。
Holmes turned to his desk and, unlocking it, drew out a small case-book, which he consulted.
海默斯转到他的办公桌前，打开抽屉，取出一个小本子，翻阅起来。
“Farintosh,” said he.
“福斯蒂安夫人。”他说。
“Ah yes, I recall the case; it was concerned with an opal tiara.
“啊，是的，我记得那桩案子；它涉及一颗珍珠耳坠。
I think it was before your time, Watson.
我认为是你的时代之前，沃森先生。
I can only say, madam, that I shall be happy to devote the same care to your case as I did to that of your friend.
我只能说，女士，我愿意像我帮助你朋友那样，对你的案子同样给予关注。
As to reward, my profession is its own reward; but you are at liberty to defray whatever expenses I may be put to, at the time which suits you best.
关于报酬，我的职业就是它的报酬；但你自由地为我支付任何费用，以你认为方便的时间。
And now I beg that you will lay before us everything that may help us in forming an opinion upon the matter.”
现在，我请求你把一切可能帮助我们形成对这件事看法的东西，都告诉我们。

“Alas!” replied our visitor, “the very horror of my situation lies in the fact that my fears are so vague, and my suspicions depend so entirely upon small points, which might seem trivial to another, that even he to whom of all others I have a right to look for help and advice looks upon all that I tell him about it as the fancies of a nervous woman.
“真遗憾！”我们的访客说，“我处境的恐怖在于，我的恐惧是那么模糊，我的怀疑完全依赖于微小的点，这些点对另一个来说可能显得微不足道，但对我来说，他对我来说，就像一个神经质的女人的幻想。
He does not say so, but I can read it from his soothing answers and averted eyes.
他没有说，但从他温和的回答和回避的眼神中，我能读出这一点。
But I have heard, Mr. Holmes, that you can see deeply into the manifold wickedness of the human heart.
但是，我先生，您能看见人类心灵的种种邪恶。
You may advise me how to walk amid the dangers which encompass me.”
您可以建议我如何在围绕我的危险中行走。
“I am all attention, madam.”
“我全神贯注，夫人。”
“My name is Helen Stoner, and I am living with my stepfather, who is the last survivor of one of the oldest Saxon families in England, the Roylotts of Stoke Moran, on the western border of Surrey.”
“我的名字是海伦·斯托特，我与我的继父同住，他是英格兰最古老Saxon家族罗伊尔特家族的最后一位成员，罗伊尔特家族的斯托顿家族，在萨里郡西部的边境。”
Holmes nodded his head.
森德罗姆先生点点头。
“The name is familiar to me,” said he.
“这个名字对我来说很熟悉，”他说道。
“The family was at one time among the richest in England, and the estates extended over the borders into Berkshire in the north, and Hampshire in the west.
“这个家族曾经是英格兰最富有的，土地延伸到伯克郡的北部，赫斯特的西部。
In the last century, however, four successive heirs were of a dissolute and wasteful disposition, and the family ruin was eventually completed by a gambler in the days of the Regency.
在上个世纪，然而，四次继承人都是放荡和挥霍的，家族的衰败最终是通过一个在维多利亚时代的赌徒完成的。
Nothing was left save a few acres of ground, and the two-hundred-year-old house, which is itself crushed under a heavy mortgage.
除了几块土地和两百年的老房子，什么都没有剩下，房子被沉重的抵押贷款压垮。

The last squire dragged out his existence there, living the horrible life of an aristocratic pauper; but his only son, my stepfather, seeing that he must adapt himself to the new conditions, obtained an advance from a relative, which enabled him to take a medical degree and went out to Calcutta, where, by his professional skill and his force of character, he established a large practice.
最后一个继承人拖着他的存在在那里度过，过着贵族的悲惨生活；但是他的唯一儿子，我的继父，看到他必须适应新的条件，从一个亲戚那里获得了贷款，这使他能够获得医学学位，并去加尔各答，凭借他的专业技能和毅力，他在那里建立了一个大型的诊所。
In a fit of anger, however, caused by some robberies which had been perpetrated in the house, he beat his native butler to death and narrowly escaped a capital sentence.
由于一次愤怒，由于在房子内发生的抢劫，他把他的原生仆人打死，差点被判处死刑。
As it was, he suffered a long term of imprisonment and afterwards returned to England a morose and disappointed man.
由于这，他遭受了一段长期的监禁，后来他回到英国，变得沮丧和失望。
“When Dr. Roylott was in India he married my mother, Mrs. Stoner, the young widow of Major-General Stoner, of the Bengal Artillery.
“当罗伊尔特医生在印度时，他娶了我的母亲，海伦·斯托特，是芒斯特的年轻寡妇，芒斯特的芒斯特，是孟加拉炮兵的少将。”
My sister Julia and I were twins, and we were only two years old at the time of my mother’s re-marriage.
我的妹妹朱莉娅和我都是双胞胎，我们是在我母亲再婚时两岁大的。

She had a considerable sum of money—not less than £ 1000 a year—and this she bequeathed to Dr. Roylott entirely while we resided with him, with a provision that a certain annual sum should be allowed to each of us in the event of our marriage.
她有一笔相当可观的财产——每年不少于1000英镑——她将全部留给罗伊尔特医生，我们居住在他家时，有规定每年给我们各一人提供一定的款项，以备我们结婚时使用。
Shortly after our return to England my mother died—she was killed eight years ago in a railway accident near Crewe.
我母亲去世——她是在八年前在克里夫车站的一次铁路事故中被杀的。
Dr. Roylott then abandoned his attempts to establish himself in practice in London and took us to live with him in the old ancestral house at Stoke Moran.
罗伊尔特医生于是放弃了在伦敦开设行医的打算，将我们带回到他老家斯托克摩尔。
The money which my mother had left was enough for all our wants, and there seemed to be no obstacle to our happiness.
我母亲留下的钱足够我们所有需要，似乎没有阻碍我们的幸福。
“But a terrible change came over our stepfather about this time.
“但这次我们父亲变得非常可怕。

Instead of making friends and exchanging visits with our neighbours, who had at first been overjoyed to see a Roylott of Stoke Moran back in the old family seat, he shut himself up in his house and seldom came out save to indulge in ferocious quarrels with whoever might cross his path.
他不再像以前那样与邻居们交朋友，也不再像以前那样与邻居们交换拜访，而是把自己关在房子里，很少出来，只是偶尔因为愤怒而与谁争吵。
Violence of temper approaching to mania has been hereditary in the men of the family, and in my stepfather’s case it had, I believe, been intensified by his long residence in the tropics.
他暴躁的性格已经遗传于家族中，特别是我父亲的情况，我认为他长期居住在热带地区，他的性格变得更加暴躁。

A series of disgraceful brawls took place, two of which ended in the police-court, until at last he became the terror of the village, and the folks would fly at his approach, for he is a man of immense strength, and absolutely uncontrollable in his anger.
一系列令人震惊的斗殴事件发生，两起斗殴事件最终被送进法庭，直到最后他成为整个村庄的恐怖，人们会躲避他的到来，因为他是一个非常强壮的人，而且非常暴躁。
“Last week he hurled the local blacksmith over a parapet into a stream, and it was only by paying over all the money which I could gather together that I was able to avert another public exposure.
“上个星期他把当地铁匠从栏杆上扔了下去，幸好我能够收集到所有我能够聚集起来的钱，才避免了又一次的公开曝光。

He had no friends at all save the wandering gipsies, and he would give these vagabonds leave to encamp upon the few acres of bramble-covered land which represent the family estate, and would accept in return the hospitality of their tents, wandering away with them sometimes for weeks on end.
他没有朋友，除了流浪的吉普赛人，他会在荒芜的灌木丛土地上让这些流浪汉安营扎寨，接受他们的帐篷的招待，有时会离开他们好几周。

He has a passion also for Indian animals, which are sent over to him by a correspondent, and he has at this moment a cheetah and a baboon, which wander freely over his grounds and are feared by the villagers almost as much as their master.
他还有对印度动物的痴迷，这些动物是通过一个通讯员寄来的，他现在正在养着一只猎豹和一只狒狒，它们在地里自由自在地游荡，被村民几乎像主人一样害怕。
“You can imagine from what I say that my poor sister Julia and I had no great pleasure in our lives.
“你可以想象从我说的话中，我的可怜的姐姐朱莉和我并没有过什么快乐的生活。
No servant would stay with us, and for a long time we did all the work of the house.
没有仆人愿意留下来，我们所有的工作都是由我们自己完成的。
She was but thirty at the time of her death, and yet her hair had already begun to whiten, even as mine has.”
她死的时候只有三十岁，但她的头发已经开始变白，就像我的头发一样。
“Your sister is dead, then?”
“你的姐姐死了，是吗？”
“She died just two years ago, and it is of her death that I wish to speak to you.
她两年前去世了，我来见你，是想说她死的事。
You can understand that, living the life which I have described, we were little likely to see anyone of our own age and position.
你明白的，我们活在描述过的那种生活里，很难遇到同龄同地位的人。
We had, however, an aunt, my mother’s maiden sister, Miss Honoria Westphail, who lives near Harrow, and we were occasionally allowed to pay short visits at this lady’s house.
然而，我们有个阿姨，我母亲的表妹，西普菲尔小姐，住在哈罗附近，我们偶尔会被允许去她家短暂停留。
Julia went there at Christmas two years ago, and met there a half-pay major of marines, to whom she became engaged.
好像在去年圣诞节，朱莉娅去了那里，遇见了在那里见的半薪海军上校，两人结了婚。

My stepfather learned of the engagement when my sister returned and offered no objection to the marriage; but within a fortnight of the day which had been fixed for the wedding, the terrible event occurred which has deprived me of my only companion.”
我的继父知道这个婚事，当我的妹妹回来时，没有反对，但婚礼的那天，婚礼的那天，婚礼的那天，发生了可怕的事情，我唯一的伴侣就消失了。
Sherlock Holmes had been leaning back in his chair with his eyes closed and his head sunk in a cushion, but he half opened his lids now and glanced across at his visitor.
科尔森霍尔摩斯正靠在椅子上，闭上眼睛，头枕在软垫上，但这时他半睁着眼睛，瞥了一眼他的访客。
“Pray be precise as to details,” said he.
“请详细说明。”他说。
“It is easy for me to be so, for every event of that dreadful time is seared into my memory.
我能这么详细，因为我对那个可怕的时期的所有事件都记忆犹新。
The manor-house is, as I have already said, very old, and only one wing is now inhabited.
这座庄园，我已经说过了，非常古老，现在只住一个翼。
The bedrooms in this wing are on the ground floor, the sitting-rooms being in the central block of the buildings.
这座庄园的卧室在底层，客厅在建筑物的中央部分。
Of these bedrooms the first is Dr. Roylott’s, the second my sister’s, and the third my own.
这三间卧室，第一间是罗伊洛特医生的，第二间是我的妹妹的，第三间是我的。
There is no communication between them, but they all open out into the same corridor.
这三间卧室之间没有沟通，但它们都通向同一个走廊。
Do I make myself plain?”
我说得清楚吗？”
“Perfectly so.”
“完全清楚。”
“The windows of the three rooms open out upon the lawn.
“三间卧室的窗户都朝草坪开。

That fatal night Dr. Roylott had gone to his room early, though we knew that he had not retired to rest, for my sister was troubled by the smell of the strong Indian cigars which it was his custom to smoke.
那个致命的夜晚，罗伊尔特医生早早地去了他的房间，尽管我们知道他并没有真正休息，因为我的妹妹被他吸烟时散发出的强烈印度雪茄的气味所困扰。
She left her room, therefore, and came into mine, where she sat for some time, chatting about her approaching wedding.
她离开房间，来到我的房间，坐在那里聊天，谈论着她的婚礼。
At eleven o’clock she rose to leave me, but she paused at the door and looked back.
在十一点的时候，她起身离开，但她在门口停留了一下，回头看了看。
“‘Tell me, Helen,’ said she, ‘have you ever heard anyone whistle in the dead of the night?’
“‘告诉我，海伦，’她说，‘你是否曾经听到过有人在深夜里吹口哨？’
“‘Never,’ said I.
“‘没有，’我说。
“‘I suppose that you could not possibly whistle, yourself, in your sleep?’
“‘我猜你不可能在梦中吹口哨，对吧？’
“‘Certainly not.
“‘当然不会。
But why?’
但为什么？’
“‘Because during the last few nights I have always, about three in the morning, heard a low, clear whistle.
“‘因为最近的几个晚上，我大约在凌晨三点的时候，总是听到一个低沉、清晰的口哨声。
I am a light sleeper, and it has awakened me.
我是一个轻度的失眠者，它把我唤醒了。
I cannot tell where it came from—perhaps from the next room, perhaps from the lawn.
我不知道它来自哪里——可能是隔壁房间，可能是草坪。
I thought that I would just ask you whether you had heard it.’
我想只是问问你，你是否听到过它。
“‘No, I have not.
“‘没有，我从来没有。
It must be those wretched gipsies in the plantation.’

“You must confine yourself to your room, on pretence of a headache, when your stepfather comes back.
你必须把自己关在房间里，借口头痛，当你那继父回来的时候。

Then when you hear him retire for the night, you must open the shutters of your window, undo the hasp, put your lamp there as a signal to us, and then withdraw quietly with everything which you are likely to want into the room which you used to occupy.
然后你听到你那继父上床睡觉的时候，必须打开你窗子的窗帘，解开窗闩，把你的灯放在那里作为我们那儿的信号，然后悄悄地把你可能要用的一切东西都带进你以前住过的那个房间去。
I have no doubt that, in spite of the repairs, you could manage there for one night.”
我相信，尽管修缮了，你仍然可以在那里过一夜。
“Oh, yes, easily.”
哦，是的，很容易。
“The rest you will leave in our hands.”
你其余的就交给我们了。
“But what will you do?”
但你将怎么办？
