“We shall spend the night in your room, and we shall investigate the cause of this noise which has disturbed you.”
我们将住在你的房间过夜，并调查打扰你的这种噪音的原因。
“I believe, Mr. Holmes, that you have already made up your mind,” said Miss Stoner, laying her hand upon my companion’s sleeve.
史宁儿說道：“霍金斯先生，我想你已經打定了主意了，”她輕輕撫摸著我同伴的袖子。
“Perhaps I have.”
“Then, for pity’s sake, tell me what was the cause of my sister’s death.”
然后，求求你，告诉我妹妹死亡的原因。
“I should prefer to have clearer proofs before I speak.”
我倒希望有了更明确的证据再来说话。
“You can at least tell me whether my own thought is correct, and if she died from some sudden fright.”
你可以至少告诉我我的想法是否正确，而且她是否死于某种突然的惊吓。
“No, I do not think so.
不，我不这样认为。
I think that there was probably some more tangible cause.
我认为可能有一个更直接的原因。
And now, Miss Stoner, we must leave you for if Dr. Roylott returned and saw us our journey would be in vain.
而现在，索纳小姐，我们必须离开你，否则若罗伊洛特医生回来看见我们，我们的旅程就会白费。
Good-bye, and be brave, for if you will do what I have told you, you may rest assured that we shall soon drive away the dangers that threaten you.”
Sherlock Holmes and I had no difficulty in engaging a bedroom and sitting-room at the Crown Inn.
夏洛克·福尔摩斯和我毫不费力地在皇冠客栈租到了一间卧室和一间起居室。
They were on the upper floor, and from our window we could command a view of the avenue gate, and of the inhabited wing of Stoke Moran Manor House.
他们住在楼上，从我们的窗口可以看到 avenue gate，以及斯科特·摩根 Manor House 的 inhabited 翼。
At dusk we saw Dr. Grimesby Roylott drive past, his huge form looming up beside the little figure of the lad who drove him.
黄昏时，我们看见格雷姆斯比·罗伊洛特医生驾车经过，他巨大的身影矗立在小车少年身边。
The boy had some slight difficulty in undoing the heavy iron gates, and we heard the hoarse roar of the Doctor’s voice and saw the fury with which he shook his clinched fists at him.
那少年解开沉重的铁门时有些轻微的困难，我们听到了医生嘶哑的声音，看见他愤怒地摇着紧握的拳头朝他打去。
The trap drove on, and a few minutes later we saw a sudden light spring up among the trees as the lamp was lit in one of the sitting-rooms.
捉拿车继续前进，几分钟后，我们看到树丛中突然亮起灯光，那是灯在一间起居室里被点亮了。
“Do you know, Watson,” said Holmes as we sat together in the gathering darkness, “I have really some scruples as to taking you to-night.
“沃森先生，”说霍尔姆斯，我们坐在黑暗中，“我确实有些顾虑，今晚带你去。”
There is a distinct element of danger.”
有一种明显的危险。
“Can I be of assistance?”
“我可以帮上忙吗？”
“Your presence might be invaluable.”
“你的出现可能会非常有用。”
“Then I shall certainly come.”
“那么我一定会来的。”
“It is very kind of you.”
“这很感激。”
“You speak of danger.
“你谈到危险。
You have evidently seen more in these rooms than was visible to me.”
你显然在这些房间中看到的比我看的多。”
“No, but I fancy that I may have deduced a little more.
“不，但我猜想我可能多看了一些。”
I imagine that you saw all that I did.”
我想象你看到的和我看到的一样多。
“I saw nothing remarkable save the bell-rope, and what purpose that could answer I confess is more than I can imagine.”
“我只是看到铃绳，至于它有什么用，我实在想象不出来。”
“You saw the ventilator, too?”
“你也看到了通风口吗？”
“Yes, but I do not think that it is such a very unusual thing to have a small opening between two rooms.
“是的，但我认为在两个房间之间有一个小开口并不罕见。”
It was so small that a rat could hardly pass through.”
它太小了，连老鼠都很难通过。
“I knew that we should find a ventilator before ever we came to Stoke Moran.”
我知道，我们到达索尔顿摩根之前，必须找到一个通风口。
“My dear Holmes!”
“亲爱的华生！”
“Oh, yes, I did.
“哦，是的，我做到了。
You remember in her statement she said that her sister could smell Dr. Roylott’s cigar.
你记得她在陈述中说她姐姐能闻到罗伊洛特医生的烟。
Now, of course that suggested at once that there must be a communication between the two rooms.
现在，当然，这立刻引起了两个房间之间的联系。
It could only be a small one, or it would have been remarked upon at the coroner’s inquiry.
只能是小的，否则在解剖官的询问中会注意到的。
I deduced a ventilator.”
我得出结论，有一个通风口。
“But what harm can there be in that?”
“但那有什么不好呢？”
“Well, there is at least a curious coincidence of dates.
“嗯，至少有日期上的巧合。
A ventilator is made, a cord is hung, and a lady who sleeps in the bed dies.
一个通风口被制造，一根绳子被挂上，一个在床上睡觉的女士死亡。
Does not that strike you?”
这不让你觉得奇怪吗？”
“I cannot as yet see any connection.”
“我目前还看不出任何联系。”
“Did you observe anything very peculiar about that bed?”
“你注意到那张床有什么特别的地方吗？”
“No.”
“没有。”
“It was clamped to the floor.
“床是被固定在地上的。”
Did you ever see a bed fastened like that before?”
你以前见过这样的床钉吗？
“I cannot say that I have.”
“我不能说我见过。”
“The lady could not move her bed.
“那位女士不能移动她的床。
It must always be in the same relative position to the ventilator and to the rope—or so we may call it, since it was clearly never meant for a bell-pull.”
无论如何，它必须始终处于与通风机和绳子（或者我们可以说，因为显然它不是为警报拉绳设计的）之间的相对位置。
“Holmes,” I cried, “I seem to see dimly what you are hinting at.
“福尔摩斯，”我叫道，“我似乎隐约看到你暗示的东西。
We are only just in time to prevent some subtle and horrible crime.”
我们只是在时间上刚刚赶到，防止一场微妙而可怕的犯罪。
“Subtle enough and horrible enough.
微妙到足以可怕。
When a doctor does go wrong he is the first of criminals.
当医生犯错时，他就是第一个罪犯。
He has nerve and he has knowledge.
他有胆量，他知道。
Palmer and Pritchard were among the heads of their profession.
普尔和普里奇特是他们的行医界头领。
This man strikes even deeper, but I think, Watson, that we shall be able to strike deeper still.
这个人比他更深，但我认为，沃森先生，我们可能会更深入。
But we shall have horrors enough before the night is over; for goodness’ sake let us have a quiet pipe and turn our minds for a few hours to something more cheerful.”
但我们在晚上结束前会遇到许多恐怖的东西；请让我们在晚上结束前，用几小时的时间，把我们的思想集中在更愉快的事情上。
About nine o’clock the light among the trees was extinguished, and all was dark in the direction of the Manor House.
在九点钟左右，树丛中的灯光熄灭了，曼诺姆庄园的方向变得一片黑暗。
Two hours passed slowly away, and then, suddenly, just at the stroke of eleven, a single bright light shone out right in front of us.
两个小时过去了，缓慢地，然后，突然，就在十一点钟的时候，一束明亮的光线照进了我们面前。
“That is our signal,” said Holmes, springing to his feet; “it comes from the middle window.”
“那是我们的信号，”福尔摩斯叫道，跳到脚上， “它来自中间窗户。”
As we passed out he exchanged a few words with the landlord, explaining that we were going on a late visit to an acquaintance, and that it was possible that we might spend the night there.
我们穿过他时，与房东交换了几句话，解释说我们是去拜访一位熟人的晚访，并且有可能会在那里过夜。
A moment later we were out on the dark road, a chill wind blowing in our faces, and one yellow light twinkling in front of us through the gloom to guide us on our sombre errand.
一会儿后，我们来到黑暗的路上，寒风吹拂着我们的脸，前方有一盏黄灯在黑暗中闪烁，指引我们进行阴郁的使命。
There was little difficulty in entering the grounds, for unrepaired breaches gaped in the old park wall.
进入旧公园的围墙中，没有发现任何问题，因为旧墙的破损处大开着。

Making our way among the trees, we reached the lawn, crossed it, and were about to enter through the window when out from a clump of laurel bushes there darted what seemed to be a hideous and distorted child, who threw itself upon the grass with writhing limbs and then ran swiftly across the lawn into the darkness.
我们在树丛中穿行，到达草坪，穿过草坪，正准备通过窗户进入时，从灌木丛中突然窜出一个看起来畸形扭曲的孩子，四肢抽搐着，然后迅速穿过草坪进入黑暗中。
“My God!”
“我的天！”我低声说，“你看到了吗？”
I whispered; “did you see it?”
海默尔此时也显得惊慌，他的手像铁钳一样紧握着我的手腕，激动不已。
Holmes was for the moment as startled as I. His hand closed like a vice upon my wrist in his agitation.
然后他发出低低的笑声，把嘴唇贴在我耳边。
Then he broke into a low laugh and put his lips to my ear.
“这是一户好人家。”他轻声说。
“It is a nice household,” he murmured.
“那是一只猴子。”
“That is the baboon.”
我已经忘记了那位医生养的奇怪宠物。
I had forgotten the strange pets which the Doctor affected.
有一只猎豹，也许在我们的肩膀上随时都能找到。
There was a cheetah, too; perhaps we might find it upon our shoulders at any moment.
我承认，当我模仿海默尔的样子脱下鞋子后，发现自己进入了卧室，心里感到轻松。
I confess that I felt easier in my mind when, after following Holmes’ example and slipping off my shoes, I found myself inside the bedroom.
我的同伴无声无息地关上了窗帘，把灯移到了桌子，然后环视着房间。
My companion noiselessly closed the shutters, moved the lamp onto the table, and cast his eyes round the room.
我们看到的景象和白天一样，一切如常。
All was as we had seen it in the daytime.
一切都和我们白天所见的一样。
Then creeping up to me and making a trumpet of his hand, he whispered into my ear again so gently that it was all that I could do to distinguish the words:
于是，他悄悄地靠近我，用手指做成一个喇叭，又在我耳边轻轻低语，声音如此之小，以至于我几乎听不清：
“The least sound would be fatal to our plans.”
“最微小的声响都会破坏我们的计划。”
I nodded to show that I had heard.
我点点头表示我已听懂。
“We must sit without light.
我们必须在黑暗中坐着。
He would see it through the ventilator.”
他会透过通风管看到的。
I nodded again.
我再次点了点头。
“Do not go asleep; your very life may depend upon it.
请不要入睡，因为你的生命可能取决于这一点。
Have your pistol ready in case we should need it.
请随时准备枪，以防万一。
I will sit on the side of the bed, and you in that chair.”
我将在床的一边坐下，你坐在那把椅子上。
I took out my revolver and laid it on the corner of the table.
我拿出手枪放在桌子角。
Holmes had brought up a long thin cane, and this he placed upon the bed beside him.
霍尔姆斯拿来了一根长而细的竹竿，把它放在床边。
By it he laid the box of matches and the stump of a candle.
他把火柴盒和一根蜡烛的烛芯放在地上。
Then he turned down the lamp, and we were left in darkness.
于是他关了灯，我们陷入黑暗之中。
How shall I ever forget that dreadful vigil?
我怎么能够忘记那可怕的守夜？
I could not hear a sound, not even the drawing of a breath, and yet I knew that my companion sat open-eyed, within a few feet of me, in the same state of nervous tension in which I was myself.
我听不到任何声音，连呼吸声也听不到，但我知道我的同伴睁着眼睛，就在几英尺之外，处于和我一样的紧张状态。
The shutters cut off the least ray of light, and we waited in absolute darkness.
门缝遮住了最后一丝光线，我们静静地等待在漆黑中。
From outside came the occasional cry of a night-bird, and once at our very window a long drawn catlike whine, which told us that the cheetah was indeed at liberty.
从外面传来偶尔的夜鸟叫声，我们甚至在窗前听到了长啸，告诉我们猎豹确实自由了。
Far away we could hear the deep tones of the parish clock, which boomed out every quarter of an hour.
我们远远地听到钟楼的深沉钟声，每半小时敲一次。
How long they seemed, those quarters!
这些时间似乎很长！
Twelve struck, and one and two and three, and still we sat waiting silently for whatever might befall.
十二点敲响了，一、二、三，我们静静地等待着什么将发生。
Suddenly there was the momentary gleam of a light up in the direction of the ventilator, which vanished immediately, but was succeeded by a strong smell of burning oil and heated metal.
突然间，从通风口方向出现了一瞬间的光亮，随即消失，但被继之而来的油味和金属的热味所取代。
Someone in the next room had lit a dark-lantern.
在隔壁房间里有人点燃了暗灯。
I heard a gentle sound of movement, and then all was silent once more, though the smell grew stronger.
我听到轻微的移动声，然后再次变得寂静，尽管气味变得更浓。
For half an hour I sat with straining ears.
我坐了半个小时。
Then suddenly another sound became audible—a very gentle, soothing sound, like that of a small jet of steam escaping continually from a kettle.
突然间，又听到了一种轻微、舒缓的声音，像小蒸汽喷射器不断从壶里喷出的蒸汽声。
The instant that we heard it, Holmes sprang from the bed, struck a match, and lashed furiously with his cane at the bell-pull.
当我们听到声音的那一刻，霍尔姆斯从床上跳起来，点燃了火柴，猛烈地用棍子击打铃拉。
“You see it, Watson?” he yelled.
“你看到了吗，沃森？”他喊道。
“You see it?”
“你看到了吗？”
But I saw nothing.
我什么也没有看到。

At the moment when Holmes struck the light I heard a low, clear whistle, but the sudden glare flashing into my weary eyes made it impossible for me to tell what it was at which my friend lashed so savagely.
当霍尔姆斯点燃火柴时，我听到一声低沉的清脆的哨声，但突然耀眼的光线使我无法分辨出是哪个地方的响声，我朋友如此猛烈地挥动棍子。
I could, however, see that his face was deadly pale and filled with horror and loathing.
我却可以看到他的脸色苍白，充满了恐惧和厌恶。
He had ceased to strike and was gazing up at the ventilator when suddenly there broke from the silence of the night the most horrible cry to which I have ever listened.
他停止了击打，正凝视着呼吸机，突然从夜的寂静中传来最可怕的哭声，这是我听过的最恐怖的哭声。
It swelled up louder and louder, a hoarse yell of pain and fear and anger all mingled in the one dreadful shriek.
这哭声越来越响，嘶哑的喊声中夹杂着痛苦、恐惧和愤怒。
They say that away down in the village, and even in the distant parsonage, that cry raised the sleepers from their beds.
他们说，在村子的尽头，甚至在遥远的牧师府，那哭声唤醒了睡梦中的人们。
It struck cold to our hearts, and I stood gazing at Holmes, and he at me, until the last echoes of it had died away into the silence from which it rose.
这声音刺痛了我们的心，我站在霍尔姆斯的面前，他站在我的面前，直到那声音的回声消失在寂静中。
“What can it mean?”
“这是什么意思？”
I gasped.
我吸了口气。
“It means that it is all over,” Holmes answered.
“这意思是已经结束了，”霍尔姆斯回答。
“And perhaps, after all, it is for the best.
“也许，最终，这对你来说也是最好的。”
Take your pistol, and we will enter Dr. Roylott’s room.”
拿起你的手枪，我们进入罗伊洛特医生的房间。
With a grave face he lit the lamp and led the way down the corridor.
他带着严肃的脸，点燃了灯，带领我们沿着走廊走。
Twice he struck at the chamber door without any reply from within.
他两次敲打在房间的门上，但门内没有任何回应。
Then he turned the handle and entered, I at his heels, with the cocked pistol in my hand.
然后他转动把手，进入房间，我紧随其后，手里拿着扣着的枪。
It was a singular sight which met our eyes.
突然出现的景象让我们目瞪口呆。
On the table stood a dark-lantern with the shutter half open, throwing a brilliant beam of light upon the iron safe, the door of which was ajar.
表面上，桌上放着一盏暗灯，门半开着，照亮了铁保险箱，门开着。
Beside this table, on the wooden chair, sat Dr. Grimesby Roylott clad in a long grey dressing-gown, his bare ankles protruding beneath, and his feet thrust into red heelless Turkish slippers.
旁边这张桌子旁，坐着格里米斯伯爵罗伊洛特医生穿着长灰色的睡衣，他的裸脚踝突出，脚趾伸进红色的无跟土耳其拖鞋里。
Across his lap lay the short stock with the long lash which we had noticed during the day.
他的腿上放着那条短的带子，上面挂着长长的鞭子，我们白天注意到的。
His chin was cocked upward and his eyes were fixed in a dreadful, rigid stare at the corner of the ceiling.
他的下巴向上翘着，眼睛盯着天花板角落。
Round his brow he had a peculiar yellow band, with brownish speckles, which seemed to be bound tightly round his head.
他的额头有一块奇怪的黄色的带子，上面有褐色的斑点，似乎被紧紧地绑在头上。
As we entered he made neither sound nor motion.
当我们进来时，他没有发出声音也没有动。
“The band! the speckled band!” whispered Holmes.
“那带子！那斑点的带子！”霍尔姆斯低声说道。
I took a step forward.
我向前迈了一步。
In an instant his strange headgear began to move, and there reared itself from among his hair the squat diamond-shaped head and puffed neck of a loathsome serpent.
突然间，他奇怪的头饰开始移动，从他头发里露出了一个小小的、像蛇一样形状的脑袋和一个膨胀的脖子。
“It is a swamp adder!” cried Holmes; “the deadliest snake in India.
“那是一条沼泽蝰！”霍尔姆斯喊道，“印度最致命的蛇。”
He has died within ten seconds of being bitten.
他死于被咬的十秒之内。
Violence does, in truth, recoil upon the violent, and the schemer falls into the pit which he digs for another.
实际上，暴力会反噬暴力者，谋略者会陷入自己挖的陷阱。
Let us thrust this creature back into its den, and we can then remove Miss Stoner to some place of shelter and let the county police know what has happened.”
让我们把这个怪物推回它的洞穴，然后我们可以把斯顿小姐送到一个避难所，让县警察知道发生了什么。

As he spoke he drew the dog-whip swiftly from the dead man’s lap, and throwing the noose round the reptile’s neck he drew it from its horrid perch and, carrying it at arm’s length, threw it into the iron safe, which he closed upon it.
他说话时，从死者的腿上迅速抽出狗鞭，用绳子套住蛇的脖子，然后从它的可怕位置上拉起它，用胳膊的长度把它扔进铁箱，铁箱关上后，他打开它。
Such are the true facts of the death of Dr. Grimesby Roylott, of Stoke Moran.
这就是格里米斯伯爵罗伊洛特医生在斯托克莫兰的死亡真相。

It is not necessary that I should prolong a narrative which has already run to too great a length by telling how we broke the sad news to the terrified girl, how we conveyed her by the morning train to the care of her good aunt at Harrow, of how the slow process of official inquiry came to the conclusion that the doctor met his fate while indiscreetly playing with a dangerous pet.
我不需要再延长一个已经写得太长的叙述，告诉如何向惊恐的少女宣布这个悲伤的消息，如何用早晨的火车把她送到哈罗的好姑妈那里，如何缓慢的官方调查最终得出结论，医生是在不经意间玩弄危险的宠物时死于危险的毒蛇。
The little which I had yet to learn of the case was told me by Sherlock Holmes as we travelled back next day.
我所知道的关于这桩案子的其他事情，是和夏洛克·福尔摩斯一起旅行回来的第二天告诉我的。
“I had,” said he, “come to an entirely erroneous conclusion which shows, my dear Watson, how dangerous it always is to reason from insufficient data.
“我也是，”他说，“得出了一个完全错误的结论，这表明，亲爱的沃森先生，从不充分的数据中推理是多么危险。

The presence of the gipsies, and the use of the word ‘band,’ which was used by the poor girl, no doubt, to explain the appearance which she had caught a hurried glimpse of by the light of her match, were sufficient to put me upon an entirely wrong scent.
贫穷女孩所说的‘圈’这个词，以及吉普赛人的存在，这些足以让我走上一个完全错误的轨迹。

I can only claim the merit that I instantly reconsidered my position when, however, it became clear to me that whatever danger threatened an occupant of the room could not come either from the window or the door.
我只能声称，当我意识到危险威胁着房间的住客时，我立刻重新考虑了我的位置。
My attention was speedily drawn, as I have already remarked to you, to this ventilator, and to the bell-rope which hung down to the bed.
我的注意力很快被吸引到这个通风口上，以及挂在床下的铃绳上。

The discovery that this was a dummy, and that the bed was clamped to the floor, instantly gave rise to the suspicion that the rope was there as a bridge for something passing through the hole and coming to the bed.
发现这只是一个假的，床被固定在地板上，立刻引起了怀疑，绳子可能是用来通过洞口和到达床的某种东西的桥梁。

The idea of a snake instantly occurred to me, and when I coupled it with my knowledge that the doctor was furnished with a supply of creatures from India, I felt that I was probably on the right track.
我想到一条蛇，当我知道医生有来自印度的动物供应时，我感觉我可能在正确的轨道上。
The idea of using a form of poison which could not possibly be discovered by any chemical test was just such a one as would occur to a clever and ruthless man who had had an Eastern training.
使用一种不可能通过任何化学测试发现的毒药的想法，正好是聪明且无情的人会想到的，他有东方的训练。
The rapidity with which such a poison would take effect would also, from his point of view, be an advantage.
这种毒药的迅速作用也会对他的观点有利。
It would be a sharp-eyed coroner, indeed, who could distinguish the two little dark punctures which would show where the poison fangs had done their work.
一个敏锐的验尸官，甚至可能无法区分在毒针上显示的两个小黑点，会如何区分。
Then I thought of the whistle.
然后我想到了哨子。
Of course he must recall the snake before the morning light revealed it to the victim.
当他早上光线揭示了蛇时，他必须回忆起在受害者面前的蛇。
He had trained it, probably by the use of the milk which we saw, to return to him when summoned.
他可能通过我们看到的牛奶来训练它，让它在召唤时返回。
He would put it through this ventilator at the hour that he thought best, with the certainty that it would crawl down the rope and land on the bed.
他会在这个通风口上用最佳时间通过，确保它沿着绳子爬下来，落在床上。
It might or might not bite the occupant, perhaps she might escape every night for a week, but sooner or later she must fall a victim.
它可能或可能不会咬住住客，也许她可能在一周内逃脱，但总有一天她必须成为受害者。
“I had come to these conclusions before ever I had entered his room.
我在进入他的房间之前就已经得出这些结论。
An inspection of his chair showed me that he had been in the habit of standing on it, which of course would be necessary in order that he should reach the ventilator.
对他的椅子进行检查，我发现他习惯于站在上面，这当然是为了能够到达通风口。
The sight of the safe, the saucer of milk, and the loop of whipcord were enough to finally dispel any doubts which may have remained.
看到保险箱、牛奶碟子和绷带环，足以最终消除任何可能存在的怀疑。
The metallic clang heard by Miss Stoner was obviously caused by her stepfather hastily closing the door of his safe upon its terrible occupant.
石匠斯特顿听到的金属撞击声显然是她父亲匆忙关闭保险箱门时，对他的可怕主人的猛烈撞击造成的。
Having once made up my mind, you know the steps which I took in order to put the matter to the proof.
一旦决定了，你就知道我采取了什么步骤来证明这一点。
I heard the creature hiss as I have no doubt that you did also, and I instantly lit the light and attacked it.”
我听到那个生物嘶吼，我也肯定你也是，我立刻点起灯，攻击它。
“With the result of driving it through the ventilator.”
通过通风口把它杀死。
“And also with the result of causing it to turn upon its master at the other side.
也通过杀死它来让它在另一边的主人面前转过身。
Some of the blows of my cane came home and roused its snakish temper, so that it flew upon the first person it saw.
我的棍子的某些击打打中了它，激怒了它的蛇性，于是它飞向它看到的第一个对象。
In this way I am no doubt indirectly responsible for Dr. Grimesby Roylott’s death, and I cannot say that it is likely to weigh very heavily upon my conscience.”
通过这种方式，我间接地对格里米斯比·罗伊尔特医生的死亡负责，我不能说这在我心中不会留下沉重的负担。

ch.et: IX. The Adventure of the Engineer’s Thumb
ch.zt: 第九篇 · 工程师大拇指案
p: Of all the problems which have been submitted to my friend, Mr. Sherlock Holmes, for solution during the years of our intimacy, there were only two which I was the means of introducing to his notice—that of Mr. Hatherley’s thumb, and that of Colonel Warburton’s madness.
我的朋友，史密斯先生，对我提出解决的难题只有两个——那就是霍特雷先生的拇指和沃布尔顿上校的疯狂。

Of these the latter may have afforded a finer field for an acute and original observer, but the other was so strange in its inception and so dramatic in its details that it may be the more worthy of being placed upon record, even if it gave my friend fewer openings for those deductive methods of reasoning by which he achieved such remarkable results.
这两个中，后者可能为敏锐和独到的观察者提供了更广阔的视野，但前者在起源和细节上如此奇特，以至于它可能更值得记录，即使它减少了我朋友的推理方法的开销，这些方法使他取得了如此惊人的成就。

The story has, I believe, been told more than once in the newspapers, but, like all such narratives, its effect is much less striking when set forth en bloc in a single half-column of print than when the facts slowly evolve before your own eyes, and the mystery clears gradually away as each new discovery furnishes a step which leads on to the complete truth.
我相信，这个故事在报纸上被报道过不止一次，但就像所有这样的叙述一样，当它被浓缩成一页半的印刷品时，它的效果比当事实慢慢在你眼前展开，谜团逐渐清晰，新的发现提供了一个步骤，这一步引导你走向完全的真相时，显得更不突出。
At the time the circumstances made a deep impression upon me, and the lapse of two years has hardly served to weaken the effect.
当时的情境对我产生了深刻的印象，两年后，这种印象并没有减弱。
It was in the summer of ’89, not long after my marriage, that the events occurred which I am now about to summarise.
在1889年夏天，不久我结婚后，发生的事件我正在总结。

I had returned to civil practice and had finally abandoned Holmes in his Baker Street rooms, although I continually visited him and occasionally even persuaded him to forgo his Bohemian habits so far as to come and visit us.
我已经回到民事执业，已经彻底放弃了霍士在贝克街的房间，尽管我经常访问他，甚至说服他放弃他的放荡习惯，以便来我们这里。
My practice had steadily increased, and as I happened to live at no very great distance from Paddington Station, I got a few patients from among the officials.
我的执业稳步增加，因为我住的地方离帕丁顿火车站不远，我得到一些官员的病人。
One of these, whom I had cured of a painful and lingering disease, was never weary of advertising my virtues and of endeavouring to send me on every sufferer over whom he might have any influence.
这个病人，我治愈了一种痛苦的、持久的疾病，他从我那里得到了我的美德的广告和试图将我介绍给任何他可能有影响力的人的病人。
One morning, at a little before seven o’clock, I was awakened by the maid tapping at the door to announce that two men had come from Paddington and were waiting in the consulting-room.
有一天早晨，七点左右，我被女仆敲门唤醒，告诉她有两个男人从帕丁顿来，正在咨询室等待。
I dressed hurriedly, for I knew by experience that railway cases were seldom trivial, and hastened downstairs.
我匆忙穿衣，因为我知道铁路案件通常是不简单的，我急忙下楼。
As I descended, my old ally, the guard, came out of the room and closed the door tightly behind him.
当我下楼时，我的老朋友，看守员，从房间里出来，紧紧关上了门。
“I’ve got him here,” he whispered, jerking his thumb over his shoulder; “he’s all right.”
“我把他带到这里来了，”他低声说，用他的拇指指着他的肩膀，“他没事。”
“What is it, then?”
“这是什么？”
I asked, for his manner suggested that it was some strange creature which he had caged up in my room.
我问道，因为他的姿态暗示着这是一只被关在房间里的小生物。
“It’s a new patient,” he whispered.
“这是新病人，”他低声说。
“I thought I’d bring him round myself; then he couldn’t slip away.
我心想自己来把他解救出来；这样他就可以溜走了。
There he is, all safe and sound.
他安然无恙地站在那里。
I must go now, Doctor; I have my dooties, just the same as you.”
我得走了，医生；我的腿也疼，和你一样。
And off he went, this trusty tout, without even giving me time to thank him.
他匆匆离去，这个忠实的向导，甚至没有给我时间道谢。
I entered my consulting-room and found a gentleman seated by the table.
我走进我的咨询室，发现桌上坐着一个先生。
He was quietly dressed in a suit of heather tweed with a soft cloth cap which he had laid down upon my books.
他穿着一件褐色的毛呢套装，戴着一顶软帽，帽上放着我的书。
Round one of his hands he had a handkerchief wrapped, which was mottled all over with bloodstains.
他的一只手上包着一块手帕，上面全是血渍。

He was young, not more than five-and-twenty, I should say, with a strong, masculine face; but he was exceedingly pale and gave me the impression of a man who was suffering from some strong agitation, which it took all his strength of mind to control.
他年轻，大约二十五岁，面庞健壮，但脸色苍白，给人的印象是受了严重的刺激，他用尽了全部的意志力来控制。
“I am sorry to knock you up so early, Doctor,” said he, “but I have had a very serious accident during the night.
“很抱歉早上这么早打扰了你，医生，”他说，“但我昨晚发生了一件非常严重的事故。
I came in by train this morning, and on inquiring at Paddington as to where I might find a doctor, a worthy fellow very kindly escorted me here.
我今天早上坐火车来的，到皮卡顿时问医生在哪里，一个值得信赖的先生很热心地把我带到这里。
I gave the maid a card, but I see that she has left it upon the side-table.”
我给女仆一张名片，但看到她放在桌边的。
I took it up and glanced at it.
我拿起名片，瞥了一眼。
“Mr. Victor Hatherley, hydraulic engineer, 16A, Victoria Street (3rd floor).”
“维克多·哈特利先生，水利工程师，16A，维多利亚街（三楼）。”
That was the name, style, and abode of my morning visitor.
那就是我早上来访者的姓名、风格和住所。
“I regret that I have kept you waiting,” said I, sitting down in my library-chair.
“我很抱歉让你久等了，”我说，坐在我的图书馆椅上。
“You are fresh from a night journey, I understand, which is in itself a monotonous occupation.”
"你昨晚旅途奔波，我明白，这本身也是一种单调的消遣。"
“Oh, my night could not be called monotonous,” said he, and laughed.
"哦，我的夜晚不能称之为单调的，"他说，并笑了。
He laughed very heartily, with a high, ringing note, leaning back in his chair and shaking his sides.
他笑得很开心，发出高亢的笑声，倚靠在椅子上，摇动着身体。
All my medical instincts rose up against that laugh.
我所有的医学直觉都反对这种笑声。
“Stop it!”
"住手！"
I cried; “pull yourself together!” and I poured out some water from a caraffe.
我喊道："振作起来！"我从水壶里倒了一些水。
It was useless, however.
无论如何是无效的。
He was off in one of those hysterical outbursts which come upon a strong nature when some great crisis is over and gone.
他再次清醒过来，非常疲倦，脸色苍白。
Presently he came to himself once more, very weary and pale-looking.
然后他再次清醒过来，非常疲倦，脸色苍白。
“I have been making a fool of myself,” he gasped.
"我把自己搞成一个傻瓜了，"他喘着气说。
“Not at all.
Drink this.”
"喝点什么吧。"
I dashed some brandy into the water, and the colour began to come back to his bloodless cheeks.
我把一些杜松子酒倒进水里，水的颜色开始恢复了。
“That’s better!” said he.
"这就好多了！"他说。
“And now, Doctor, perhaps you would kindly attend to my thumb, or rather to the place where my thumb used to be.”
"现在，医生，或许你能够照顾一下我的拇指，或者说是拇指的位置。"
He unwound the handkerchief and held out his hand.
他解开手帕，伸出右手。
It gave even my hardened nerves a shudder to look at it.
看到它，连我这坚硬的神经也忍不住打了个寒战。
There were four protruding fingers and a horrid red, spongy surface where the thumb should have been.
有四根突出的指头，一个可怕的红、海绵状的表面，应该是拇指的位置。
It had been hacked or torn right out from the roots.
它是被割破或撕裂的，从根部割断。
“Good heavens!”
“天啊！”
I cried, “this is a terrible injury.
我叫道，“这是一次可怕的伤害。
It must have bled considerably.”
它一定流了很多血。”
“Yes, it did.
“是的，它流了很多血。”
I fainted when it was done, and I think that I must have been senseless for a long time.
“我晕倒了，它割断了，我估计我可能昏迷了好一段时间。
When I came to I found that it was still bleeding, so I tied one end of my handkerchief very tightly round the wrist and braced it up with a twig.”
我醒来时发现伤口还在流血，所以我紧紧地把我的手帕绑在手腕上，用树枝支撑起来。”
“Excellent!
“好极了！”
You should have been a surgeon.”
你应该是个外科医生。”
“It is a question of hydraulics, you see, and came within my own province.”
“这是个液压问题，你看，这正是我的专业。”
“This has been done,” said I, examining the wound, “by a very heavy and sharp instrument.”
“这伤口是用一种非常重的、锋利的工具割破的。”
“A thing like a cleaver,” said he.
“是的，它用的是像刀一样的工具。”
“An accident, I presume?”
“这是一起意外，是吗？”
“By no means.”
“绝对不是。”
“What! a murderous attack?”
“什么！一场谋杀？”
“Very murderous indeed.”
“非常凶残的。”
“You horrify me.”
“你吓死我了。”
I sponged the wound, cleaned it, dressed it, and finally covered it over with cotton wadding and carbolised bandages.
我用纱布包扎伤口，清洗干净，然后用纱布和炭疽绷带覆盖。
He lay back without wincing, though he bit his lip from time to time.
他躺下时没有痛苦的表情，只是时不时地咬咬嘴唇。
“How is that?”
“这是怎么回事？”
I asked when I had finished.
我问完后，我是否已经完成。
“Capital!
“很好！
Between your brandy and your bandage, I feel a new man.
“我喝的威士忌和用绷带包扎，感觉像换了一个人。”
I was very weak, but I have had a good deal to go through.”
我很虚弱，但我已经经历了很多。
“Perhaps you had better not speak of the matter.
“也许你最好不要提起这件事。”
It is evidently trying to your nerves.”
它显然在折磨你的神经。”
“Oh, no, not now.
“哦，不，现在不要。

I shall have to tell my tale to the police; but, between ourselves, if it were not for the convincing evidence of this wound of mine, I should be surprised if they believed my statement, for it is a very extraordinary one, and I have not much in the way of proof with which to back it up; and, even if they believe me, the clues which I can give them are so vague that it is a question whether justice will be done.”
我必须把我的故事告诉警察，但私下里，如果我没有这伤口的有力证据，我怀疑他们是否相信我的陈述，因为这是一条非常奇异的陈述，我没有很多可以支持它的东西；而且，即使他们相信我，我给他们的线索也太模糊，以至于是否能公正地审判还值得怀疑。

“Ha!” cried I, “if it is anything in the nature of a problem which you desire to see solved, I should strongly recommend you to come to my friend, Mr. Sherlock Holmes, before you go to the official police.”
“哦！”我叫道，“如果这是一道可以解决的难题，我强烈建议你先去我朋友，史密斯先生·福尔摩斯那里，而不是去官方警察。”
“Oh, I have heard of that fellow,” answered my visitor, “and I should be very glad if he would take the matter up, though of course I must use the official police as well.
“哦，我听说过那个人，我非常乐意如果他能解决这个问题，当然，我必须使用官方警察。”
Would you give me an introduction to him?”
你会给我介绍他吗？
“I’ll do better.
“我会做得更好。”
I’ll take you round to him myself.”
我会亲自带你去。
“I should be immensely obliged to you.”
“我非常感激你。”
“We’ll call a cab and go together.
“我们叫一辆出租车，一起走。”
We shall just be in time to have a little breakfast with him.
我们刚好赶上给他一点早餐。
Do you feel equal to it?”
你觉得自己能胜任吗？
“Yes; I shall not feel easy until I have told my story.”
“是的，我直到把我的故事讲出来才感到安心。”
“Then my servant will call a cab, and I shall be with you in an instant.”
“那么我的仆人会叫出租车，我立刻就会到。”
I rushed upstairs, explained the matter shortly to my wife, and in five minutes was inside a hansom, driving with my new acquaintance to Baker Street.
我冲上楼，向我妻子解释了这件事，五分钟内我进了车里，和我新认识的人一起开车到贝克街。

Sherlock Holmes was, as I expected, lounging about his sitting-room in his dressing-gown, reading the agony column of The Times and smoking his before-breakfast pipe, which was composed of all the plugs and dottles left from his smokes of the day before, all carefully dried and collected on the corner of the mantelpiece.
福尔摩斯先生，正如我所预料的，正悠闲地坐在他的衣帽间里，读着《泰晤士报》的痛苦版，正在吃他前一天早餐的烟斗，烟斗里有所有剩下的烟丝，都精心地干燥和收集在壁炉架的角落里。
He received us in his quietly genial fashion, ordered fresh rashers and eggs, and joined us in a hearty meal.
他用他平和的风格接待我们，叫了新鲜的煎肉和鸡蛋，和我们一起吃了一顿丰盛的早餐。
When it was concluded he settled our new acquaintance upon the sofa, placed a pillow beneath his head, and laid a glass of brandy and water within his reach.
当他得出结论时，他把我们新认识的人放在沙发上，把枕头放在他的头上，然后把一杯威士忌和水放在他的伸手可及的地方。
“It is easy to see that your experience has been no common one, Mr. Hatherley,” said he.
“从你经验中，可以看出你不是普通人，”他说。
“Pray, lie down there and make yourself absolutely at home.
“请，躺下，让你自己完全感到舒适。
Tell us what you can, but stop when you are tired and keep up your strength with a little stimulant.”
告诉我们你所知道的，但当你感到疲倦时，保持体力的补充，用一点兴奋剂。”
“Thank you,” said my patient, “but I have felt another man since the doctor bandaged me, and I think that your breakfast has completed the cure.
“谢谢，”病人说，“但我感觉另一个男人，自从医生包扎我时，我觉得你的早餐完成了治疗。
I shall take up as little of your valuable time as possible, so I shall start at once upon my peculiar experiences.”
我将尽可能少占用你宝贵的时间，所以我将立即开始我的独特经历。

Holmes sat in his big armchair with the weary, heavy-lidded expression which veiled his keen and eager nature, while I sat opposite to him, and we listened in silence to the strange story which our visitor detailed to us.
森林坐在他那大扶手椅上，带着疲惫，沉重的眼睑遮盖了他敏锐和渴望的本性，而我坐在他对面，我们默默地听这位访客详细叙述他的奇特故事。
“You must know,” said he, “that I am an orphan and a bachelor, residing alone in lodgings in London.
“你必须知道，我是孤儿和单身汉，独自居住在伦敦的住所里。
By profession I am a hydraulic engineer, and I have had considerable experience of my work during the seven years that I was apprenticed to Venner & Matheson, the well-known firm, of Greenwich.
我的职业是水力工程师，我在韦恩纳&马森斯的著名公司里服役七年，积累了相当的经验。

Two years ago, having served my time, and having also come into a fair sum of money through my poor father’s death, I determined to start in business for myself and took professional chambers in Victoria Street.
两年前，当我完成了我的工作，并且也因为我可怜的父亲的死亡而得到了一笔可观的财富，我决定自己创业，并在维多利亚街开设了专业办公室。
“I suppose that everyone finds his first independent start in business a dreary experience.
“我想每个人都觉得第一次独立创业的体验是乏味的。
To me it has been exceptionally so.
对我来说，它特别如此。
During two years I have had three consultations and one small job, and that is absolutely all that my profession has brought me.
在两年里，我有三次咨询，一次小工作，这是我职业带来的全部。
My gross takings amount to £ 27 10s.
我的净收入为27英镑10先令。
Every day, from nine in the morning until four in the afternoon, I waited in my little den, until at last my heart began to sink, and I came to believe that I should never have any practice at all.
每天从上午九点到下午四点，我在我的小房间等待，直到最后我的心脏开始下沉，我开始相信我将永远不会有任何业务。
“Yesterday, however, just as I was thinking of leaving the office, my clerk entered to say there was a gentleman waiting who wished to see me upon business.
“然而，昨天，当我正打算离开办公室时，我的秘书进来对我说，有一位先生要见我，因为有业务。
He brought up a card, too, with the name of ‘Colonel Lysander Stark’ engraved upon it.
他也带来了名片，名片上刻着“少校洛桑·斯各特”的名字。
Close at his heels came the colonel himself, a man rather over the middle size, but of an exceeding thinness.
随即紧随其后的是那位上校，一个身材中等但异常瘦削的人。
I do not think that I have ever seen so thin a man.
我从未见过这么瘦的人。
His whole face sharpened away into nose and chin, and the skin of his cheeks was drawn quite tense over his outstanding bones.
他的整个脸都变得尖锐起来，鼻子和下巴也变得紧绷，突出的骨头也变得绷紧。
Yet this emaciation seemed to be his natural habit, and due to no disease, for his eye was bright, his step brisk, and his bearing assured.
但这种消瘦似乎是他天生的习惯，不是因为疾病，因为他的眼睛明亮，步伐轻快，举止从容。
He was plainly but neatly dressed, and his age, I should judge, would be nearer forty than thirty.
他穿着非常整洁，判断他的年龄大约在四十岁左右。
“‘Mr.
“‘Mr. Hatherley?’ 他问道，带着一些德语的口音。
Hatherley?’ said he, with something of a German accent.
“哈瑟利？”他说道，语气中带着几分德式口音。
‘You have been recommended to me, Mr. Hatherley, as being a man who is not only proficient in his profession but is also discreet and capable of preserving a secret.’
“我鞠躬，感觉像一个年轻人一样受到如此优待。
“I bowed, feeling as flattered as any young man would at such an address.
“‘请问，是谁推荐我的？’”
‘May I ask who it was who gave me so good a character?’
“‘好吧，也许现在我不能告诉你，因为就在这个时候，我从同一个人那里听说，您都是孤儿，单身汉，住在伦敦独自一人。’”
“‘Well, perhaps it is better that I should not tell you that just at this moment.
“‘这完全正确，’我回答说，‘但您会原谅我如果我表示，我不认为这些与我的职业资格有任何关系。’”
I have it from the same source that you are both an orphan and a bachelor and are residing alone in London.’
我从同一个人那里听说，你和他都是孤儿，单身汉，都在伦敦独自居住。
“‘That is quite correct,’ I answered; ‘but you will excuse me if I say that I cannot see how all this bears upon my professional qualifications.
“‘那是完全正确的，’我回答道，‘但你如果允许我这么说，我无法理解这与我的专业资格有何关联。’”
I understand that it was on a professional matter that you wished to speak to me?’
我明白，那是为了一个专业上的事情，你来找我的？
“‘Undoubtedly so.
““当然了。”
But you will find that all I say is really to the point.
但是你发现，我所说的一切，都是真的很直截了当。

I have a professional commission for you, but absolute secrecy is quite essential—absolute secrecy, you understand, and of course we may expect that more from a man who is alone than from one who lives in the bosom of his family.’
我有一份专业的工作给你，但绝对的保密是必须的——绝对的保密，你明白的，当然我们也会从一个独自一人的人那里，比从一个住在家庭中的一个人那里，更期待得到更多的信任。”
“‘If I promise to keep a secret,’ said I, ‘you may absolutely depend upon my doing so.’
““如果我答应保密，”我说，“你绝对可以信赖我。”
“He looked very hard at me as I spoke, and it seemed to me that I had never seen so suspicious and questioning an eye.
““你答应了，”他说。
“‘Do you promise, then?’ said he at last.
““是的，我答应了。”
“‘Yes, I promise.’
““绝对的、完全的沉默，在任何时间、任何地点、任何时间之后？
“‘Absolute and complete silence before, during, and after?
不提及任何与这件事有关的任何事情，无论是口头的还是书面的？”
No reference to the matter at all, either in word or writing?’
““我已经给你我的承诺了。”
“‘I have already given you my word.’
“‘Very good.’
他突然站起来，像闪电一样穿过房间，然后猛地打开门。
He suddenly sprang up, and darting like lightning across the room he flung open the door.
外面的那篇文字是空的。
The passage outside was empty.
““那就好。”他说回来。
“‘That’s all right,’ said he, coming back.
“‘那就好了，’他说，回来时说道。”
‘I know that clerks are sometimes curious as to their master’s affairs.
我知道职员有时会对他们的主人生意感兴趣。
Now we can talk in safety.’
现在我们可以安全地交谈了。
He drew up his chair very close to mine and began to stare at me again with the same questioning and thoughtful look.
他把椅子靠近我，再次用同样的疑惑和沉思的目光盯着我。
“A feeling of repulsion, and of something akin to fear had begun to rise within me at the strange antics of this fleshless man.
“一种排斥感和某种类似恐惧的感觉在我心中开始上升，对这个肉身空虚的人的奇异行为感到奇怪。
Even my dread of losing a client could not restrain me from showing my impatience.
即使对失去一个客户我感到恐惧，也无法阻止我表现出我的急躁。
“‘I beg that you will state your business, sir,’ said I; ‘my time is of value.’
“‘我恳求您陈述您的业务，先生，’我说道，‘我的时间是宝贵的。’
Heaven forgive me for that last sentence, but the words came to my lips.
天哪，我刚才那句话，但话到嘴边。
“‘How would fifty guineas for a night’s work suit you?’ he asked.
“‘如何，五十镑的工钱合适吗？’他问道。
“‘Most admirably.’
“‘I say a night’s work, but an hour’s would be nearer the mark.
“‘我讲的是工钱，但一小时的工钱更接近实际。
I simply want your opinion about a hydraulic stamping machine which has got out of gear.
我只是想听听关于一台失灵的液压压印机的意见。
If you show us what is wrong we shall soon set it right ourselves.
如果你们告诉我们问题所在，我们很快就能自己解决。
What do you think of such a commission as that?’
你对这样的委托怎么看？
“‘The work appears to be light and the pay munificent.’
“‘看起来工作很轻，工资丰厚。’
“‘Precisely so.
“‘正是这样。’
We shall want you to come to-night by the last train.’
我们今晚要乘最后一班火车去的。
“‘Where to?’
““去哪儿？”
“‘To Eyford, in Berkshire.
““去伯克郡的伊弗福德。
It is a little place near the borders of Oxfordshire, and within seven miles of Reading.
它位于奥英斯郡的边境附近，距读城七英里。
There is a train from Paddington which would bring you there at about 11:15.’
从皮特森顿车站出发的火车大约在11:15到达伊弗福德站。
“‘Very good.’
“‘I shall come down in a carriage to meet you.’
““我会坐马车来接你。”
“‘There is a drive, then?’
““有马车吗？”
“‘Yes, our little place is quite out in the country.
““是的，我们的小地方完全在乡下。
It is a good seven miles from Eyford Station.’
伊弗福德车站距我们有七英里。”
“‘Then we can hardly get there before midnight.
“那么我们很难在午夜前到达。
I suppose there would be no chance of a train back.
我猜想回程的火车没有机会了。
I should be compelled to stop the night.’
我不得不过夜。”
“‘Yes, we could easily give you a shake-down.’
““我们很容易给你安排一下。”
“‘That is very awkward.
““那很不巧。”
Could I not come at some more convenient hour?’
“我难道不能找个更方便的时间来吗？”
“‘We have judged it best that you should come late.
“我们觉得最好你来晚一些。”
It is to recompense you for any inconvenience that we are paying to you, a young and unknown man, a fee which would buy an opinion from the very heads of your profession.
这是为了补偿你对我们带来的不便，一个年轻而未知的男子，这是一笔足以买来你所在行内最高层意见的费用。
Still, of course, if you would like to draw out of the business, there is plenty of time to do so.’
但是，当然，如果你愿意拖长时间，可以继续拖长时间。
“I thought of the fifty guineas, and of how very useful they would be to me.
“我想到五十先令，想到它们对我有多么有用。
‘Not at all,’ said I, ‘I shall be very happy to accommodate myself to your wishes.
“不，”我说，“我很乐意按照您的意愿来安排。
I should like, however, to understand a little more clearly what it is that you wish me to do.’
我想，不过，想了解一下您希望我做什么。”
“‘Quite so.
“完全正确。
It is very natural that the pledge of secrecy which we have exacted from you should have aroused your curiosity.
这是自然的，因为我们要求你保密的承诺已经引起了你的好奇心。
I have no wish to commit you to anything without your having it all laid before you.
我没有意愿未经你同意就让你陷入任何事情。
I suppose that we are absolutely safe from eavesdroppers?’
我猜我们绝对安全，没有耳目窥探的可能？
“‘Entirely.’
“完全。”
“‘Then the matter stands thus.
“那么事情就这样。
You are probably aware that fuller’s-earth is a valuable product, and that it is only found in one or two places in England?’
你大概知道，白矾是一种珍贵的产品，只在英格兰的几个地方发现？
“‘I have heard so.’
“我听说过。”
“‘Some little time ago I bought a small place—a very small place—within ten miles of Reading.
“有些时间之前，我在读尔德附近买了一块小地方。
I was fortunate enough to discover that there was a deposit of fuller’s-earth in one of my fields.
我很幸运地发现我田地里有一笔全草土的积蓄。

On examining it, however, I found that this deposit was a comparatively small one, and that it formed a link between two very much larger ones upon the right and left—both of them, however, in the grounds of my neighbours.
仔细检查之后，我发现这积蓄是相当小的，而它与右和左的两处较大的积蓄之间，都是一条相当大的纽带，但它们都是邻人的地里。
These good people were absolutely ignorant that their land contained that which was quite as valuable as a gold-mine.
这些好人们完全不知道他们地里有那么珍贵的东西，就像一个金矿一样。
Naturally, it was to my interest to buy their land before they discovered its true value, but unfortunately I had no capital by which I could do this.
自然，为了买他们的地，以便在他们发现它的真正价值之前买邻人的地，我需要有足够的资本，但不幸的是我没有资本。

I took a few of my friends into the secret, however, and they suggested that we should quietly and secretly work our own little deposit and that in this way we should earn the money which would enable us to buy the neighbouring fields.
我和几位朋友秘密地分享了这个秘密，他们建议我们秘密地和秘密地工作我们的积蓄，这样我们就可以在这些邻人的地里买地。
This we have now been doing for some time, and in order to help us in our operations we erected a hydraulic press.
我们现在已经这样做了一段时间，并且为了帮助我们进行这些工作，我们已经建造了一台水力压榨机。
This press, as I have already explained, has got out of order, and we wish your advice upon the subject.
这台压榨机，正如我之前已经解释过的，已经出了毛病，我们希望您的建议关于这个问题。

We guard our secret very jealously, however, and if it once became known that we had hydraulic engineers coming to our little house, it would soon rouse inquiry, and then, if the facts came out, it would be good-bye to any chance of getting these fields and carrying out our plans.
我们非常谨慎地保护我们的秘密，如果有一天有人知道我们有水力工程师来到我们的小屋，很快就会引起询问，如果事实被揭露，那么，我们计划的任何机会就会消失。
That is why I have made you promise me that you will not tell a human being that you are going to Eyford to-night.
为什么我让你保证你今晚不会去埃弗德？
I hope that I make it all plain?’
我希望我解释得清楚吗？

“‘I quite follow you,’ said I. ‘The only point which I could not quite understand was what use you could make of a hydraulic press in excavating fuller’s-earth, which, as I understand, is dug out like gravel from a pit.’
““我完全理解你，唯一不能完全理解的是你如何利用水力压榨机挖掘全草土，这，正如我理解的，是像从坑里挖出来的沙子一样挖掘出来的。”
“‘Ah!’ said he carelessly, ‘we have our own process.
“啊！”他漫不经心地说，“我们有自己的方法。
We compress the earth into bricks, so as to remove them without revealing what they are.
我们把土压成砖，这样就可以不揭示它们是什么。
But that is a mere detail.
但这只是细节。
I have taken you fully into my confidence now, Mr. Hatherley, and I have shown you how I trust you.’
我现在已经把一切都告诉你了，赫特利先生，我也向你展示了我对你的信任。
He rose as he spoke.
他说话时站了起来。
‘I shall expect you, then, at Eyford at 11:15.’
“我将在11：15时到达伊弗福德。”
“‘I shall certainly be there.’
“‘我肯定会去的。’”
“‘And not a word to a soul.’
“‘而且，不和任何人说一句话。’”
He looked at me with a last long, questioning gaze, and then, pressing my hand in a cold, dank grasp, he hurried from the room.
他看着我，用最后的一次，带着疑问的目光，然后，用冰冷的，潮湿的手掌抓住我的手，他匆忙从房间里走了出去。
“Well, when I came to think it all over in cool blood I was very much astonished, as you may both think, at this sudden commission which had been intrusted to me.
“好了，当我冷静地思考这件事时，我非常惊讶，正如你们俩可以认为的那样，我突然被委托的任务。
On the one hand, of course, I was glad, for the fee was at least tenfold what I should have asked had I set a price upon my own services, and it was possible that this order might lead to other ones.
一方面，当然我很高兴，因为报酬至少是我要的十倍，而且可能这单任务会带来其他任务。

On the other hand, the face and manner of my patron had made an unpleasant impression upon me, and I could not think that his explanation of the fuller’s-earth was sufficient to explain the necessity for my coming at midnight, and his extreme anxiety lest I should tell anyone of my errand.
另一方面，我的主人的面孔和举止给我留下了不愉快的印象，我不能认为他的解释，即屠夫的草是足够的，来解释我必须在午夜到达的原因，以及他极端的担心，我不应该告诉任何人我的任务。
However, I threw all fears to the winds, ate a hearty supper, drove to Paddington, and started off, having obeyed to the letter the injunction as to holding my tongue.
无论如何，我抛开一切恐惧，吃了一顿饱饭，开车到皮卡迪利，然后出发，我完全遵守了不要说任何话的命令。
“At Reading I had to change not only my carriage but my station.
“在雷丁，我必须更换我的车和站。
However, I was in time for the last train to Eyford, and I reached the little dim-lit station after eleven o’clock.
但是，我赶上了最后一班到伊弗福德的列车，我在11点左右到达了小而昏暗的车站。
I was the only passenger who got out there, and there was no one upon the platform save a single sleepy porter with a lantern.
我是唯一一个下车的人，站台上除了一个睡着的行李员和一盏灯笼外，没有其他人。
As I passed out through the wicket gate, however, I found my acquaintance of the morning waiting in the shadow upon the other side.
当我穿过铁门时，我发现我早晨的熟人站在另一边的阴影中。
Without a word he grasped my arm and hurried me into a carriage, the door of which was standing open.
他一句话也没有说，就抓住我的手臂，把我带进了开着的车厢，门是开着的。
He drew up the windows on either side, tapped on the wood-work, and away we went as fast as the horse could go.”
他把窗户拉上，敲敲木头，我们就像坐上了马车一样飞驰而去。
“One horse?” interjected Holmes.
“只有一匹马？”霍尔姆斯插嘴道。
“Yes, only one.”
“是的，只有这一匹。”
“Did you observe the colour?”
“你注意到颜色了吗？”
“Yes, I saw it by the side-lights when I was stepping into the carriage.
“是的，我是在马车进站时看到的。
It was a chestnut.”
它是栗色的。”
“Tired-looking or fresh?”
“看起来疲倦还是新鲜？”
“Oh, fresh and glossy.”
“哦，新鲜又光泽。”
“Thank you.
“谢谢。
I am sorry to have interrupted you.
我很抱歉打断了你。
Pray continue your most interesting statement.”
希望你继续你的精彩描述。”
“Away we went then, and we drove for at least an hour.
“然后我们出发了，我们开了至少一小时。
Colonel Lysander Stark had said that it was only seven miles, but I should think, from the rate that we seemed to go, and from the time that we took, that it must have been nearer twelve.
萨克森上校说，那只有七英里，但我估计，从我们走的速度和所花的时间来看，应该是在十二英里左右。”
He sat at my side in silence all the time, and I was aware, more than once when I glanced in his direction, that he was looking at me with great intensity.
他始终坐在我的旁边，沉默地坐着，我多次在看他时，发现他目光炯炯。
The country roads seem to be not very good in that part of the world, for we lurched and jolted terribly.
那里的一些乡村道路看起来并不好，因为我们颠簸得厉害。
I tried to look out of the windows to see something of where we were, but they were made of frosted glass, and I could make out nothing save the occasional bright blur of a passing light.
我试图透过窗户看看我们所在的地方，但它们是用碎玻璃制成的，只能看到偶尔闪过的光亮。
Now and then I hazarded some remark to break the monotony of the journey, but the colonel answered only in monosyllables, and the conversation soon flagged.
不时地，我尝试着插话来打破旅途的单调，但上尉只用简单的几个字回答，谈话很快就停了下来。
At last, however, the bumping of the road was exchanged for the crisp smoothness of a gravel-drive, and the carriage came to a stand.
最后，路上的颠簸被沙石路的平稳所取代，马车停了下来。
Colonel Lysander Stark sprang out, and, as I followed after him, pulled me swiftly into a porch which gaped in front of us.
布莱克上尉跳了出来，我紧跟在他后面，拉着他进入一个敞开的门廊。
We stepped, as it were, right out of the carriage and into the hall, so that I failed to catch the most fleeting glance of the front of the house.
我们像跳出来一样，走进了大厅，以至于我没能捕捉到房子前部的最微小的一瞥。
The instant that I had crossed the threshold the door slammed heavily behind us, and I heard faintly the rattle of the wheels as the carriage drove away.
我刚跨过门槛，门就重重地关上了，我隐隐约约听到车轮的嘎吱声，马车驶离了。
“It was pitch dark inside the house, and the colonel fumbled about looking for matches and muttering under his breath.
“屋里漆黑一片，上尉摸索着找火柴，嘴里嘀咕着。
Suddenly a door opened at the other end of the passage, and a long, golden bar of light shot out in our direction.
突然，门廊的另一端打开，一束长长的金色光线射向我们。
It grew broader, and a woman appeared with a lamp in her hand, which she held above her head, pushing her face forward and peering at us.
这光线变得更亮了，一个女人出现了，手里拿着一盏灯，她举着灯，脸凑近，用眼睛看着我们。
I could see that she was pretty, and from the gloss with which the light shone upon her dark dress I knew that it was a rich material.
我可以看到她很漂亮，从灯光反射在她黑色衣服上的光泽，我知道那是一种昂贵的材料。
She spoke a few words in a foreign tongue in a tone as though asking a question, and when my companion answered in a gruff monosyllable she gave such a start that the lamp nearly fell from her hand.
她说了几句用外国语言的话，语气好像在问问题，我的同伴用单调的单音回答，她发出了一种惊叫，灯几乎从她的手中掉下来。
Colonel Stark went up to her, whispered something in her ear, and then, pushing her back into the room from whence she had come, he walked towards me again with the lamp in his hand.
布莱克上尉走到她身边，低声说了几句话，然后推她回到房间，从她离开的房间走过来，手里拿着灯。
“‘Perhaps you will have the kindness to wait in this room for a few minutes,’ said he, throwing open another door.
“也许你得在房间里等几分钟，”他说着打开了一扇门。
It was a quiet, little, plainly furnished room, with a round table in the centre, on which several German books were scattered.
这是一个安静的小房间，圆桌上散着几本德国书。
Colonel Stark laid down the lamp on the top of a harmonium beside the door.
布莱克上尉把灯放在门旁边的一架钢琴上。
‘I shall not keep you waiting an instant,’ said he, and vanished into the darkness.
我不会让你久等的，”他说道，然后消失在黑暗中。
“I glanced at the books upon the table, and in spite of my ignorance of German I could see that two of them were treatises on science, the others being volumes of poetry.
我瞥了一眼桌子上的书，尽管我对德语一无所知，但我还是能看出其中两本书是关于科学的，另外两本是诗集。
Then I walked across to the window, hoping that I might catch some glimpse of the country-side, but an oak shutter, heavily barred, was folded across it.
我走到窗前，希望我能捕捉到一些乡村的景象，但是一扇沉重的木窗被折叠在窗前。
It was a wonderfully silent house.
这是一间非常安静的房子。
There was an old clock ticking loudly somewhere in the passage, but otherwise everything was deadly still.
在走廊里，有一只古老的钟在响，但除此之外，一切都是死一般的寂静。
A vague feeling of uneasiness began to steal over me.
一种不安的感觉开始在我心中蔓延。
Who were these German people, and what were they doing living in this strange, out-of-the-way place?
这些德国人是谁，他们在这样一个奇怪、偏远的地方住着做什么？
And where was the place?
这个地方在哪里？
I was ten miles or so from Eyford, that was all I knew, but whether north, south, east, or west I had no idea.
我离伊弗福德大约有十英里远，这我知道，但我不知道是往哪个方向。
For that matter, Reading, and possibly other large towns, were within that radius, so the place might not be so secluded, after all.
例如，雷丁，以及可能的其他大城市，都在这个范围内，所以这个地方可能并不是那么偏远。
Yet it was quite certain, from the absolute stillness, that we were in the country.
从绝对的寂静中，我们确实是在农村。
I paced up and down the room, humming a tune under my breath to keep up my spirits and feeling that I was thoroughly earning my fifty-guinea fee.
我在房间里来回踱步，哼着一首曲子来保持我的精神，并觉得我完全值得五十先令的报酬。
“Suddenly, without any preliminary sound in the midst of the utter stillness, the door of my room swung slowly open.
“突然间，在一片死寂中，我的房间门缓缓打开。
The woman was standing in the aperture, the darkness of the hall behind her, the yellow light from my lamp beating upon her eager and beautiful face.
女人站在门缝里，黑暗的走廊后面是她的身影，我灯的黄色光线照在她渴望美丽而美丽的脸上。
I could see at a glance that she was sick with fear, and the sight sent a chill to my own heart.
我一眼就能看出她害怕得要命，看到这种情景，我的心里也感到一阵寒意。

She held up one shaking finger to warn me to be silent, and she shot a few whispered words of broken English at me, her eyes glancing back, like those of a frightened horse, into the gloom behind her.
她举起一根颤抖的手指，警告我保持沉默，她用破碎的英语低声对我说了几句话，她的目光像受惊的马一样，投向她身后黑暗的地方。
“‘I would go,’ said she, trying hard, as it seemed to me, to speak calmly; ‘I would go.
“‘我愿意去，’她说，似乎努力想冷静下来；‘我愿意去。
I should not stay here.
我不会留下来。”
There is no good for you to do.’
这对你没有好处。”
“‘But, madam,’ said I, ‘I have not yet done what I came for.
“‘但是，夫人，’我说，‘我还没有完成我来这里的任务。”
I cannot possibly leave until I have seen the machine.’
我不能离开，直到我看过机器。”
“‘It is not worth your while to wait,’ she went on.
“‘这不值得你等，’她继续说。”
‘You can pass through the door; no one hinders.’
“‘你可以通过门，没有人阻拦。”
And then, seeing that I smiled and shook my head, she suddenly threw aside her constraint and made a step forward, with her hands wrung together.
然后，看到我微笑着摇了摇头，她突然松开了约束，向前迈了一步，双手绞在一起。
‘For the love of Heaven!’ she whispered, ‘get away from here before it is too late!’
“为了天上的圣母，”她低声说，“快离开这里，否则太晚了！”
“But I am somewhat headstrong by nature, and the more ready to engage in an affair when there is some obstacle in the way.
“但是，我天生有些倔强，当有障碍时，我更愿意参与一场交易。
I thought of my fifty-guinea fee, of my wearisome journey, and of the unpleasant night which seemed to be before me.
我想到五十先令的报酬，艰难的旅程，以及即将到来的不愉快的夜晚。
Was it all to go for nothing?
这一切都值得吗？
Why should I slink away without having carried out my commission, and without the payment which was my due?
我为什么要偷偷溜走，没有履行我的任务，也没有应得的报酬？
This woman might, for all I knew, be a monomaniac.
这个女人可能只是个单相思。
With a stout bearing, therefore, though her manner had shaken me more than I cared to confess, I still shook my head and declared my intention of remaining where I was.
因为她举止摇摆，虽然我掩饰不住内心的震惊，但她仍然摇摇头，表示她要留在原地。
She was about to renew her entreaties when a door slammed overhead, and the sound of several footsteps was heard upon the stairs.
她正要重提请求时，头顶上砰地一声，楼梯上传来脚步声。
She listened for an instant, threw up her hands with a despairing gesture, and vanished as suddenly and as noiselessly as she had come.
她屏息凝神，双手一摊，绝望地消失，就像她来时一样迅速而无声。
“The newcomers were Colonel Lysander Stark and a short thick man with a chinchilla beard growing out of the creases of his double chin, who was introduced to me as Mr. Ferguson.
“新来的两位是克拉伦斯·斯图尔特上校和一个身材矮小、留着绒毛胡子的中年男子，他被介绍给我为弗格森先生。
“‘This is my secretary and manager,’ said the colonel.
“‘这是我的秘书和经理，’上校说。
‘By the way, I was under the impression that I left this door shut just now.
“‘顺便说一下，我刚才以为刚才把门关上了。
I fear that you have felt the draught.’
我怕你感到冷风。”
“‘On the contrary,’ said I, ‘I opened the door myself because I felt the room to be a little close.’
“‘恰恰相反，’我说，‘我开门是因为我觉得房间有点闷热。’
“He shot one of his suspicious looks at me.
“他对我投了一瞥可疑的目光。
‘Perhaps we had better proceed to business, then,’ said he.
“‘也许我们最好开始工作了，’他说。
‘Mr.
‘弗格森先生和我将带你去看机器。
Ferguson and I will take you up to see the machine.’
‘我最好戴上帽子，我猜吧？’
“‘I had better put my hat on, I suppose.’
“‘哦，不，就在屋里。’
“‘Oh, no, it is in the house.’
“‘你挖地三尺的工夫是在屋里吗？’
“‘What, you dig fuller’s-earth in the house?’
“‘挖地三尺的工夫是在屋里吗？’
“‘No, no.
"不，不。
This is only where we compress it.
这只是我们压缩的地方。
But never mind that.
但别管那。
All we wish you to do is to examine the machine and to let us know what is wrong with it.’
我们只是希望你仔细检查一下机器，告诉我们机器出了什么问题。"
“We went upstairs together, the colonel first with the lamp, the fat manager and I behind him.
"我们一起上楼，将军先拿手电筒，胖子经理和我随后。
It was a labyrinth of an old house, with corridors, passages, narrow winding staircases, and little low doors, the thresholds of which were hollowed out by the generations who had crossed them.
这是一幢老房子，有走廊、通道、狭窄的螺旋楼梯和低矮的小门，门槛都因几代人走过而被掏空。
There were no carpets and no signs of any furniture above the ground floor, while the plaster was peeling off the walls, and the damp was breaking through in green, unhealthy blotches.
没有地毯，也没有地面以上的家具，石膏剥落，墙壁发霉，绿色的、不健康的斑点。
I tried to put on as unconcerned an air as possible, but I had not forgotten the warnings of the lady, even though I disregarded them, and I kept a keen eye upon my two companions.
我尽量保持最不关心的样子，但没有忘记那位女士的警告，尽管我忽视了，我仍然时刻注意着我的两位同伴。
Ferguson appeared to be a morose and silent man, but I could see from the little that he said that he was at least a fellow-countryman.
Ferguson看起来是一个沉默寡言的人，但我从他所说的不多的几句话中可以看出，他至少是同乡。
“Colonel Lysander Stark stopped at last before a low door, which he unlocked.
"将军最后在低门前停下，他打开门。
Within was a small, square room, in which the three of us could hardly get at one time.
里面是一个小方房间，我们三个人不能同时进去。
Ferguson remained outside, and the colonel ushered me in.
Ferguson在外面，将军把我带进房间。
“‘We are now,’ said he, ‘actually within the hydraulic press, and it would be a particularly unpleasant thing for us if anyone were to turn it on.
"我们现在，"他说，"实际上是在液压机内，如果有人要启动它，那将是非常不愉快的事情。
The ceiling of this small chamber is really the end of the descending piston, and it comes down with the force of many tons upon this metal floor.
这个小房间的天花板实际上就是下降的活塞的末端，它以巨大的力量压在这个金属地板上。
There are small lateral columns of water outside which receive the force, and which transmit and multiply it in the manner which is familiar to you.
有小的水柱外侧，它们接收并传递这种力量，就像你们熟悉的那样。
The machine goes readily enough, but there is some stiffness in the working of it, and it has lost a little of its force.
这台机器运转得相当顺畅，但做工有些僵硬，力量也有所减弱。
Perhaps you will have the goodness to look it over and to show us how we can set it right.’
也许你会注意到它，让我们看看我们如何让它恢复正常。
“I took the lamp from him, and I examined the machine very thoroughly.
“我从他手中拿走了手电筒，仔细检查了这台机器。
It was indeed a gigantic one, and capable of exercising enormous pressure.
它确实是一个巨大的机器，能够承受巨大的压力。

When I passed outside, however, and pressed down the levers which controlled it, I knew at once by the whishing sound that there was a slight leakage, which allowed a regurgitation of water through one of the side cylinders.
当我离开机器旁，按下控制它的杠杆时，我立刻听到了吱吱的声响，我知道有一小部分水漏了出来，通过机器的一个侧缸。
An examination showed that one of the india-rubber bands which was round the head of a driving-rod had shrunk so as not quite to fill the socket along which it worked.
检查发现，一个橡胶环，圆着一个驱动杆，已经收缩，几乎填不满工作时的孔。

This was clearly the cause of the loss of power, and I pointed it out to my companions, who followed my remarks very carefully and asked several practical questions as to how they should proceed to set it right.
这显然是力量损失的原因，我指出了这一点，我的同伴们仔细听了我的话，并询问了如何修复它。
When I had made it clear to them, I returned to the main chamber of the machine and took a good look at it to satisfy my own curiosity.
当我向他们解释清楚后，我返回了机器的主室，仔细看了看，满足了自己的好奇心。
It was obvious at a glance that the story of the fuller’s-earth was the merest fabrication, for it would be absurd to suppose that so powerful an engine could be designed for so inadequate a purpose.
一眼看去，这个故事显然是胡编乱造的，因为这样强大的发动机怎么可能设计用于如此不切实际的目的。
The walls were of wood, but the floor consisted of a large iron trough, and when I came to examine it I could see a crust of metallic deposit all over it.
墙壁是木头的，但地板是由一个大型铁槽组成的，当我检查它时，可以看到整个金属沉积物。
I had stooped and was scraping at this to see exactly what it was when I heard a muttered exclamation in German and saw the cadaverous face of the colonel looking down at me.
我弯下腰，正在刮这个，听到一句德语的低语，看到那位尸骨般的将军俯视着我。
“‘What are you doing there?’ he asked.
“‘你在做什么？’他问道。
“I felt angry at having been tricked by so elaborate a story as that which he had told me.
“我对他被编造出如此复杂的谎言感到愤怒。
‘I was admiring your fuller’s-earth,’ said I; ‘I think that I should be better able to advise you as to your machine if I knew what the exact purpose was for which it was used.’
‘我正在欣赏你的‘更衣机’，’我说，‘我想如果我知道它被用来做什么，我会更好地建议你如何使用它。’
“The instant that I uttered the words I regretted the rashness of my speech.
我一开口，就后悔了。
His face set hard, and a baleful light sprang up in his grey eyes.
他面沉心寒，灰蓝色的眼睛里燃起了凶光。
“‘Very well,’ said he, ‘you shall know all about the machine.’
“‘很好，’他说道，‘你将知道机器的全部情况。’”
He took a step backward, slammed the little door, and turned the key in the lock.
他后退一步，关上了小门，然后转动了钥匙。
I rushed towards it and pulled at the handle, but it was quite secure, and did not give in the least to my kicks and shoves.
我冲了过去，拉住了把手，但门却很坚固，丝毫没有松动。
‘Hullo!’
I yelled.
我大叫。
‘Hullo!
Colonel!
“阁下！”
Let me out!’
“让我出来！”
“And then suddenly in the silence I heard a sound which sent my heart into my mouth.
“然后突然在寂静中我听到了一种声音，这声音使我心脏贴着喉咙。
It was the clank of the levers and the swish of the leaking cylinder.
这是机器的杠杆咔嚓声和漏油的铁管哗哗声。
He had set the engine at work.
他启动了引擎。
The lamp still stood upon the floor where I had placed it when examining the trough.
灯依然放在地板上，当我检查槽子时放上去的地方。
By its light I saw that the black ceiling was coming down upon me, slowly, jerkily, but, as none knew better than myself, with a force which must within a minute grind me to a shapeless pulp.
用灯光我看到黑色的天花板慢慢落下，缓慢而有节律地，但我知道，没有人比我自己更清楚，这种力在不到一分钟内将把我磨成肉泥。
I threw myself, screaming, against the door, and dragged with my nails at the lock.
我冲了过去，尖叫着，用指甲死命地拉住锁。
I implored the colonel to let me out, but the remorseless clanking of the levers drowned my cries.
我恳求上校放我出去，但沉重的杠杆声淹没了我的呼喊。
The ceiling was only a foot or two above my head, and with my hand upraised I could feel its hard, rough surface.
房顶离我的头顶只有几英尺，我抬起手就能感觉到它坚硬粗糙的表面。
Then it flashed through my mind that the pain of my death would depend very much upon the position in which I met it.
然后，这念头闪过我的脑海：死亡的痛苦将取决于我与它相遇的姿势。
If I lay on my face the weight would come upon my spine, and I shuddered to think of that dreadful snap.
如果我趴在地上，重量会压在我的脊椎上，我忍不住想那可怕的咔嚓声。
Easier the other way, perhaps; and yet, had I the nerve to lie and look up at that deadly black shadow wavering down upon me?
更容易的另一面，也许；但要是我有勇气躺下，抬头看那致命的黑色阴影悬在头顶上，又会怎样呢？
Already I was unable to stand erect, when my eye caught something which brought a gush of hope back to my heart.
我已经无法站直，当我眼睛捕捉到什么时，心中涌起一股希望。
“I have said that though the floor and ceiling were of iron, the walls were of wood.
“我已经说过，尽管地面和天花板都是铁制的，墙壁却是木头的。
As I gave a last hurried glance around, I saw a thin line of yellow light between two of the boards, which broadened and broadened as a small panel was pushed backward.
我最后匆匆瞥了一眼，看到两块木板之间有一条细线的黄色光，它逐渐变宽，直到一个小门被推开。
For an instant I could hardly believe that here was indeed a door which led away from death.
在我眼前出现了一扇门，似乎通往死亡之外。
The next instant I threw myself through, and lay half-fainting upon the other side.
突然间，我倒了下去，躺在另一边。
The panel had closed again behind me, but the crash of the lamp, and a few moments afterwards the clang of the two slabs of metal, told me how narrow had been my escape.
门板又关上了，但灯的撞击声和金属板的撞击声告诉我，我差点儿丧命。

“I was recalled to myself by a frantic plucking at my wrist, and I found myself lying upon the stone floor of a narrow corridor, while a woman bent over me and tugged at me with her left hand, while she held a candle in her right.
“我被一阵急切的抓挠我的手腕所唤醒，我发现自己躺在一条狭窄走廊的石地板上，一个女人俯身在我身上，用左手抓我，用右手拿着蜡烛。
It was the same good friend whose warning I had so foolishly rejected.
这是那个我如此粗心地拒绝警告的好朋友。
“‘Come! come!’ she cried breathlessly.
“‘来吧！来吧！’她喘着气喊道。
‘They will be here in a moment.
“他们马上就会来的。”
They will see that you are not there.
他们要看到你不在那里。
Oh, do not waste the so-precious time, but come!’
哦，不要浪费这如此珍贵的时间，快点来！
“This time, at least, I did not scorn her advice.
“这次，至少，我没有轻视她的建议。”
I staggered to my feet and ran with her along the corridor and down a winding stair.
我踉跄地站起身，和她沿着走廊跑，沿着蜿蜒的楼梯跑。

The latter led to another broad passage, and just as we reached it we heard the sound of running feet and the shouting of two voices, one answering the other from the floor on which we were and from the one beneath.
这条路通向另一个宽阔的通道，我们刚走到那里，就听到脚步声和两个人的喊叫，一个回答另一个，从我们脚下和我们下面的地板传来。
My guide stopped and looked about her like one who is at her wit’s end.
我的向导停下来，像一个无助的人一样四处张望。
Then she threw open a door which led into a bedroom, through the window of which the moon was shining brightly.
然后她打开了一扇门，通向一间卧室，透过窗户，月亮正照得很亮。
“‘It is your only chance,’ said she.
“‘这是你唯一的希望，’她说。”
‘It is high, but it may be that you can jump it.’
“它很高，但也许你可以跳过去。”

“As she spoke a light sprang into view at the further end of the passage, and I saw the lean figure of Colonel Lysander Stark rushing forward with a lantern in one hand and a weapon like a butcher’s cleaver in the other.
“她说话时，一个光亮出现在通道的另一端，我看到路易斯将军斯通瘦削的身影，手里拿着一盏灯笼，另一只手拿着像屠宰场的刀一样的武器。
I rushed across the bedroom, flung open the window, and looked out.
我冲过卧室，打开窗户，向外看去。
How quiet and sweet and wholesome the garden looked in the moonlight, and it could not be more than thirty feet down.
在月光下，花园看起来多么安静、甜美和健康，离地面只有三十多英尺。
I clambered out upon the sill, but I hesitated to jump until I should have heard what passed between my saviour and the ruffian who pursued me.
我爬到窗台上，但直到听到救我的人和追赶我的强盗之间的对话，我才决定跳下去。
If she were ill-used, then at any risks I was determined to go back to her assistance.
如果她受了虐待，那么为了任何风险，我都是决心回到她的帮助。
The thought had hardly flashed through my mind before he was at the door, pushing his way past her; but she threw her arms round him and tried to hold him back.
这个念头刚闪过我的脑海，他就推开了门，穿过她，但她抱着他，试图阻止他。
“‘Fritz!
“福尔摩斯！”
Fritz!’ she cried in English, ‘remember your promise after the last time.
“Fritz!”她用英语喊道，“记住上次后的诺言。”
You said it should not be again.
你说的不应当再这样了。
He will be silent!
他将保持沉默！
Oh, he will be silent!’
哦，他将保持沉默！
“‘You are mad, Elise!’ he shouted, struggling to break away from her.
“‘你发疯了，艾丽丝！’他大喊，试图挣脱她。
‘You will be the ruin of us.
你将毁掉我们。
He has seen too much.
他见多识广。
Let me pass, I say!’
请让我过去！
He dashed her to one side, and, rushing to the window, cut at me with his heavy weapon.
他把她推开一边，冲到窗前，用他的沉重武器向我猛砍。
I had let myself go, and was hanging by the hands to the sill, when his blow fell.
我放松了警惕，正靠在窗台上，这时他的一拳打过来。
I was conscious of a dull pain, my grip loosened, and I fell into the garden below.
我感到一阵钝痛，手被松开了，我掉进了下面的花园。
“I was shaken but not hurt by the fall; so I picked myself up and rushed off among the bushes as hard as I could run, for I understood that I was far from being out of danger yet.
我被摔得摇晃了一下，但没有受伤，于是我站起身来，冲向灌木丛，尽可能快地跑过去，因为我明白我还没有脱离危险。
Suddenly, however, as I ran, a deadly dizziness and sickness came over me.
然而，当我奔跑时，一种致命的眩晕和恶心突然袭来。
I glanced down at my hand, which was throbbing painfully, and then, for the first time, saw that my thumb had been cut off and that the blood was pouring from my wound.
我低头看了看自己的手，那手正剧烈地疼痛着，然后，第一次，我看到我的拇指被切掉，伤口的血液正从伤口里流出来。
I endeavoured to tie my handkerchief round it, but there came a sudden buzzing in my ears, and next moment I fell in a dead faint among the rose-bushes.
我试图把手帕系在上面，但突然间耳中传来嗡嗡声，下一刻我便在玫瑰丛中昏厥过去。
“How long I remained unconscious I cannot tell.
“我昏迷的时间有多久，我记不清了。”
It must have been a very long time, for the moon had sunk, and a bright morning was breaking when I came to myself.
必须是很久的时间，因为月亮已经沉下去了，黎明时分的天空才刚刚露出。
My clothes were all sodden with dew, and my coat-sleeve was drenched with blood from my wounded thumb.
我的衣服都湿透了，外套袖子也被我受伤的手指浸湿了。
The smarting of it recalled in an instant all the particulars of my night’s adventure, and I sprang to my feet with the feeling that I might hardly yet be safe from my pursuers.
这种疼痛让我立刻想起了整个夜晚的经历，我猛地站起身来，感觉自己的敌人可能还没放过我。
But to my astonishment, when I came to look round me, neither house nor garden were to be seen.
但令我惊讶的是，当我环顾四周时，连房子和花园都看不见了。

I had been lying in an angle of the hedge close by the high road, and just a little lower down was a long building, which proved, upon my approaching it, to be the very station at which I had arrived upon the previous night.
我躺在篱笆的一角，靠近那条主路，而稍低一点的地方有一栋长屋，证明我是在前一天晚上到达那里的。
Were it not for the ugly wound upon my hand, all that had passed during those dreadful hours might have been an evil dream.
如果不是手上有一道丑陋的伤口，这一切在那些可怕的时光里可能都只是个恶梦。
“Half dazed, I went into the station and asked about the morning train.
“半迷糊，我走进车站，向工作人员打听今天早上有哪趟列车。
There would be one to Reading in less than an hour.
一个小时后，就有列车到读城了。
The same porter was on duty, I found, as had been there when I arrived.
同一个工作人员，我后来发现，和我到达时一样，还在值班。
I inquired of him whether he had ever heard of Colonel Lysander Stark.
我问他是否听说过科特兰斯大佐。
The name was strange to him.
这个名字对他来说是陌生的。
Had he observed a carriage the night before waiting for me?
他是否注意到前一天晚上有一辆马车等在了我面前？
No, he had not.
不，他没有。
Was there a police-station anywhere near?
附近有没有警察局？
There was one about three miles off.
有，大约三英里外。
“It was too far for me to go, weak and ill as I was.
“我太虚弱了，身体也不好，走不了那么远。”
I determined to wait until I got back to town before telling my story to the police.
我决定等回到镇上再把事情告诉警察。
It was a little past six when I arrived, so I went first to have my wound dressed, and then the doctor was kind enough to bring me along here.
到了六点半，我到镇上去了，于是先去包扎伤口，然后医生过来把我带到这里。
I put the case into your hands and shall do exactly what you advise.”
我把事情交给你，你告诉我该怎么做。
We both sat in silence for some little time after listening to this extraordinary narrative.
我们俩听了这个非常奇怪的叙述之后，沉默了片刻。
Then Sherlock Holmes pulled down from the shelf one of the ponderous commonplace books in which he placed his cuttings.
罗素霍尔姆斯从书架上拉了一本厚实的剪报集，放在那里。
“Here is an advertisement which will interest you,” said he.
“这是个广告，对你很有兴趣。”他说。
“It appeared in all the papers about a year ago.
“一年前，它在报纸上刊登过。
Listen to this: ‘Lost, on the 9th inst., Mr. Jeremiah Hayling, aged twenty-six, a hydraulic engineer.
听听这个：‘丢失，9日，先生杰里米·哈林，26岁，水力工程师。
Left his lodgings at ten o’clock at night, and has not been heard of since.
他离开旅馆在晚上十点钟，之后就再没有听到他的消息。
Was dressed in,’ etc., etc. Ha!
他穿着，等等。哈！
That represents the last time that the colonel needed to have his machine overhauled, I fancy.”
那个代表上个月最后一次需要对机器进行保养，我想。”
“Good heavens!” cried my patient.
“天啊！”我的病人叫道。
“Then that explains what the girl said.”
那么，这就解释了那个女孩所说的。
“Undoubtedly.
当然。

It is quite clear that the colonel was a cool and desperate man, who was absolutely determined that nothing should stand in the way of his little game, like those out-and-out pirates who will leave no survivor from a captured ship.
从头到尾，这个老将军就是一个冷静而又决绝的人，他绝对决心不让任何事情阻挡住他那小小的计划，就像那些彻底的海盗会把俘虏的船只上的所有幸存者都杀死一样。
Well, every moment now is precious, so if you feel equal to it we shall go down to Scotland Yard at once as a preliminary to starting for Eyford.”
好吧，现在每分每秒都很宝贵，所以如果你觉得可以的话，我们现在就去苏格兰公墓，然后再去伊福德。
Some three hours or so afterwards we were all in the train together, bound from Reading to the little Berkshire village.
几个小时后，我们所有人都上了火车，从雷丁出发，去到伯克郡的小村庄。
There were Sherlock Holmes, the hydraulic engineer, Inspector Bradstreet, of Scotland Yard, a plain-clothes man, and myself.
有，水力工程师，苏格兰公墓的侦探，便衣警察，还有我。
Bradstreet had spread an ordnance map of the county out upon the seat and was busy with his compasses drawing a circle with Eyford for its centre.
铁路的座位上，布雷斯特正在用他的罗盘画一个以伊福德为中心的圆。
“There you are,” said he.
“你就是说的这个圆。”
“That circle is drawn at a radius of ten miles from the village.
“那圆是画在离村庄十英里远的地方的。
The place we want must be somewhere near that line.
我们要找的地方，必须在那个线附近。
You said ten miles, I think, sir.”
你说十英里，我猜的。
“It was an hour’s good drive.”
“那是一小时的车程。”
“And you think that they brought you back all that way when you were unconscious?”
“你认为他们把你带到这么远的地方，你昏迷的时候？”
“They must have done so.
“他们必须是这样做的。”
I have a confused memory, too, of having been lifted and conveyed somewhere.”
我也有点模糊的记忆，好像被抬起来，然后被带到某个地方。
“What I cannot understand,” said I, “is why they should have spared you when they found you lying fainting in the garden.
我不明白的是，他们为什么在发现你昏倒在花园里时没有放过你。
Perhaps the villain was softened by the woman’s entreaties.”
可能是因为那个坏蛋被女人的恳求所打动。
“I hardly think that likely.
我几乎认为不可能。
I never saw a more inexorable face in my life.”
我一生中从未见过一个更无情的面孔。
“Oh, we shall soon clear up all that,” said Bradstreet.
“哦，很快就会弄清楚的。”布雷斯特说。
“Well, I have drawn my circle, and I only wish I knew at what point upon it the folk that we are in search of are to be found.”
“好吧，我已经画了一个圈，我希望知道我们正在寻找的人在圈里什么地方。
“I think I could lay my finger on it,” said Holmes quietly.
“我认为我可以指出来。”夏洛克·霍尔平静地说。
“Really, now!” cried the inspector, “you have formed your opinion!
“真的吗？”检查员说，“你已经形成了自己的观点！
Come, now, we shall see who agrees with you.
来吧，现在我们看看谁会同意你的观点。
I say it is south, for the country is more deserted there.”
我说那是南方，因为那里的地方更荒凉。
“And I say east,” said my patient.
“我同意东方。”我的病人说。
“I am for west,” remarked the plain-clothes man.
“我同意西方。”穿制服的人说。
“There are several quiet little villages up there.”
“那里有几个安静的小村庄。”
“And I am for north,” said I, “because there are no hills there, and our friend says that he did not notice the carriage go up any.”
“我同意北方。”我说，“因为那里没有山丘，我们的朋友说他没有注意到车往哪里开。
“Come,” cried the inspector, laughing; “it’s a very pretty diversity of opinion.
“来吧，检查员笑着说，这真是一个非常多样化的意见。
We have boxed the compass among us.
我们已经把地图都画完了。
Who do you give your casting vote to?”
你投谁一票呢？
“You are all wrong.”
“你们都错了。”
“But we can’t all be.”
“但是我们不能都去。”
“Oh, yes, you can.
“哦，是的，你们可以去。
This is my point.”
这是我的观点。
He placed his finger in the centre of the circle.
他把手指放在圆圈的中心。
“This is where we shall find them.”
“这就是我们能找到他们的地方。”
“But the twelve-mile drive?” gasped Hatherley.
“但是十二英里路？”哈特莱尔惊叫道。
“Six out and six back.
“六人出去，六人回来。
Nothing simpler.
简单极了。
You say yourself that the horse was fresh and glossy when you got in.
你自己说，你一进马车时，马是新鲜的，光亮的。
How could it be that if it had gone twelve miles over heavy roads?”
你怎么可能说，如果它在重路上走了十二英里呢？
“Indeed, it is a likely ruse enough,” observed Bradstreet thoughtfully.
“当然，这是一条很合理的骗术。”布雷斯特思意味深长地说。
“Of course there can be no doubt as to the nature of this gang.”
“当然，这是一群人，这是一群人。”
“None at all,” said Holmes.
“全无此事，”福尔摩斯说道。
“They are coiners on a large scale, and have used the machine to form the amalgam which has taken the place of silver.”
它们是大型假币制造者，曾用机器制造汞合金来取代银。
“We have known for some time that a clever gang was at work,” said the inspector.
Inspector said, “我们已经知道有一伙聪明的歹徒在活动了一些时间。”
“They have been turning out half-crowns by the thousand.
他们正在大批量地铸造半硬币。
We even traced them as far as Reading, but could get no farther, for they had covered their traces in a way that showed that they were very old hands.
我们甚至追踪到雷丁，但还是无法进一步，因为他们掩盖了踪迹，这表明他们是老手。
But now, thanks to this lucky chance, I think that we have got them right enough.”
但如今，多亏了这次幸运的机遇，我想我们已经把他们认对了。
But the inspector was mistaken, for those criminals were not destined to fall into the hands of justice.
但警官却错了，那些罪犯并非注定落入法律的手中。

As we rolled into Eyford Station we saw a gigantic column of smoke which streamed up from behind a small clump of trees in the neighbourhood and hung like an immense ostrich feather over the landscape.
我们驶入伊弗福德车站时，看到一片巨大的烟柱从附近一小片树林后面升起，烟柱像巨大的鸵鸟羽毛一样笼罩着 landscape。
“A house on fire?” asked Bradstreet as the train steamed off again on its way.
“有房子着火了吗？”布雷德斯提问火车再次启动前行时说道。
“Yes, sir!” said the station-master.
“When did it break out?”
“何时爆发的？”
“I hear that it was during the night, sir, but it has got worse, and the whole place is in a blaze.”
我听见是在夜间发生的， sir，但情况变得更糟了，整个地方都在燃烧。
“Whose house is it?”
“这是哪一家的房子？”
“Dr. Becher’s.”
“贝彻医生的。”
“Tell me,” broke in the engineer, “is Dr. Becher a German, very thin, with a long, sharp nose?”
Tell me,”打断工程师说,“贝彻博士是德国人,身材瘦削,鼻梁高而尖?”
The station-master laughed heartily.
站长哈哈大笑。
“No, sir, Dr. Becher is an Englishman, and there isn’t a man in the parish who has a better-lined waistcoat.
“不，先生，博士贝彻是英国人，这个村庄里没有一个男人穿得比他更合身的马甲。
But he has a gentleman staying with him, a patient, as I understand, who is a foreigner, and he looks as if a little good Berkshire beef would do him no harm.”
但他的房间里住着一个病人，一个外国客人，看起来好像一点好布什里牛肉对他也没有坏处。”
The station-master had not finished his speech before we were all hastening in the direction of the fire.
站长还没说完，我们就急忙朝火场的方向走去。

The road topped a low hill, and there was a great widespread whitewashed building in front of us, spouting fire at every chink and window, while in the garden in front three fire-engines were vainly striving to keep the flames under.
路面在低丘上拐了个弯，前面是一大片白墙，冒着火光，窗户和门洞里都喷出火焰，而花园里有三辆消防车在努力控制火焰。
“That’s it!” cried Hatherley, in intense excitement.
“那才是呢！”赫特勒兴奋地叫道。
“There is the gravel-drive, and there are the rose-bushes where I lay.
“那是一条鹅卵石车道，那里是我躺的地方。
That second window is the one that I jumped from.”
那第二扇窗户是我跳下去的。”
“Well, at least,” said Holmes, “you have had your revenge upon them.
“好了，至少，”说霍尔姆斯，“你已经为他们报了仇。

There can be no question that it was your oil-lamp which, when it was crushed in the press, set fire to the wooden walls, though no doubt they were too excited in the chase after you to observe it at the time.
从那以后，没有人再提到过那个美丽的女人，那个阴险的德国人，或者那个忧郁的英国人。
Now keep your eyes open in this crowd for your friends of last night, though I very much fear that they are a good hundred miles off by now.”
现在，你得在人群中睁大眼睛寻找昨天的那些人，尽管我怀疑他们现在离这里已经有一百多英里了。
And Holmes’ fears came to be realised, for from that day to this no word has ever been heard either of the beautiful woman, the sinister German, or the morose Englishman.
现在，霍尔姆斯的恐惧变成了现实，从那以后，再也没有人提到过那个美丽的女人，那个阴险的德国人，或者那个忧郁的英国人。

Early that morning a peasant had met a cart containing several people and some very bulky boxes driving rapidly in the direction of Reading, but there all traces of the fugitives disappeared, and even Holmes’ ingenuity failed ever to discover the least clue as to their whereabouts.
那天早上，一个农夫遇见一辆载着几个人和一些非常笨重的箱子的马车，正在朝读物驶去，但那里的痕迹已经消失，连霍尔姆斯的智慧也无法发现他们藏身的地方。
The firemen had been much perturbed at the strange arrangements which they had found within, and still more so by discovering a newly severed human thumb upon a window-sill of the second floor.
夕阳西下，他们终于成功地控制了火焰，但没有在屋顶倒塌之前，整个地方都被烧毁，只剩下一些扭曲的管子和铁管，没有留下机器的任何痕迹，这机器是我们的不幸的同伴花了很大代价建造的。

About sunset, however, their efforts were at last successful, and they subdued the flames, but not before the roof had fallen in, and the whole place been reduced to such absolute ruin that, save some twisted cylinders and iron piping, not a trace remained of the machinery which had cost our unfortunate acquaintance so dearly.
然而，太阳落山时，他们的努力终于成功了，但未能阻止屋顶坍塌，整个地方被彻底破坏，只剩下一些扭曲的管子和铁管，这些管子和铁管是他们不幸的同伴花费了大量代价才建造的。

Large masses of nickel and of tin were discovered stored in an out-house, but no coins were to be found, which may have explained the presence of those bulky boxes which have been already referred to.
大块的镍和锡被发现储存在一个棚子里，但没有发现硬币，这可能解释了那些体积庞大的箱子的存在。

How our hydraulic engineer had been conveyed from the garden to the spot where he recovered his senses might have remained forever a mystery were it not for the soft mould, which told us a very plain tale.
如若液压工程师是从花园被带到那个地方恢复知觉的，那这个谜团就永远无法解开，但若不是，软泥告诉我们一个非常清晰的真相。
He had evidently been carried down by two persons, one of whom had remarkably small feet and the other unusually large ones.
他显然是被两个人带下来的，其中一个人的脚特别小，另一个人的脚特别大。
On the whole, it was most probable that the silent Englishman, being less bold or less murderous than his companion, had assisted the woman to bear the unconscious man out of the way of danger.
总的来说，沉默的英国人，比他的同伴更胆小或更凶残，很可能帮助女人把那个不省人事的人从危险中带了出来。
“Well,” said our engineer ruefully as we took our seats to return once more to London, “it has been a pretty business for me!
“嗯，”工程师苦笑道，当我们再次回到伦敦时，说，“这对我来说真是个不错的生意！
I have lost my thumb and I have lost a fifty-guinea fee, and what have I gained?”
我的手指和我丢失的五十先令都丢了，我得到了什么？”
“Experience,” said Holmes, laughing.
“经验”，说霍尔姆斯，笑着，“间接地也许有价值，你知道，你只要把话说出来，就能赢得你一生中成为优秀同伴的声誉。”
“Indirectly it may be of value, you know; you have only to put it into words to gain the reputation of being excellent company for the remainder of your existence.”
“间接地说，也许对你有用。你只要把话说出来，就能赢得你余生的优秀社交声誉。”

ch.et: X. The Adventure of the Noble Bachelor
ch.zt: 第十篇 · 单身贵族案
p: The Lord St. Simon marriage, and its curious termination, have long ceased to be a subject of interest in those exalted circles in which the unfortunate bridegroom moves.
塞尔蒙大主婚事，以及它的奇特结局，早已不为世人所关注，尤其是在那些不幸新娘子活动的尊贵圈子里。
Fresh scandals have eclipsed it, and their more piquant details have drawn the gossips away from this four-year-old drama.
新闻事件接踵而至，遮盖了它，而那些更引人注目的细节又将八卦人士引开了，对这四年前的戏剧。

As I have reason to believe, however, that the full facts have never been revealed to the general public, and as my friend Sherlock Holmes had a considerable share in clearing the matter up, I feel that no memoir of him would be complete without some little sketch of this remarkable episode.
作为我所知道的，此事的全部事实从未向公众公开过，而我朋友夏洛克·福尔摩斯在其中扮演了相当重要的角色，因此，我感觉，没有对他的某些简要描述，他的传记将不完整。

It was a few weeks before my own marriage, during the days when I was still sharing rooms with Holmes in Baker Street, that he came home from an afternoon stroll to find a letter on the table waiting for him.
几周前我的婚礼，是在我与福尔摩斯先生同住的贝克街的那几天，他从下午散步回来，发现桌上有一封信等着他。

I had remained indoors all day, for the weather had taken a sudden turn to rain, with high autumnal winds, and the jezail bullet which I had brought back in one of my limbs as a relic of my Afghan campaign throbbed with dull persistence.
我整天待在家里，因为天气突然变雨，秋风凛冽，我带来的阿富汗战役中的一枚弹片仍然在痛。

With my body in one easy-chair and my legs upon another, I had surrounded myself with a cloud of newspapers until at last, saturated with the news of the day, I tossed them all aside and lay listless, watching the huge crest and monogram upon the envelope upon the table and wondering lazily who my friend’s noble correspondent could be.
我坐在一个易拉椅上，腿放在另一个，我周围环绕着一堆报纸，直到最后，我被这一天的新闻所饱和，我扔掉了所有报纸，躺下懒洋洋地，看着桌上大号和字母标志的信封，想着我的朋友的高贵的信件来自谁。
“Here is a very fashionable epistle,” I remarked as he entered.
“这是封很时髦的信件，”我边说边进屋。
“Your morning letters, if I remember right, were from a fish-monger and a tide-waiter.”
“你的早晨信件，如果我记得对的话，是从一个鱼贩和一个潮汐守望者那里来的。”
“Yes, my correspondence has certainly the charm of variety,” he answered, smiling, “and the humbler are usually the more interesting.
“是的，我的信件确实有变化多端的趣味，而更卑微的往往更有趣。
This looks like one of those unwelcome social summonses which call upon a man either to be bored or to lie.”
这看起来像是一个不受欢迎的社会邀请，要么让人无聊，要么撒谎。
He broke the seal and glanced over the contents.
他解开信封，浏览了一下内容。
“Oh, come, it may prove to be something of interest, after all.”
“哦，来，也许会有些有趣的东西。”
“Not social, then?”
“不是社交的，是吗？”
“No, distinctly professional.”
“没有，完全专业。”
“And from a noble client?”
“从一位高贵的客户那里？”
“One of the highest in England.”
“英格兰最高的。”
“My dear fellow, I congratulate you.”
“亲爱的朋友，我祝贺你。”
“I assure you, Watson, without affectation, that the status of my client is a matter of less moment to me than the interest of his case.
“我保证，华生先生，坦率地，对于我的客户的地位对我来说，比他案件的利害关系小得多。”
It is just possible, however, that that also may not be wanting in this new investigation.
“然而，也许也未必没有这一点在新调查中。”
You have been reading the papers diligently of late, have you not?”
“你最近认真地阅读报纸了吗？”
“It looks like it,” said I ruefully, pointing to a huge bundle in the corner.
“我遗憾地指着角落里的一大堆说：‘是的，’我叹口气，‘那是的，’我指指一个大包，‘你也许可以寄给我。”
“I have had nothing else to do.”
“我没有什么事可做。”
“It is fortunate, for you will perhaps be able to post me up.
“幸运的是，你也许可以寄给我。”
I read nothing except the criminal news and the agony column.
“我只读刑事新闻和痛苦的专栏。”
The latter is always instructive.
“后者总是很有教育意义。”
