But if you have followed recent events so closely you must have read about Lord St. Simon and his wedding?”
“但是，如果你最近事件如此认真地阅读，你一定读到过斯蒂芬逊伯爵和他的婚礼吧？”
“Oh, yes, with the deepest interest.”
“哦，是的，很感兴趣。”
“That is well.
“很好。”
The letter which I hold in my hand is from Lord St. Simon.
“我手里的信是斯蒂芬逊伯爵的。”
I will read it to you, and in return you must turn over these papers and let me have whatever bears upon the matter.
“我读给你听，你必须翻过这些文件，让我知道与这件事有关的任何东西。”
This is what he says:
这是他说的。
“‘MY DEAR MR.

St. Simon 似乎没有放松他的态度，只是皱着眉头，紧闭着嘴唇，耐心地听完了这个长篇叙述。
“Excuse me,” he said, “but it is not my custom to discuss my most intimate personal affairs in this public manner.”
“对不起，”他说，“但这是我的习惯，不讨论我最私人的事情在公共场合。”
“Then you won’t forgive me?
“那你不会原谅我吗？
You won’t shake hands before I go?”
你不会握手离开吗？
“Oh, certainly, if it would give you any pleasure.”
“哦，当然，如果你觉得愉快的话。”
He put out his hand and coldly grasped that which she extended to him.
他伸出手，冷冷地握住她递过来的手。
“I had hoped,” suggested Holmes, “that you would have joined us in a friendly supper.”
“我希望，”霍尔姆斯建议，“你愿意和我们一起在友好的晚餐中。”
“I think that there you ask a little too much,” responded his Lordship.
“我想你要求太多了，”他的主人回应。
“I may be forced to acquiesce in these recent developments, but I can hardly be expected to make merry over them.
“我可能被迫接受这些最近的发展，但我很难期待在这些事情上开心。
I think that with your permission I will now wish you all a very good-night.”
我希望你同意，我现在要向你道晚安。”
He included us all in a sweeping bow and stalked out of the room.
他向我们所有人做了个大礼，然后走出了房间。
“Then I trust that you at least will honour me with your company,” said Sherlock Holmes.
“那么，我希望你至少会赏光陪我一回，”夏洛克·福尔摩斯说道。

“It is always a joy to meet an American, Mr. Moulton, for I am one of those who believe that the folly of a monarch and the blundering of a minister in far-gone years will not prevent our children from being some day citizens of the same world-wide country under a flag which shall be a quartering of the Union Jack with the Stars and Stripes.”
“我一向认为，美国佬是件乐事，因为我觉得，一个君主的愚蠢和大臣的失误，不会阻止我们的孩子有一天成为世界公民，旗上半旗半星条旗。”

“The case has been an interesting one,” remarked Holmes when our visitors had left us, “because it serves to show very clearly how simple the explanation may be of an affair which at first sight seems to be almost inexplicable.
“这个案子确实很有趣，因为这清楚地表明，一个看起来几乎不可解释的事情，其实可能非常简单。”
Nothing could be more natural than the sequence of events as narrated by this lady, and nothing stranger than the result when viewed, for instance, by Mr. Lestrade of Scotland Yard.”
这位女士叙述的事件，从头到尾都显得非常自然，而当从苏格兰场的侦探先生的角度来看时，结果却显得非常奇怪。
“You were not yourself at fault at all, then?”
“你不是自己有错吗？”

“From the first, two facts were very obvious to me, the one that the lady had been quite willing to undergo the wedding ceremony, the other that she had repented of it within a few minutes of returning home.
“从头到尾，我看得出，这位女士非常愿意参加婚礼仪式，另外，她也后悔了，仅仅几分钟后就回家了。”
Obviously something had occurred during the morning, then, to cause her to change her mind.
显然，事情在早上发生了，才导致她改变了主意。
What could that something be?
什么能是？
She could not have spoken to anyone when she was out, for she had been in the company of the bridegroom.
她不可能在出门时跟任何人说话，因为她在新郎的陪伴下。
Had she seen someone, then?
她是不是看到过什么人？

If she had, it must be someone from America because she had spent so short a time in this country that she could hardly have allowed anyone to acquire so deep an influence over her that the mere sight of him would induce her to change her plans so completely.
如果她看到过，那么，这个人必须是美国人，因为她在这一国家逗留的时间太短，不可能让任何人对她产生如此深的影响，以至于看到他就会改变她完全的计划。
You see we have already arrived, by a process of exclusion, at the idea that she might have seen an American.
既然我们已经排除了其他可能性，那么，她可能看到过一个美国人。
Then who could this American be, and why should he possess so much influence over her?
那么，这个人是谁，为什么他会对她有如此大的影响？
It might be a lover; it might be a husband.
他可能是她的爱人，也可能是她的丈夫。
Her young womanhood had, I knew, been spent in rough scenes and under strange conditions.
我知道，她年轻的时候，是在粗野的场景和奇怪的条件下度过的。
So far I had got before I ever heard Lord St. Simon’s narrative.
到目前为止，我之前从未听过关于斯蒂芬逊伯爵的叙述。

When he told us of a man in a pew, of the change in the bride’s manner, of so transparent a device for obtaining a note as the dropping of a bouquet, of her resort to her confidential maid, and of her very significant allusion to claim-jumping—which in miners’ parlance means taking possession of that which another person has a prior claim to—the whole situation became absolutely clear.
他向我们讲述了在圣堂里坐着的人，新娘的举止改变，透明到极点的获取便条的方法，对她的密友的求助，以及她对声称跳租的非常明显的暗示——在矿工的术语中，意思是抢占他人的先占权——整个情况变得完全清晰。
She had gone off with a man, and the man was either a lover or was a previous husband—the chances being in favour of the latter.”
她和一个男人一起离开了，这个男人要么是一个情人，要么是一个前夫——可能性更大是后者。”
“And how in the world did you find them?”
“你是怎么找到他们的？”
“It might have been difficult, but friend Lestrade held information in his hands the value of which he did not himself know.
“可能很难，但朋友莱斯特德手里有信息的价值，他自己并不知道。”
The initials were, of course, of the highest importance, but more valuable still was it to know that within a week he had settled his bill at one of the most select London hotels.”
当然，这些都是非常重要的，但更重要的是要知道在一周内他已结清了在伦敦最精选的酒店的账单。”
“How did you deduce the select?”
“你是怎么得出精选的？”
“By the select prices.
“通过精选的价格。”
Eight shillings for a bed and eightpence for a glass of sherry pointed to one of the most expensive hotels.
八先令八便士的床和八便士的酒杯，指向了最昂贵的酒店。
There are not many in London which charge at that rate.
在伦敦没有那么多的酒店，以这种价格。

In the second one which I visited in Northumberland Avenue, I learned by an inspection of the book that Francis H. Moulton, an American gentleman, had left only the day before, and on looking over the entries against him, I came upon the very items which I had seen in the duplicate bill.
在北诺斯盖支大道我参观的第二处，我通过查看那本书得知，美国绅士弗朗西斯·H·莫尔顿前一天才刚离开，翻阅他的账目时，我发现的那些项目正是我在副本账单上看到过的。

His letters were to be forwarded to 226 Gordon Square; so thither I travelled, and being fortunate enough to find the loving couple at home, I ventured to give them some paternal advice and to point out to them that it would be better in every way that they should make their position a little clearer both to the general public and to Lord St. Simon in particular.
他的信件要寄到226戈登广场；因此我前往那里，幸运的是找到了这对热恋中的夫妇，我冒昧地给他们提了一些父辈的建议，并指出他们应该使他们的处境更清楚，对公众和斯蒂芬逊伯爵来说尤其如此。
I invited them to meet him here, and, as you see, I made him keep the appointment.”
我邀请他们在这里会面，并，正如你所见，我让他保持预约。”
“But with no very good result,” I remarked.
“但结果并不很好，”我评论道。
“His conduct was certainly not very gracious.”
“他的行为显然并不很礼貌。”
“Ah, Watson,” said Holmes, smiling, “perhaps you would not be very gracious either, if, after all the trouble of wooing and wedding, you found yourself deprived in an instant of wife and of fortune.
“啊，华生，”夏洛克·霍尔姆斯微笑着说道，“也许你也不会对我如此客气，如果在一切努力之后，你发现自己在瞬间失去了妻子和财富。”
I think that we may judge Lord St. Simon very mercifully and thank our stars that we are never likely to find ourselves in the same position.
我认为我们可以很公正地看待圣·盛公爵，并感谢上苍我们永远不会遇到类似的情况。
Draw your chair up and hand me my violin, for the only problem we have still to solve is how to while away these bleak autumnal evenings.”
跟我过来，帮我拉椅子，给我我的小提琴，因为我们唯一要解决的问题就是如何在这寒冷的秋季夜晚消磨时光。”

ch.et: XI. The Adventure of the Beryl Coronet
ch.zt: 第十一篇 · 绿玉皇冠案
p: “Holmes,” said I as I stood one morning in our bow-window looking down the street, “here is a madman coming along.
"福尔摩斯先生，" 我站在窗前，望着街上的人，说，“有个疯子正朝这里走来。”
It seems rather sad that his relatives should allow him to come out alone.”
“看来他的亲戚们让他一个人出来很不开心。”我的朋友懒洋洋地从椅子上站起来，穿着大衣的口袋里掏出手帕，看着我的肩膀。
My friend rose lazily from his armchair and stood with his hands in the pockets of his dressing-gown, looking over my shoulder.
他是个五十多岁的人，高大，肥胖，威严，穿着黑色的长袍，闪闪发光的帽子，整洁的棕色长裤，和剪裁得体的浅灰色长裤。
It was a bright, crisp February morning, and the snow of the day before still lay deep upon the ground, shimmering brightly in the wintry sun.
那是明亮而寒冷的二月早晨，前一天的雪仍然覆盖在地面上，闪耀着在冬天的阳光下。
Down the centre of Baker Street it had been ploughed into a brown crumbly band by the traffic, but at either side and on the heaped-up edges of the footpaths it still lay as white as when it fell.
在巴克街的中心，它已经被交通碾成了一块棕色的碎块，但在两侧和路缘上，它仍然像下雪时一样白。
The grey pavement had been cleaned and scraped, but was still dangerously slippery, so that there were fewer passengers than usual.
灰色的路面已经清洁和刮平，但仍然非常滑，所以乘客比平时少。
Indeed, from the direction of the Metropolitan Station no one was coming save the single gentleman whose eccentric conduct had drawn my attention.
真的，从通往曼彻斯特站的方向，没有人来，除了那个古怪的行为吸引了我的注意的人。
He was a man of about fifty, tall, portly, and imposing, with a massive, strongly marked face and a commanding figure.
他是个五十多岁的人，高大，肥胖，威严，穿着黑色的长袍，闪闪发光的帽子，整洁的棕色长裤，和剪裁得体的浅灰色长裤。
He was dressed in a sombre yet rich style, in black frock-coat, shining hat, neat brown gaiters, and well-cut pearl-grey trousers.
他穿着一种古怪的对比，他的衣服和相貌显得很不协调，因为他正在跑步，偶尔发出轻微的弹簧，就像一个不太习惯跑步的人，对腿的负担感到厌倦。

Yet his actions were in absurd contrast to the dignity of his dress and features, for he was running hard, with occasional little springs, such as a weary man gives who is little accustomed to set any tax upon his legs.
他跑着，用手抓着，扭着头，把脸扭成最奇怪的扭曲。
As he ran he jerked his hands up and down, waggled his head, and writhed his face into the most extraordinary contortions.
“他到底在看什么？”我问道。
“What on earth can be the matter with him?”
“他正在看房子的数字。”福尔摩斯说，搓着他的手。
I asked.
“我确信他要来这儿。”福尔摩斯说，搓着他的手。
“He is looking up at the numbers of the houses.”
他正抬头望着房屋的数字。
“I believe that he is coming here,” said Holmes, rubbing his hands.
“我相信他要来，”华生说，搓搓手。
“Here?”
“这里？”
“Yes; I rather think he is coming to consult me professionally.
Yes; 我倒觉得他可能是来向我专业咨询的。
I think that I recognise the symptoms.
我认为我认出了症状。
Ha! did I not tell you?”
哈！我不是已经告诉你了吗？
As he spoke, the man, puffing and blowing, rushed at our door and pulled at our bell until the whole house resounded with the clanging.
他说着，那人喘着气，吹着口哨，冲向我们的门，拉扯我们的铃铛，直到整个房子都回荡着铃铛的叮当声。
A few moments later he was in our room, still puffing, still gesticulating, but with so fixed a look of grief and despair in his eyes that our smiles were turned in an instant to horror and pity.
几秒钟后，他已进入我们的房间，仍然喘着粗气，仍然挥动着手臂，但眼睛里充满了如此固定绝望的悲哀和绝望，使我们瞬间的笑容转为 horror 和 pity 。
For a while he could not get his words out, but swayed his body and plucked at his hair like one who has been driven to the extreme limits of his reason.
一时他无法说出话来，摇晃着身体，揪着头发，像一个已经被逼到理智极限的人。
Then, suddenly springing to his feet, he beat his head against the wall with such force that we both rushed upon him and tore him away to the centre of the room.
然后，他突然跳起身来，用如此巨大的力量撞击墙壁，以致我们都冲上前把他拉到房间中央。
Sherlock Holmes pushed him down into the easy-chair and, sitting beside him, patted his hand and chatted with him in the easy, soothing tones which he knew so well how to employ.
福尔摩斯推他坐到安乐椅里，自己则坐在他身边，拍着他的手，用他那熟悉得能驾轻就熟地运用的亲切柔和的语气跟他聊天。
“You have come to me to tell your story, have you not?” said he.
“你来告诉我你的故事，不是吗？”他说道。
“You are fatigued with your haste.
你因急躁已疲倦了。
Pray wait until you have recovered yourself, and then I shall be most happy to look into any little problem which you may submit to me.”
祈请稍待你恢复过来，然后我将非常乐意为你提交的任何小问题提供解答。
The man sat for a minute or more with a heaving chest, fighting against his emotion.
那人坐了片刻，胸口起伏，极力抑制自己的感情。
Then he passed his handkerchief over his brow, set his lips tight, and turned his face towards us.
然后他擦了擦额角，紧闭嘴唇，转过脸来对着我们。
“No doubt you think me mad?” said he.
“你一定以为我发疯了？”他说道。
“I see that you have had some great trouble,” responded Holmes.
“我看你遇到了极大的麻烦了，” Holmes 回答。
“God knows I have!—a trouble which is enough to unseat my reason, so sudden and so terrible is it.
上帝知道我有过！——一个足以使我精神崩溃的麻烦，如此突然而如此可怕。
Public disgrace I might have faced, although I am a man whose character has never yet borne a stain.
公之 disgrace 我也许得面对，虽然我是个从未玷污人格的人。
Private affliction also is the lot of every man; but the two coming together, and in so frightful a form, have been enough to shake my very soul.
私人的痛苦也是每个男人都会遭遇的；但两者一起到来，而且是以如此可怕的形态，已经足以动摇我的心灵。
Besides, it is not I alone.
此外，这并非我一人之不幸。
The very noblest in the land may suffer unless some way be found out of this horrible affair.”
大地上的最崇高人物也可能受害除非找到某种办法解决这件可怕的事。
“Pray compose yourself, sir,” said Holmes, “and let me have a clear account of who you are and what it is that has befallen you.”
请镇定，先生，”福尔摩斯说，“然后让我清楚地知道你是谁，发生了什么事。”
“My name,” answered our visitor, “is probably familiar to your ears.
我的名字，”我们的访客回答说，“可能已经熟悉到您的耳朵了。”
I am Alexander Holder, of the banking firm of Holder & Stevenson, of Threadneedle Street.”
我是阿瑟克斯勒，霍尔斯特与辛普森银行的阿瑟克斯勒，-threadneedle街。
The name was indeed well known to us as belonging to the senior partner in the second largest private banking concern in the City of London.
这个名字 indeed 已经是我们所熟悉的，因为它属于伦敦市中心第二大私人银行集团的第二大股东。
What could have happened, then, to bring one of the foremost citizens of London to this most pitiable pass?
伦敦最有名望的市民中，怎么会有一个落到如此悲惨的地步？
We waited, all curiosity, until with another effort he braced himself to tell his story.
我们静候着，满怀着好奇，直到他又费力地挺起身子来讲述他的故事。
“I feel that time is of value,” said he; “that is why I hastened here when the police inspector suggested that I should secure your co-operation.
我说：“我觉得时间是有价值的，所以当警察 inspector 建议我寻求你合作时，我便急忙赶来了。
I came to Baker Street by the Underground and hurried from there on foot, for the cabs go slowly through this snow.
我乘地铁来到贝克街，然后步行赶到，因为这雪使出租车走得非常慢。
That is why I was so out of breath, for I am a man who takes very little exercise.
那是我喘得厉害的原因，因为我是个很少运动的人。
I feel better now, and I will put the facts before you as shortly and yet as clearly as I can.
我现在感觉好多了，我会尽可能清晰地把事实告诉你们。

“It is, of course, well known to you that in a successful banking business as much depends upon our being able to find remunerative investments for our funds as upon our increasing our connection and the number of our depositors.
“当然，对于你们来说，成功的银行业务很大程度上取决于我们能够找到回报率高的投资，以及扩大与存款人的关系和存款数量。
One of our most lucrative means of laying out money is in the shape of loans, where the security is unimpeachable.
我们在这一方面做得相当好，最近几年来，我们已经为许多大名鼎鼎的家族提供了巨额贷款，这些贷款的担保是无可挑剔的。
We have done a good deal in this direction during the last few years, and there are many noble families to whom we have advanced large sums upon the security of their pictures, libraries, or plate.
“在过去的几年里，我们在这方面做得相当好，有很多大名鼎鼎的家族向我们提供了巨额贷款，这些贷款的担保是他们的画作、图书馆或餐具。
“Yesterday morning I was seated in my office at the bank when a card was brought in to me by one of the clerks.
“昨天早上，我在银行的办公室里坐着，一个职员递给我一张名片。

I started when I saw the name, for it was that of none other than—well, perhaps even to you I had better say no more than that it was a name which is a household word all over the earth—one of the highest, noblest, most exalted names in England.
当我看到名字时，我感到很震惊，因为这名字是世界上无人不知的，是英国最尊贵、最高尚、最崇高名字之一。
I was overwhelmed by the honour and attempted, when he entered, to say so, but he plunged at once into business with the air of a man who wishes to hurry quickly through a disagreeable task.
我被这种荣誉所震撼，试图表达出来，但他立刻开始做生意，好像他希望尽快完成一项令人不快的任务。
“‘Mr.
“‘先生，’他说，‘我听说你们在习惯上会提供资金。’
Holder,’ said he, ‘I have been informed that you are in the habit of advancing money.’
“‘我们公司会这样做，只要担保是好的。’
“‘The firm does so when the security is good.’
我回答。
I answered.
“‘我必须立即得到50,000英镑。’
“‘It is absolutely essential to me,’ said he, ‘that I should have £ 50,000 at once.
我当然可以向我的朋友借这么小的金额十倍，但我更愿意把它作为一项生意来做，我自己来完成这项生意。
I could, of course, borrow so trifling a sum ten times over from my friends, but I much prefer to make it a matter of business and to carry out that business myself.
在我的位置上，你们可以很容易理解，把自己置于义务之下是不明智的。
In my position you can readily understand that it is unwise to place one’s self under obligations.’
“‘为了什么期限，我可以问，’他说。
“‘For how long, may I ask, do you want this sum?’
“‘我必须立即得到50,000英镑。’
I asked.
我问了。
“‘Next Monday I have a large sum due to me, and I shall then most certainly repay what you advance, with whatever interest you think it right to charge.
“下周星期一我有一笔大额款项到期，那时我一定偿还你垫付的款项，加收你认为合适的利息。”
But it is very essential to me that the money should be paid at once.’
但是马上付钱对我非常重要。
“‘I should be happy to advance it without further parley from my own private purse,’ said I, ‘were it not that the strain would be rather more than it could bear.
‘我可以从自己的私人 purse 中借给你，’我说道，‘只是怕它承受不了太大的压力。’
If, on the other hand, I am to do it in the name of the firm, then in justice to my partner I must insist that, even in your case, every businesslike precaution should be taken.’
如果，反之，我要是以公司的名义去做的话，那么为了对我的合伙人公正起见，我必须坚持，在即使是你的情况下，也应该采取一切商务上的谨慎措施。
“‘I should much prefer to have it so,’ said he, raising up a square, black morocco case which he had laid beside his chair.
‘我宁愿这样处理，’他说道，举起旁边椅子旁的一个方形黑羊皮信封装了起来。
‘You have doubtless heard of the Beryl Coronet?’
‘你或许听说过贝里尔王冠?’
“‘One of the most precious public possessions of the empire,’ said I.
‘帝国最珍贵的公有财产之一，’我说。
“‘Precisely.’
‘精确如此。’
He opened the case, and there, imbedded in soft, flesh-coloured velvet, lay the magnificent piece of jewellery which he had named.
他打开箱子，里面，嵌在柔软的肉色丝绒中，躺着那件他命名为 magnificent 的精美珠宝。
‘There are thirty-nine enormous beryls,’ said he, ‘and the price of the gold chasing is incalculable.
The lowest estimate would put the worth of the coronet at double the sum which I have asked.
最低估计会将冠冕的价值估算为我所求金额的两倍。
I am prepared to leave it with you as my security.’
我愿意把它留给你作我担保之用。
“I took the precious case into my hands and looked in some perplexity from it to my illustrious client.
我把那珍贵的匣子握在手里，在它和我的 illustrious client 之间困惑地看了起来。
“‘You doubt its value?’ he asked.
‘你怀疑它的价值？’他问。
“‘Not at all.
‘一点也不。’
I only doubt—’
我只怀疑——‘
“‘The propriety of my leaving it.
‘处理这件事务的 propriety.’
You may set your mind at rest about that.
你可以放心关于那件事。
I should not dream of doing so were it not absolutely certain that I should be able in four days to reclaim it.
四天之后我一定能把它拿回来，否则我做梦也不会让它被别人拿走。
It is a pure matter of form.
它是形式问题而已。
Is the security sufficient?’
安全措施够吗？
“‘Ample.’
“‘You understand, Mr. Holder, that I am giving you a strong proof of the confidence which I have in you, founded upon all that I have heard of you.
‘你明白，霍尔特先生，我给你这么强有力的证明，是因为我对你的信任建立在我的所了解的你的一切之上。’

I rely upon you not only to be discreet and to refrain from all gossip upon the matter but, above all, to preserve this coronet with every possible precaution because I need not say that a great public scandal would be caused if any harm were to befall it.
我信赖你不仅要在这件事上保持谨慎，避免一切传闻，而且最重要的是，要以最可能的谨慎保护这顶王冠，因为我说不出如果万一有什么不测，会引起一场巨大的公众丑闻。
Any injury to it would be almost as serious as its complete loss, for there are no beryls in the world to match these, and it would be impossible to replace them.
任何损伤到它都会几乎和完全失去一样严重，因为世界上没有蓝宝石能与之相比，要完全替换它们是不可想象的。
I leave it with you, however, with every confidence, and I shall call for it in person on Monday morning.’
我把它交给你，然而我满怀信心，星期一上午我会亲自来取。
“Seeing that my client was anxious to leave, I said no more but, calling for my cashier, I ordered him to pay over fifty £ 1000 notes.
见 client 想要离开，我说了句什么也没再说，叫来出纳员，命令他付给我五百张一百镑的钞票。
When I was alone once more, however, with the precious case lying upon the table in front of me, I could not but think with some misgivings of the immense responsibility which it entailed upon me.
当再次独自一人，珍贵的箱子摆在面前桌上时，我也不由得有些犹豫地想到它对我所承担的巨大责任。
There could be no doubt that, as it was a national possession, a horrible scandal would ensue if any misfortune should occur to it.
毫无疑问，既然它是国家的财产，如果它有任何不幸发生，将会引起一场可怕的丑闻。
I already regretted having ever consented to take charge of it.
我已经后悔当初同意接手这件事。
However, it was too late to alter the matter now, so I locked it up in my private safe and turned once more to my work.
然而，现在改变这个已经太迟了，所以我把箱子锁在私人保险箱里，再次投入工作。
“When evening came I felt that it would be an imprudence to leave so precious a thing in the office behind me.
“傍晚时分，我觉得把这么珍贵的东西留在办公室里是不明智的。”
Bankers’ safes had been forced before now, and why should not mine be?
银行的保险箱已经被人打开过，为什么我的不能呢？
If so, how terrible would be the position in which I should find myself!
如果如此，我将处于多么可怕的位置！
I determined, therefore, that for the next few days I would always carry the case backward and forward with me, so that it might never be really out of my reach.
因此，我决定接下来几天里，我总是带着箱子走，这样它就不会真的离开我的掌控。
With this intention, I called a cab and drove out to my house at Streatham, carrying the jewel with me.
为了这个目的，我叫了一辆出租车，去我住在斯特汉姆的房子，带着珠宝。
I did not breathe freely until I had taken it upstairs and locked it in the bureau of my dressing-room.
我直到锁好箱子上楼，放在梳妆台的保险箱里，才放松了呼吸。
“And now a word as to my household, Mr. Holmes, for I wish you to thoroughly understand the situation.
“现在，关于我的家庭，史密斯先生，我希望你完全理解这个情况。
My groom and my page sleep out of the house, and may be set aside altogether.
我的仆人和我的侍童睡在外面，也许可以完全取消。
I have three maid-servants who have been with me a number of years and whose absolute reliability is quite above suspicion.
我有三个女仆，她们跟我在一起已经好几年了，她们的绝对可靠是完全不可怀疑的。
Another, Lucy Parr, the second waiting-maid, has only been in my service a few months.
另一个，露西·帕尔，第二位女仆，只有在服务我不到几个月。
She came with an excellent character, however, and has always given me satisfaction.
她来了，有很好的品行，一直给我满意。
She is a very pretty girl and has attracted admirers who have occasionally hung about the place.
她是一个非常漂亮的姑娘，吸引了那些偶尔在地方附近徘徊的崇拜者。
That is the only drawback which we have found to her, but we believe her to be a thoroughly good girl in every way.
这是我们的唯一缺点，但我们认为她是一个完全好的女孩。
“So much for the servants.
“所以仆人们的事就不用说了。
My family itself is so small that it will not take me long to describe it.
我家人口本来就少，我用不了多久就能把他们描述清楚。
I am a widower and have an only son, Arthur.
我是个鳏夫，只有一个儿子，叫阿瑟。
He has been a disappointment to me, Mr. Holmes—a grievous disappointment.
他让我失望了，先生·赫尔克里·波洛，一个巨大的失望。
I have no doubt that I am myself to blame.
我对自己感到很抱歉。
People tell me that I have spoiled him.
人们都说我毁了他。
Very likely I have.
很可能我毁了他。
When my dear wife died I felt that he was all I had to love.
当我亲爱的妻子去世时，我感到他就是我所爱的一切。
I could not bear to see the smile fade even for a moment from his face.
我不能忍受看到他脸上的笑容消失哪怕一瞬间。
I have never denied him a wish.
我从来没有拒绝过他任何愿望。
Perhaps it would have been better for both of us had I been sterner, but I meant it for the best.
也许对双方来说，我过于严厉一点会更好，但我觉得这是最好的。
“It was naturally my intention that he should succeed me in my business, but he was not of a business turn.
“我本来打算让他继承我的事业，但他是不务正业的。
He was wild, wayward, and, to speak the truth, I could not trust him in the handling of large sums of money.
他很野，很任性，而且，说实话，我不能信任他处理大量金钱。
When he was young he became a member of an aristocratic club, and there, having charming manners, he was soon the intimate of a number of men with long purses and expensive habits.
他年轻时加入了贵族俱乐部，那里他有漂亮的举止，很快就成了有钱人的密友。

He learned to play heavily at cards and to squander money on the turf, until he had again and again to come to me and implore me to give him an advance upon his allowance, that he might settle his debts of honour.
他学会了在牌桌上玩得很厉害，花掉钱在赛马上，直到他不得不向我请求提前支取他的生活费，以便偿还他的债务。
He tried more than once to break away from the dangerous company which he was keeping, but each time the influence of his friend, Sir George Burnwell, was enough to draw him back again.
他不止一次试图摆脱那危险的圈子，但每次都被他朋友，乔治爵士的影响所吸引，把他拉了回来。

“And, indeed, I could not wonder that such a man as Sir George Burnwell should gain an influence over him, for he has frequently brought him to my house, and I have found myself that I could hardly resist the fascination of his manner.
“事实上，我不能奇怪像乔治爵士这样的人会对他产生影响，因为他经常带他到我家，我发现自己几乎无法抗拒他那方式的魅力。
He is older than Arthur, a man of the world to his finger-tips, one who had been everywhere, seen everything, a brilliant talker, and a man of great personal beauty.
他是亚瑟的长者，浑身世故，见多识广，曾到过许多地方，见过许多事情，是个出色的谈吐者，而且是个极有个人魅力的男人。

Yet when I think of him in cold blood, far away from the glamour of his presence, I am convinced from his cynical speech and the look which I have caught in his eyes that he is one who should be deeply distrusted.
但当我从冷血的角度思考他时，远远地离开他的光芒，我相信他的冷嘲热讽和我看到他眼睛里的目光，他应该深深被怀疑。
So I think, and so, too, thinks my little Mary, who has a woman’s quick insight into character.
我这样想，我的小玛丽也一样，她有女人的敏锐洞察力。
“And now there is only she to be described.
“现在只有她可以描述。
She is my niece; but when my brother died five years ago and left her alone in the world I adopted her, and have looked upon her ever since as my daughter.
她是我的侄女，但当我哥哥五年前去世，留下她一个人的时候，我收养了她，并一直把她看作是我的女儿。
She is a sunbeam in my house—sweet, loving, beautiful, a wonderful manager and housekeeper, yet as tender and quiet and gentle as a woman could be.
她是我在家里的一缕阳光——甜美、爱慕、美丽，一个非凡的管理者和家庭主妇，但又像女人一样温柔和安静。
She is my right hand.
她是我的右手。
I do not know what I could do without her.
我不知道我怎么能没有她。
In only one matter has she ever gone against my wishes.
在只有一个方面，她曾经违背了我的意愿。
Twice my boy has asked her to marry him, for he loves her devotedly, but each time she has refused him.
我的男孩两次要求她嫁给他，因为他深深地爱着她，但每次她都拒绝了他。
I think that if anyone could have drawn him into the right path it would have been she, and that his marriage might have changed his whole life; but now, alas! it is too late—forever too late!
我认为如果有人能把他引到正确的道路上，那一定是她，他的婚姻可能会改变他的整个生活，但现在，唉！已经太晚了——永远太晚了！
“Now, Mr. Holmes, you know the people who live under my roof, and I shall continue with my miserable story.
“现在，先生，你了解住在我家的人，我将继续讲述我的不幸故事。

“When we were taking coffee in the drawing-room that night after dinner, I told Arthur and Mary my experience, and of the precious treasure which we had under our roof, suppressing only the name of my client.
“那天晚上我们在客厅吃咖啡，我告诉阿瑟和玛丽我的经历，以及我们屋顶上珍贵的宝藏，只抑制了我的客户的名字。
Lucy Parr, who had brought in the coffee, had, I am sure, left the room; but I cannot swear that the door was closed.
路西莉·帕尔小姐进来时带来了咖啡，我肯定她离开了房间，但我不敢保证门是关上的。
Mary and Arthur were much interested and wished to see the famous coronet, but I thought it better not to disturb it.
玛丽和阿瑟非常感兴趣，希望能看到那顶著名的王冠，但我认为最好不要打扰他们。
“‘Where have you put it?’ asked Arthur.
“‘你把帽子放在哪里了？’阿瑟问道。
“‘In my own bureau.’
“‘在我的书桌里放着的。’
“‘Well, I hope to goodness the house won’t be burgled during the night.’ said he.
“‘好吧，我希望晚上不会有人偷窃这房子。’他说。
“‘It is locked up,’ I answered.
“‘它锁着的，’我回答。
“‘Oh, any old key will fit that bureau.
“‘哦，随便一把钥匙都能开那个书桌。’
When I was a youngster I have opened it myself with the key of the box-room cupboard.’
当我还是个孩子时，我曾经自己用书柜的钥匙打开过那个书桌。
“He often had a wild way of talking, so that I thought little of what he said.
他常常会用一种奇怪的方式说话，所以我对他的话不怎么在意。
He followed me to my room, however, that night with a very grave face.
他那天晚上跟着我来到我的房间，脸上带着严肃的表情。
“‘Look here, dad,’ said he with his eyes cast down, ‘can you let me have £ 200?’
“‘爸爸，’他说，‘你能给我200英镑吗？’
“‘No, I cannot!’
“‘不行，我不能！’
I answered sharply.
我回答得很严厉。
‘I have been far too generous with you in money matters.’
‘我太慷慨了，’我回答说。
“‘You have been very kind,’ said he, ‘but I must have this money, or else I can never show my face inside the club again.’
“‘你太慷慨了，’他说，‘但我必须得到这笔钱，否则我永远不能再次出现在俱乐部里。’
“‘And a very good thing, too!’
I cried.
我 cried。
“‘Yes, but you would not have me leave it a dishonoured man,’ said he.
“是的，但你不让我成为一个名誉扫地的人，”他说道。
‘I could not bear the disgrace.
‘我受不了这种耻辱。’
I must raise the money in some way, and if you will not let me have it, then I must try other means.’
我必须设法筹这笔款，如果你不肯让我用，我只好另想办法。
“I was very angry, for this was the third demand during the month.
我很生气，因为这是本月内的第三次要求。
‘You shall not have a farthing from me,’ I cried, on which he bowed and left the room without another word.
‘你一个先令也别想从我身上讨来，’我喊道，他便躬身告退，连一句别的也没有说。
“When he was gone I unlocked my bureau, made sure that my treasure was safe, and locked it again.
当他离开后，我打开我的书桌，确保我的宝藏安全无虞，又将其锁上。
Then I started to go round the house to see that all was secure—a duty which I usually leave to Mary but which I thought it well to perform myself that night.
然后我开始绕着房子转一圈，看看一切是否都安全了——这通常由玛丽来做，但我认为今晚应该自己来完成。
As I came down the stairs I saw Mary herself at the side window of the hall, which she closed and fastened as I approached.
我下楼时，看见玛丽自己站在大厅一侧的窗户旁，她在我走近时关上了窗户并锁上了。
“‘Tell me, dad,’ said she, looking, I thought, a little disturbed, ‘did you give Lucy, the maid, leave to go out to-night?’
“‘告诉我，爸爸，”她说着，我心想她似乎有点心神不宁，“你今晚给了女仆露西外出的许可吗？”
“‘Certainly not.’
“当然没有。”
“‘She came in just now by the back door.
‘她刚才经后门進來的。’
I have no doubt that she has only been to the side gate to see someone, but I think that it is hardly safe and should be stopped.’
我毫不怀疑她只是到侧门去看人，但她去的并不安全，应该阻止。
“‘You must speak to her in the morning, or I will if you prefer it.
“你必须在早上跟她说话，否则我会的。
Are you sure that everything is fastened?’
你确定一切都系好了吗？
“‘Quite sure, dad.’
““完全确定，爸爸。”
“‘Then, good-night.’
““那么，晚安。”
I kissed her and went up to my bedroom again, where I was soon asleep.
我吻了她，又回到我的卧室，很快就睡着了。
“I am endeavouring to tell you everything, Mr. Holmes, which may have any bearing upon the case, but I beg that you will question me upon any point which I do not make clear.”
“我正试图告诉您一切，史密斯先生，这可能与案件有关，但请您在我不清楚的地方提问。”
“On the contrary, your statement is singularly lucid.”
“相反，您的陈述非常清晰。”
“I come to a part of my story now in which I should wish to be particularly so.
“我现在要讲到我故事的一个部分，我希望能特别清楚。”
I am not a very heavy sleeper, and the anxiety in my mind tended, no doubt, to make me even less so than usual.
我不是个很重的睡者，心里的焦虑可能使我更不睡了。
About two in the morning, then, I was awakened by some sound in the house.
大约凌晨两点，我被房屋里传来的声音惊醒。
It had ceased ere I was wide awake, but it had left an impression behind it as though a window had gently closed somewhere.
那声音停止了，但我醒来时，那声音还在，好像窗户轻轻关上了。
I lay listening with all my ears.
我屏息静听。
Suddenly, to my horror, there was a distinct sound of footsteps moving softly in the next room.
突然，我的恐惧发作，传来轻微的脚步声在隔壁房间。
I slipped out of bed, all palpitating with fear, and peeped round the corner of my dressing-room door.
我从床上滑下，全身颤抖，探出衣橱门的角落。
“‘Arthur!’
“‘阿奇尔！’
I screamed, ‘you villain! you thief!
我尖叫道：“你这个坏蛋！你这个小偷！”
How dare you touch that coronet?’
怎么敢碰那顶王冠？
“The gas was half up, as I had left it, and my unhappy boy, dressed only in his shirt and trousers, was standing beside the light, holding the coronet in his hands.
我的煤气半点没减，正如我离开时一样，我可怜的孩子只穿着衬衣和裤子，站在灯旁，手里拿着王冠。
He appeared to be wrenching at it, or bending it with all his strength.
他似乎在扭力，或者用尽全身力气弯曲。
At my cry he dropped it from his grasp and turned as pale as death.
我的喊声，他从手中掉落，脸色煞白。
I snatched it up and examined it.
我拾起它，仔细查看。
One of the gold corners, with three of the beryls in it, was missing.
一枚金角上，有三颗红宝石，不见了。
“‘You blackguard!’
“‘你混蛋！’
I shouted, beside myself with rage.
我怒不可遏地大喊。
‘You have destroyed it!
“你毁了它！
You have dishonoured me forever!
你玷污了我的名誉！
Where are the jewels which you have stolen?’
你偷走了什么珠宝？
“‘Stolen!’ he cried.
“‘偷走的！’他喊道。
“‘Yes, thief!’
“‘是的，小偷！’
I roared, shaking him by the shoulder.
我吼叫，用肩膀撞他。
“‘There are none missing.
“‘没有丢失的。’
There cannot be any missing,’ said he.
他说道：“不可能有遗漏的。”
“‘There are three missing.
“‘有三个失踪的。”
And you know where they are.
“你知道他们藏在哪里。”
Must I call you a liar as well as a thief?
“我难道不能把你说成骗子和小偷吗？”
Did I not see you trying to tear off another piece?’
“我看见你试图撕掉另一块吗？”
“‘You have called me names enough,’ said he, ‘I will not stand it any longer.
“‘你已经叫了我够多的脏话了，’他说道，‘我再也忍受不了了。”
I shall not say another word about this business, since you have chosen to insult me.
“我不会再说关于这件事的话了，既然你选择侮辱我。”
I will leave your house in the morning and make my own way in the world.’
“我明天早晨离开你的房子，自己在世界上谋生。”
“‘You shall leave it in the hands of the police!’
“‘你让警察处理吧！’”
I cried half-mad with grief and rage.
我哭得半死半疯。
‘I shall have this matter probed to the bottom.’
“我要把这件事彻底调查清楚。”
“‘You shall learn nothing from me,’ said he with a passion such as I should not have thought was in his nature.
“‘你不会从我这里学到什么的，’他说道，‘我不会再说了。”’
‘If you choose to call the police, let the police find what they can.’
“如果你选择报警，让警察找到他们能找到的东西。”
“By this time the whole house was astir, for I had raised my voice in my anger.
“这时整个房子都骚动起来，因为我愤怒地高声喊叫。”
Mary was the first to rush into my room, and, at the sight of the coronet and of Arthur’s face, she read the whole story and, with a scream, fell down senseless on the ground.
莫莉第一个冲进我的房间，看到冠冕和阿瑟的脸，她读出了整个故事，尖叫着倒在了地上。
I sent the housemaid for the police and put the investigation into their hands at once.
我叫女仆去报案，立刻把调查交给了他们。
When the inspector and a constable entered the house, Arthur, who had stood sullenly with his arms folded, asked me whether it was my intention to charge him with theft.
当警官和一名警员进入房子时，阿瑟，一个闷闷不乐地双臂交叉站着的人，问我是否打算把他的罪行定罪。
I answered that it had ceased to be a private matter, but had become a public one, since the ruined coronet was national property.
我回答说，这已经不再是私事了，而是成了公事，因为那顶毁了的冠冕是国家财产。
I was determined that the law should have its way in everything.
我决心让法律在一切事情上都占上风。
“‘At least,’ said he, ‘you will not have me arrested at once.
“‘至少，’他说，‘你不会立刻把我逮捕。
It would be to your advantage as well as mine if I might leave the house for five minutes.’
为了你的利益以及我的利益，我如果可以离开房子五分钟的话，我应该可以离开房子五分钟。

“‘That you may get away, or perhaps that you may conceal what you have stolen,’ said I. And then, realising the dreadful position in which I was placed, I implored him to remember that not only my honour but that of one who was far greater than I was at stake; and that he threatened to raise a scandal which would convulse the nation.
“‘那你可以逃走，或者也许你藏匿了你偷的东西，’我说。然后，意识到我所处的可怕的处境，我恳求他记住，不仅我的荣誉，而且比我更大的一个人的荣誉，都处于危险之中，而且他威胁要掀起一场全国性的丑闻。
He might avert it all if he would but tell me what he had done with the three missing stones.
如果你能够告诉我你把那三块失踪的宝石藏在哪里，那么一切都可以原谅和忘记。
“‘You may as well face the matter,’ said I; ‘you have been caught in the act, and no confession could make your guilt more heinous.

他要求允许他出去五分钟！
The dear fellow wanted to see if the missing piece were at the scene of the struggle.
这个可怜的人想看看丢失的部件是否在冲突的现场。
How cruelly I have misjudged him!”
我多么残酷地误解了他！
“When I arrived at the house,” continued Holmes, “I at once went very carefully round it to observe if there were any traces in the snow which might help me.
“当我到达房子时，我立刻小心地绕着它观察，看看雪地上是否有任何痕迹，这些痕迹可能有助于我。”
I knew that none had fallen since the evening before, and also that there had been a strong frost to preserve impressions.
我知道自从前一天晚上以来没有掉下来，而且我也知道由于强霜保存了痕迹。
I passed along the tradesmen’s path, but found it all trampled down and indistinguishable.
我沿着商人路径走，但发现它都被踩平了，无法区分。
Just beyond it, however, at the far side of the kitchen door, a woman had stood and talked with a man, whose round impressions on one side showed that he had a wooden leg.
然而，就在它旁边，厨房门的另一边，一个女人和一个男人在那里交谈，他们的圆形印记表明他有一个木腿。

I could even tell that they had been disturbed, for the woman had run back swiftly to the door, as was shown by the deep toe and light heel marks, while Wooden-leg had waited a little, and then had gone away.
我甚至能知道他们被打扰了，因为女人迅速跑回门，这通过深深的脚趾和浅的脚跟痕迹显示出来，而木腿则等待了一会儿，然后离开了。
I thought at the time that this might be the maid and her sweetheart, of whom you had already spoken to me, and inquiry showed it was so.
我当时认为这可能是女仆和她的丈夫，你已经向我提到过，调查证实是这样。

I passed round the garden without seeing anything more than random tracks, which I took to be the police; but when I got into the stable lane a very long and complex story was written in the snow in front of me.
我绕着花园走，但发现除了随机的痕迹，什么也没有看到，这些痕迹我把它看作是警察；但当我进入马厩小巷时，我看到在雪前有一个非常长和复杂的故事情节。
“There was a double line of tracks of a booted man, and a second double line which I saw with delight belonged to a man with naked feet.
“有一条双线的靴子人的痕迹，另一条双线我看到了，我非常高兴，属于一个赤脚的人。
I was at once convinced from what you had told me that the latter was your son.
我立刻相信了你所说的，后者是你儿子。
The first had walked both ways, but the other had run swiftly, and as his tread was marked in places over the depression of the boot, it was obvious that he had passed after the other.
第一个走了两趟，但第二个跑得很快，他的足迹在靴底的凹陷处有明显的标记，可以知道他是在他后面经过的。
I followed them up and found they led to the hall window, where Boots had worn all the snow away while waiting.
我跟着他们来到大厅的窗户前，发现他们通往窗户，而Boots已经把雪都赶走了，因为他是在等待。
Then I walked to the other end, which was a hundred yards or more down the lane.
然后我走到另一端，那是几百码或更远的路。
I saw where Boots had faced round, where the snow was cut up as though there had been a struggle, and, finally, where a few drops of blood had fallen, to show me that I was not mistaken.
我看到Boots已经转过身，雪被切开，好像有挣扎，最后，几滴血滴落在地上，让我知道我没有错。
Boots had then run down the lane, and another little smudge of blood showed that it was he who had been hurt.
Boos然后跑下路，另一个小滴血显示他被伤了。
When he came to the high road at the other end, I found that the pavement had been cleared, so there was an end to that clue.
当他来到另一端的高路时，我发现路面已经被清理，所以线索就结束了。
“On entering the house, however, I examined, as you remember, the sill and framework of the hall window with my lens, and I could at once see that someone had passed out.
“然而，进入房子时，我检查了大厅窗户的门槛和框架，我一眼就看到有人经过。
I could distinguish the outline of an instep where the wet foot had been placed in coming in.
我可以看到湿脚的脚印，那是湿脚放在进来时的轮廓。
I was then beginning to be able to form an opinion as to what had occurred.
我开始能够形成一个意见，发生了什么。

A man had waited outside the window; someone had brought the gems; the deed had been overseen by your son; he had pursued the thief; had struggled with him; they had each tugged at the coronet, their united strength causing injuries which neither alone could have effected.
有人在外面等，有人带来宝石，你的儿子负责了这个行为，他追捕了小偷，和他斗争，他们互相揪住了冠冕，他们联合的力量造成了无法单独完成的伤害。
He had returned with the prize, but had left a fragment in the grasp of his opponent.
他带着奖品回来，但留下一个碎片在对手的手中。
So far I was clear.
到目前为止，我清楚了。
The question now was, who was the man, and who was it brought him the coronet?
现在的问题是，谁是这个人，谁是带来冠冕的人？
“It is an old maxim of mine that when you have excluded the impossible, whatever remains, however improbable, must be the truth.
“这是我的一个老格言，当你排除不可能时，剩下的无论多么不可能，必定是真理。”
Now, I knew that it was not you who had brought it down, so there only remained your niece and the maids.
现在我知道不是你把那东西弄下来的，所以只剩下你妹妹和女仆了。
But if it were the maids, why should your son allow himself to be accused in their place?
但是，如果女仆是罪犯，你儿子为什么要在她们的名义下被指控？
There could be no possible reason.
无法找到任何合理的解释。
As he loved his cousin, however, there was an excellent explanation why he should retain her secret—the more so as the secret was a disgraceful one.
既然他爱自己的侄子，那么保留她的秘密就有很好的解释——更确切地说，因为这个秘密是丢脸的。
When I remembered that you had seen her at that window, and how she had fainted on seeing the coronet again, my conjecture became a certainty.
当我想到你曾在那个窗户前见到她，她再次看到皇冠时晕倒，我的猜测变成了确定无疑。
“And who could it be who was her confederate?
“谁是她的同谋？
A lover evidently, for who else could outweigh the love and gratitude which she must feel to you?
一个显然的恋人，因为谁比她对你的爱和感激更重？
I knew that you went out little, and that your circle of friends was a very limited one.
我知道你很少外出，朋友圈子也很小。
But among them was Sir George Burnwell.
但其中有一个是乔治爵士。
I had heard of him before as being a man of evil reputation among women.
我以前听说过他，因为他对男人来说是女人中的坏人。
It must have been he who wore those boots and retained the missing gems.
他必须是那个穿靴子的人，保留丢失的宝石。
Even though he knew that Arthur had discovered him, he might still flatter himself that he was safe, for the lad could not say a word without compromising his own family.
即使他知道亚瑟已经发现了他，他仍然可能会自欺欺人，认为自己是安全的，因为这个孩子不能说一句话而不牵涉到他的家庭。
“Well, your own good sense will suggest what measures I took next.
“好吧，你的良知会建议我接下来采取什么措施。

I went in the shape of a loafer to Sir George’s house, managed to pick up an acquaintance with his valet, learned that his master had cut his head the night before, and, finally, at the expense of six shillings, made all sure by buying a pair of his cast-off shoes.
我化装成一个闲人来到乔治爵士的家，设法与他的仆人结识，得知他的主人前一天晚上割掉了他的头，最后，以六便士的代价，确保了这一切。
With these I journeyed down to Streatham and saw that they exactly fitted the tracks.”
用这些我前往斯特哈姆，看到它们完全符合痕迹。”
“I saw an ill-dressed vagabond in the lane yesterday evening,” said Mr. Holder.
“我昨天晚上在小巷里看到一个衣衫褴褛的流浪汉。”霍尔先生说。
“Precisely.
“正是我。
It was I. I found that I had my man, so I came home and changed my clothes.
我发现我捉住了人，于是回家换衣服。
It was a delicate part which I had to play then, for I saw that a prosecution must be avoided to avert scandal, and I knew that so astute a villain would see that our hands were tied in the matter.
那时我扮演了一个微妙的角色，因为我知道要避免指控，以免引起丑闻，而且我知道这样一个精明的坏蛋会注意到我们的手在这件事上被绑住了。
I went and saw him.
我去见他。
At first, of course, he denied everything.
一开始，当然他否认一切。
But when I gave him every particular that had occurred, he tried to bluster and took down a life-preserver from the wall.
但当我给他提供了所有发生的事情，他试图辩解，从墙上取下救生圈。
I knew my man, however, and I clapped a pistol to his head before he could strike.
我知道我的人，于是在他可以击打之前扣动了扳机。
Then he became a little more reasonable.
然后他变得稍微有点理智。
I told him that we would give him a price for the stones he held—£ 1000 apiece.
我告诉他，我们将会给他每块石头1000英镑。
That brought out the first signs of grief that he had shown.
这才显示出他第一次流露出的悲伤迹象。
‘Why, dash it all!’ said he, ‘I’ve let them go at six hundred for the three!’
“天啊！”他说，“我把它们卖给了他们六百英镑！”
I soon managed to get the address of the receiver who had them, on promising him that there would be no prosecution.
我很快设法弄到收件人的地址，承诺不会追究。
Off I set to him, and after much chaffering I got our stones at £ 1000 apiece.
我去见他，告诉他一切都正常，最终在两点左右回到我的床上，尽管我可能称其为一场真正辛苦的工作。”
Then I looked in upon your son, told him that all was right, and eventually got to my bed about two o’clock, after what I may call a really hard day’s work.”
然后我去看望了你的儿子，告诉他一切都好，并在大约两点的时候上了床，那是我一个真正辛苦的日子之后。
“A day which has saved England from a great public scandal,” said the banker, rising.
“今天拯救了英格兰免受重大公众丑闻，”银行家站起来说道。
“Sir, I cannot find words to thank you, but you shall not find me ungrateful for what you have done.
“先生，我找不到词句来感谢你，但你所做的事我不会对你不感激的。
Your skill has indeed exceeded all that I have heard of it.
你的确超出了我所听到的所有技能。
And now I must fly to my dear boy to apologise to him for the wrong which I have done him.
现在我必须飞到我亲爱的儿子那里向他道歉，因为我做了他所受的错误。
As to what you tell me of poor Mary, it goes to my very heart.
关于你告诉我关于可怜的玛丽的事，它触及了我的心。
Not even your skill can inform me where she is now.”
甚至你的技能也无法告诉我她现在在哪里。
“I think that we may safely say,” returned Holmes, “that she is wherever Sir George Burnwell is.
“我认为我们可以说，”霍尔姆斯回答道，“她现在在哪里，是英国的乔治·班维尔先生。
It is equally certain, too, that whatever her sins are, they will soon receive a more than sufficient punishment.”
也毫无疑问，她所犯的罪行，很快就会收到一个更充分的惩罚。”

ch.et: XII. The Adventure of the Copper Beeches
ch.zt: 第十二篇 · 铜山毛榉案
p: “To the man who loves art for its own sake,” remarked Sherlock Holmes, tossing aside the advertisement sheet of The Daily Telegraph, “it is frequently in its least important and lowliest manifestations that the keenest pleasure is to be derived.
“对那些只因艺术本身而热爱艺术的人来说，”夏洛克·福尔摩斯说道，随手将《每日电讯报》的广告单扔在一边，“他们从艺术最微不足道和最低劣的体现中往往能获得最强烈的乐趣。

It is pleasant to me to observe, Watson, that you have so far grasped this truth that in these little records of our cases which you have been good enough to draw up, and, I am bound to say, occasionally to embellish, you have given prominence not so much to the many causes célèbres and sensational trials in which I have figured but rather to those incidents which may have been trivial in themselves, but which have given room for those faculties of deduction and of logical synthesis which I have made my special province.”
对我来说，沃森先生，你已经注意到，你已经抓住了这个真理，你在你所绘制的这些记录中，以及我必须承认，你偶尔会加以美化的一些记录中，你已经把不那么重要的和不引人注目的事件放在了主要位置，而不是放在了记录我所擅长的推理和逻辑合成能力上的那些事件上。
“And yet,” said I, smiling, “I cannot quite hold myself absolved from the charge of sensationalism which has been urged against my records.”
“然而，”我笑着说，“我不能完全摆脱对我的记录中被指责为‘轰动性’的指控的指控。

“You have erred, perhaps,” he observed, taking up a glowing cinder with the tongs and lighting with it the long cherry-wood pipe which was wont to replace his clay when he was in a disputatious rather than a meditative mood—“you have erred perhaps in attempting to put colour and life into each of your statements instead of confining yourself to the task of placing upon record that severe reasoning from cause to effect which is really the only notable feature about the thing.”
“也许你错了，”他观察到，用钳子夹起了一根炽热的炭火，用它点燃了他惯常使用的长樱桃木烟斗，这烟斗在争辩时比在沉思时更常见，“也许你在试图在每个陈述中添加颜色和生命，而不是把记录中真正唯一显著的特征——从原因到结果的严格推理——放在主要位置。

“It seems to me that I have done you full justice in the matter,” I remarked with some coldness, for I was repelled by the egotism which I had more than once observed to be a strong factor in my friend’s singular character.
“在我看来，我对你已经公正了，”我冷淡地说，因为我不喜欢我朋友的某些特质，我曾经观察到它们是强大力量。
“No, it is not selfishness or conceit,” said he, answering, as was his wont, my thoughts rather than my words.
“不，这不是自私或自大，”他说，回答我的想法而不是我的话。
“If I claim full justice for my art, it is because it is an impersonal thing—a thing beyond myself.
“如果我声称我的艺术得到了公正，那是因为它是一个无我之物。
Crime is common.
犯罪是普遍的。
Logic is rare.
逻辑是罕见的。
Therefore it is upon the logic rather than upon the crime that you should dwell.
因此，你应该关注逻辑，而不是犯罪。
You have degraded what should have been a course of lectures into a series of tales.”
你把什么应该是一个讲座系列变成了一个故事系列。
It was a cold morning of the early spring, and we sat after breakfast on either side of a cheery fire in the old room at Baker Street.
那是一个寒冷的早春早晨，我们坐在比克街比克街的旧房间里，一边的火炉旁，一边的火炉旁，早餐后。
A thick fog rolled down between the lines of dun-coloured houses, and the opposing windows loomed like dark, shapeless blurs through the heavy yellow wreaths.
一片浓雾从房屋的线条中漫延开来，对面的窗户像厚重的黄色雾气一样，像黑暗的、形状模糊的模糊。
Our gas was lit and shone on the white cloth and glimmer of china and metal, for the table had not been cleared yet.
我们煤气灯亮着，照在白色的布料和瓷器和金属的闪光上，因为桌子还没有被清理。

Sherlock Holmes had been silent all the morning, dipping continuously into the advertisement columns of a succession of papers until at last, having apparently given up his search, he had emerged in no very sweet temper to lecture me upon my literary shortcomings.
夏洛克·福尔摩斯在上午一直沉默，不断从一系列报纸的广告栏中汲取，直到最后，似乎放弃了搜索，他出来时带着非常不愉快的脾气，来教训我我的文学缺点。

“At the same time,” he remarked after a pause, during which he had sat puffing at his long pipe and gazing down into the fire, “you can hardly be open to a charge of sensationalism, for out of these cases which you have been so kind as to interest yourself in, a fair proportion do not treat of crime, in its legal sense, at all.
“同时，”他停顿了一下，一边坐在长烟管上，一边凝视着火光，“你很难被指控为耸人听闻，因为你所关心的案件中，有一大部分与犯罪无关，从法律的角度来看。”

The small matter in which I endeavoured to help the King of Bohemia, the singular experience of Miss Mary Sutherland, the problem connected with the man with the twisted lip, and the incident of the noble bachelor, were all matters which are outside the pale of the law.
我帮助布拉格国王的微小事情，玛丽小姐的奇异经历，与那张歪嘴男子的问题，以及那位单身贵族的事件，都是法律之外的事项。
But in avoiding the sensational, I fear that you may have bordered on the trivial.”
但我避免耸人听闻，恐怕你可能偏向于琐碎。
“The end may have been so,” I answered, “but the methods I hold to have been novel and of interest.”
“那结果可能如此，但我所持的方法是新颖且有趣的。”

“Pshaw, my dear fellow, what do the public, the great unobservant public, who could hardly tell a weaver by his tooth or a compositor by his left thumb, care about the finer shades of analysis and deduction!
“呸，亲爱的，公众，那些根本不知道织布工靠什么辨认，不知道打字员靠什么辨认的，对这些细节分析和推理有什么兴趣！”
But, indeed, if you are trivial, I cannot blame you, for the days of the great cases are past.
但事实上，如果你是琐碎的，我不能责怪你，因为那些伟大的案件的时代已经过去了。
Man, or at least criminal man, has lost all enterprise and originality.
人类，或者至少犯罪的人，已经失去了进取心和原创性。
As to my own little practice, it seems to be degenerating into an agency for recovering lost lead pencils and giving advice to young ladies from boarding-schools.
关于我的小业务，似乎已经退化成一个找回丢失铅笔的机构和给年轻小姐们提建议的机构。
I think that I have touched bottom at last, however.
我认为我已经到达了终点。
This note I had this morning marks my zero-point, I fancy.
今天早上我写的这封信，是我零点的标志，我想。
Read it!”
读！
He tossed a crumpled letter across to me.
他把一团皱巴巴的信件扔给我。
It was dated from Montague Place upon the preceding evening, and ran thus:
日期是前一天晚上，写着：
“DEAR MR.
“亲爱的先生，
HOLMES,—I am very anxious to consult you as to whether I should or should not accept a situation which has been offered to me as governess.
霍尔姆斯——我很担心能否接受我被介绍给我的情况，是否应该接受。
I shall call at half-past ten to-morrow if I do not inconvenience you.
如果明天十点半我再来，我不会打扰你的。
Yours faithfully,
你忠实的，
“VIOLET HUNTER.”
“Do you know the young lady?”
“你知道那位小姐吗？”
I asked.
我问。
“Not I.”
“不认识。”
“It is half-past ten now.”
“现在是十点半了。”
“Yes, and I have no doubt that is her ring.”
“是的，而且我肯定那是个戒指。”
“It may turn out to be of more interest than you think.
“也许会比你想象的更有趣。
You remember that the affair of the blue carbuncle, which appeared to be a mere whim at first, developed into a serious investigation.
你还记得蓝宝石案，一开始看起来只是个玩笑，后来发展成了一次严肃的调查。
It may be so in this case, also.”
这也可能如此。”
“Well, let us hope so.
“好吧，希望如此。
But our doubts will very soon be solved, for here, unless I am much mistaken, is the person in question.”
但我们的疑惑很快就会解开，因为在这里，除非我搞错了，这个人就是你所说的那个人。”
As he spoke the door opened and a young lady entered the room.
他说话间，门开了，一个年轻小姐走进了房间。
She was plainly but neatly dressed, with a bright, quick face, freckled like a plover’s egg, and with the brisk manner of a woman who has had her own way to make in the world.
她打扮得很清楚，但整洁，脸色明亮，像一只雏鸟的蛋，举止像一个在世上占了上风的女性。

“You will excuse my troubling you, I am sure,” said she, as my companion rose to greet her, “but I have had a very strange experience, and as I have no parents or relations of any sort from whom I could ask advice, I thought that perhaps you would be kind enough to tell me what I should do.”
“打扰一下，我确定，”她说道，当我的同伴起身迎接她时， “但我有过非常奇怪的经历，而我没有任何父母或任何关系的人可以向他们寻求建议，所以我认为也许你愿意告诉我应该怎么做。”
“Pray take a seat, Miss Hunter.
“请坐，小姐汉默。”
I shall be happy to do anything that I can to serve you.”
我会很高兴能为你做任何我能做的。”
I could see that Holmes was favourably impressed by the manner and speech of his new client.
我可以看到，福尔摩斯对他的新客户的态度和言辞印象深刻。
He looked her over in his searching fashion, and then composed himself, with his lids drooping and his finger-tips together, to listen to her story.
他用一种搜寻的目光打量了她，然后整理好自己，闭上眼睛，指尖并拢，以便听她讲故事。

“I have been a governess for five years,” said she, “in the family of Colonel Spence Munro, but two months ago the colonel received an appointment at Halifax, in Nova Scotia, and took his children over to America with him, so that I found myself without a situation.
“我已经当了五年家庭教师，”她说，“在斯彭斯·穆罗家族，但我两个月前，当上诺瓦斯克的总督，带着他的孩子们去了美国，所以我发现自己没有一个职位。
I advertised, and I answered advertisements, but without success.
我广告，我回答广告，但没有成功。
At last the little money which I had saved began to run short, and I was at my wit’s end as to what I should do.
最后，我节省下来的那点钱开始耗尽，我束手无策，不知道该怎么办。
“There is a well-known agency for governesses in the West End called Westaway’s, and there I used to call about once a week in order to see whether anything had turned up which might suit me.

“Your narrative promises to be a most interesting one.”
你的叙述 promises to be a most interesting one。
“You will find it rather disconnected, I fear, and there may prove to be little relation between the different incidents of which I speak.
你会发现我的叙述颇为 disconnected，恐怕，而且我所说的不同事件之间可能并无关系。
On the very first day that I was at the Copper Beeches, Mr. Rucastle took me to a small outhouse which stands near the kitchen door.
在铜蜂巢的头一天，鲁斯克斯特先生带我去看一间靠近厨房门的小储藏室。
As we approached it I heard the sharp rattling of a chain, and the sound as of a large animal moving about.
我们走近时，我听到一阵尖锐的链条碰撞声，以及一只大动物走动的声音。
“‘Look in here!’ said Mr. Rucastle, showing me a slit between two planks.
‘看里面!’鲁斯克斯特先生说，他给我看了一下两块木板之间的缝隙。
‘Is he not a beauty?’
他不是美男子吗？
“I looked through and was conscious of two glowing eyes, and of a vague figure huddled up in the darkness.
我仔细查看，心中感到两双明亮的眼睛，以及模糊的影子蜷缩在黑暗中。
“‘Don’t be frightened,’ said my employer, laughing at the start which I had given.
“别怕，”我的雇主笑着说，我一开始的反应。
‘It’s only Carlo, my mastiff.
“那是我的狗卡洛，我的猎犬。
I call him mine, but really old Toller, my groom, is the only man who can do anything with him.
我把他当作我的，但真正的老托尔，我的马夫，才是他唯一能控制的。
We feed him once a day, and not too much then, so that he is always as keen as mustard.
每天只喂一次，不多，这样他永远像芥末一样灵敏。
Toller lets him loose every night, and God help the trespasser whom he lays his fangs upon.
托尔让他每晚放出来，老天保佑，他咬伤了闯入者。
For goodness’ sake don’t you ever on any pretext set your foot over the threshold at night, for it’s as much as your life is worth.’
请不要在任何借口下，任何理由下，踏入我家的门槛，因为那对你来说，生命值不值得。
“The warning was no idle one, for two nights later I happened to look out of my bedroom window about two o’clock in the morning.
这警告并非空穴来风，因为两天后，我半夜两点左右，从卧室窗口往外看。
It was a beautiful moonlight night, and the lawn in front of the house was silvered over and almost as bright as day.
夜晚的月亮，银色的草坪，几乎像白天一样明亮。
I was standing, rapt in the peaceful beauty of the scene, when I was aware that something was moving under the shadow of the copper beeches.
我站在那里，沉浸在场景的和平美丽中，突然，我意识到，有东西在铜枫树阴影下移动。
As it emerged into the moonshine I saw what it was.
当它从阴影中显现出来时，我看到了什么。
It was a giant dog, as large as a calf, tawny tinted, with hanging jowl, black muzzle, and huge projecting bones.
它是一只巨大的狗，像一头小牛一样大小，棕褐色的，下巴垂着，黑色的嘴，巨大的骨头突出。
It walked slowly across the lawn and vanished into the shadow upon the other side.
它慢慢地穿过草坪，消失在另一边的阴影中。
That dreadful sentinel sent a chill to my heart which I do not think that any burglar could have done.
那可怕的哨兵，让我心寒，我怀疑任何小偷都无法做到。
“And now I have a very strange experience to tell you.
"现在我要告诉你一件非常奇怪的事情。
I had, as you know, cut off my hair in London, and I had placed it in a great coil at the bottom of my trunk.
你知道，我在伦敦剪掉了我的头发，把它放在箱子底部的一个大螺旋里。
One evening, after the child was in bed, I began to amuse myself by examining the furniture of my room and by rearranging my own little things.
有一天晚上，当孩子上床后，我开始在房间里玩，把我的东西重新整理。
There was an old chest of drawers in the room, the two upper ones empty and open, the lower one locked.
房间里有一个抽屉柜，上两个抽屉空着，下边的抽屉锁着。
I had filled the first two with my linen, and as I had still much to pack away I was naturally annoyed at not having the use of the third drawer.
我把上两个抽屉装满了我的衣服，因为还有许多东西需要打包，所以我对第三抽屉没有使用感到很生气。
It struck me that it might have been fastened by a mere oversight, so I took out my bunch of keys and tried to open it.
我想到可能是因为一个疏忽，所以我拿出我的钥匙，试着打开它。
The very first key fitted to perfection, and I drew the drawer open.
首先的钥匙完美地打开，我打开抽屉。
There was only one thing in it, but I am sure that you would never guess what it was.
只有一个东西在里面，但我确定你不会猜到是什么。
It was my coil of hair.
是我的螺旋头发。
“I took it up and examined it.
"我拿起来，仔细看了看。
It was of the same peculiar tint, and the same thickness.
它的颜色和厚度都一样。
But then the impossibility of the thing obtruded itself upon me.
但那奇怪的事情突然出现在我的脑海里。
How could my hair have been locked in the drawer?
为什么我的头发会被锁在抽屉里？
With trembling hands I undid my trunk, turned out the contents, and drew from the bottom my own hair.
我颤抖着打开我的箱子，把里面的东西都拿出来，从底部拿出我的头发。
I laid the two tresses together, and I assure you that they were identical.
我把两束头发放在一起，你肯定它们是一样的。
Was it not extraordinary?
这不是很奇怪吗？
Puzzle as I would, I could make nothing at all of what it meant.
尽管我百思不得其解，但我什么也想不通。
I returned the strange hair to the drawer, and I said nothing of the matter to the Rucastles as I felt that I had put myself in the wrong by opening a drawer which they had locked.
我把那奇怪的头发放回抽屉里，然后对鲁卡斯特尔夫妇什么也没说，因为我觉得我打开他们锁着的抽屉犯了错。
“I am naturally observant, as you may have remarked, Mr. Holmes, and I soon had a pretty good plan of the whole house in my head.
“我天生就观察力敏锐，正如你可能注意到的，先生·霍尔姆斯，我很快就有了整个房子的大概计划。
There was one wing, however, which appeared not to be inhabited at all.
但是，有一个翼房似乎根本没有人居住。
A door which faced that which led into the quarters of the Tollers opened into this suite, but it was invariably locked.
一个门，面向通往 Tollers 的房间，打开到这个套间，但总是锁着的。

One day, however, as I ascended the stair, I met Mr. Rucastle coming out through this door, his keys in his hand, and a look on his face which made him a very different person to the round, jovial man to whom I was accustomed.
有一天，当我上楼梯时，我遇见了鲁卡斯特尔先生，他手里拿着钥匙，脸上带着一种让我觉得他完全变了一个人的表情。
His cheeks were red, his brow was all crinkled with anger, and the veins stood out at his temples with passion.
他的脸颊红了，额头皱巴巴的，眉头紧皱，额头上的血管突起。
He locked the door and hurried past me without a word or a look.
他锁上门，匆匆走过我身边，一句话也没说，也没有看我一眼。
“This aroused my curiosity, so when I went out for a walk in the grounds with my charge, I strolled round to the side from which I could see the windows of this part of the house.
“这引起了我的好奇心，所以我散步时带着我的客人，走到房子这一部分的窗户后面。
There were four of them in a row, three of which were simply dirty, while the fourth was shuttered up.
有四扇窗户，三扇是脏的，而第四扇是关着的。
They were evidently all deserted.
它们显然都空着。
As I strolled up and down, glancing at them occasionally, Mr. Rucastle came out to me, looking as merry and jovial as ever.
我走来走去，不时地看看它们，鲁卡斯特尔先生走过来，看起来和往常一样快乐和开朗。
“‘Ah!’ said he, ‘you must not think me rude if I passed you without a word, my dear young lady.
“‘啊！’他说，‘你不要以为我对你粗鲁，亲爱的小姐。
I was preoccupied with business matters.’
我忙于处理公务。”
“I assured him that I was not offended.
"我向他保证，我没有生气。
‘By the way,’ said I, ‘you seem to have quite a suite of spare rooms up there, and one of them has the shutters up.’
"顺便说一句，"我说,"你似乎在上面住着一间相当宽敞的房间，其中一间房的窗帘是关着的。
“He looked surprised and, as it seemed to me, a little startled at my remark.
"他显得很惊讶，似乎对我这句话有些吃惊。
“‘Photography is one of my hobbies,’ said he.
"‘摄影是我的业余爱好，’他说。
‘I have made my dark room up there.
"我在我那上面的暗室里已经布置好了。
But, dear me! what an observant young lady we have come upon.
但天啊！我们怎么会遇到这么一个精明的姑娘呢？
Who would have believed it?
谁会相信这样的事情？
Who would have ever believed it?’
谁会相信这样的事情呢？
He spoke in a jesting tone, but there was no jest in his eyes as he looked at me.
他用开玩笑的口吻说话，但他的眼睛里没有开玩笑的神情，当他看着我时。
I read suspicion there and annoyance, but no jest.
我在怀疑和不满中读到了，但没有开玩笑。
“Well, Mr. Holmes, from the moment that I understood that there was something about that suite of rooms which I was not to know, I was all on fire to go over them.
"先生，福尔摩斯先生，从我理解到那间房间中有些东西我不了解，我立刻就燃起了去那里的热情。
It was not mere curiosity, though I have my share of that.
它不只是好奇心，虽然我也有一点好奇心。
It was more a feeling of duty—a feeling that some good might come from my penetrating to this place.
它更多是一种责任感，一种感觉，有些好事可能会从我深入到这个地方。
They talk of woman’s instinct; perhaps it was woman’s instinct which gave me that feeling.
人们谈论女人的直觉，也许就是女人的直觉给了我这种感觉。
At any rate, it was there, and I was keenly on the lookout for any chance to pass the forbidden door.
无论如何，它在那里，我时刻都在寻找任何机会通过那扇被禁止的门。
“It was only yesterday that the chance came.
只有昨天，机会才出现。
I may tell you that, besides Mr. Rucastle, both Toller and his wife find something to do in these deserted rooms, and I once saw him carrying a large black linen bag with him through the door.
我可以告诉你，除了鲁卡斯特先生，特尔和他妻子在这些空荡荡的房间中都有事可做，我曾经看到他带着一个大黑布袋走过门。
Recently he has been drinking hard, and yesterday evening he was very drunk; and when I came upstairs there was the key in the door.
近来他喝得厉害，昨天晚上他很醉，当我上楼时，门上的钥匙在门里。
I have no doubt at all that he had left it there.
我绝对确定他把钥匙放在那里了。
Mr. and Mrs. Rucastle were both downstairs, and the child was with them, so that I had an admirable opportunity.
鲁卡斯特夫妇都在楼下，孩子也在，所以我有一个绝佳的机会。
I turned the key gently in the lock, opened the door, and slipped through.
我轻轻地转动钥匙，打开了门，然后穿过。
“There was a little passage in front of me, unpapered and uncarpeted, which turned at a right angle at the farther end.
“在我前面有一个小通道，未纸未毯，转角在后面。
Round this corner were three doors in a line, the first and third of which were open.
在这条小道拐角处有三扇门，第一和第三扇是开着的。
They each led into an empty room, dusty and cheerless, with two windows in the one and one in the other, so thick with dirt that the evening light glimmered dimly through them.
每扇门通向一个空荡荡的房间，灰暗而无生气，有两个窗户在一间，另一个在另一间，上面布满灰尘，以至于晚上光线微弱地透过它们。
The centre door was closed, and across the outside of it had been fastened one of the broad bars of an iron bed, padlocked at one end to a ring in the wall, and fastened at the other with stout cord.
中心的门是关着的，外面的一扇门上有一个宽宽的铁床栏杆，锁在墙上的一端，另一端用结实的绳子锁住。
The door itself was locked as well, and the key was not there.
门本身也锁着，钥匙不在那里。
This barricaded door corresponded clearly with the shuttered window outside, and yet I could see by the glimmer from beneath it that the room was not in darkness.
这扇被封锁的门与外面的关闭的窗户相呼应，但我可以看到从下面的缝隙中透出微弱的光线，房间并不完全黑暗。
Evidently there was a skylight which let in light from above.
显然有一个天窗，从上面引入光线。

As I stood in the passage gazing at the sinister door and wondering what secret it might veil, I suddenly heard the sound of steps within the room and saw a shadow pass backward and forward against the little slit of dim light which shone out from under the door.
当我站在通道中，凝视着那邪恶的门，想着它可能隐藏什么秘密，突然听到房间里脚步声，看到一个影子在小缝的光线中前后移动。
A mad, unreasoning terror rose up in me at the sight, Mr. Holmes.
鲁斯卡斯特先生，我 Holmes，你感到一种疯狂的恐惧。
My overstrung nerves failed me suddenly, and I turned and ran—ran as though some dreadful hand were behind me clutching at the skirt of my dress.
我的神经突然绷紧，我转身就跑——跑得像有人在我背后抓着我的裙子似的。
I rushed down the passage, through the door, and straight into the arms of Mr. Rucastle, who was waiting outside.
我冲下走廊，穿过门，径直来到鲁卡斯特先生的身边，他正站在外面。
“‘So,’ said he, smiling, ‘it was you, then.
“‘是的，’他说，微笑着，“那正是你。”
I thought that it must be when I saw the door open.’
我心想，那一定是我看到门打开时。
“‘Oh, I am so frightened!’
“‘哦，我好怕啊！’”
I panted.
我喘着气。
“‘My dear young lady! my dear young lady!’—you cannot think how caressing and soothing his manner was—‘and what has frightened you, my dear young lady?’
“‘亲爱的小姐！亲爱的小姐！’——你一定想不到他那温柔体贴的样子——‘你为什么这么害怕，亲爱的小姐？’”
“But his voice was just a little too coaxing.
“但他的声音有点儿过分温柔。”
He overdid it.
他做得有点儿过分。
I was keenly on my guard against him.
我对他的过分温柔很警惕。
“‘I was foolish enough to go into the empty wing,’ I answered.
“‘我太蠢了，走进空荡荡的房间，’我回答说。
‘But it is so lonely and eerie in this dim light that I was frightened and ran out again.
“但因为光线昏暗，我感到很害怕，又跑了出来。
Oh, it is so dreadfully still in there!’
“哦，那里面太寂静了！”
“‘Only that?’ said he, looking at me keenly.
“‘只是这样吗？’他说，看着我。
“‘Why, what did you think?’
“‘为什么这样？’
I asked.
我问。
“‘Why do you think that I lock this door?’
‘为什么你认为我会锁这扇门？’
“‘I am sure that I do not know.’
‘我确信我没有知道。’
“‘It is to keep people out who have no business there.
‘那是为了把那些没有业务往那里的人挡在外面。’
Do you see?’
你看？
He was still smiling in the most amiable manner.
他仍然带着最和蔼的笑容。
“‘I am sure if I had known—’
‘我 certainty if I had known—’
“‘Well, then, you know now.
And if you ever put your foot over that threshold again’—here in an instant the smile hardened into a grin of rage, and he glared down at me with the face of a demon—‘I’ll throw you to the mastiff.’
And if you ever put your foot over that threshold again’—这里，他瞬间笑容变成了怒火，瞪着我，脸上像恶魔一样——“‘I’ll throw you to the mastiff.’
“I was so terrified that I do not know what I did.
“我如此害怕，以至于我不知道我做了什么。
I suppose that I must have rushed past him into my room.
我猜想我可能已经冲过了他走进我的房间。
I remember nothing until I found myself lying on my bed trembling all over.
我记不起任何事情，直到我发现自己躺在床上，全身颤抖。
Then I thought of you, Mr. Holmes.
然后我想起你，先生·霍尔姆斯。
I could not live there longer without some advice.
我不能在那里待下去，需要一些建议。
I was frightened of the house, of the man, of the woman, of the servants, even of the child.
我害怕这座房子，这个人，这个女人，甚至孩子。
They were all horrible to me.
他们对我都很可怕。
If I could only bring you down all would be well.
如果我能把你带下去一切都会好起来。
Of course I might have fled from the house, but my curiosity was almost as strong as my fears.
当然我可能从房子逃走，但我的好奇心几乎和恐惧一样强烈。
My mind was soon made up.
我很快决定了。
I would send you a wire.
我会给你发电报。
I put on my hat and cloak, went down to the office, which is about half a mile from the house, and then returned, feeling very much easier.
我戴上帽子和外套，走到离房子大约半英里远的办公室，然后返回，感觉轻松多了。

A horrible doubt came into my mind as I approached the door lest the dog might be loose, but I remembered that Toller had drunk himself into a state of insensibility that evening, and I knew that he was the only one in the household who had any influence with the savage creature, or who would venture to set him free.
我接近门时，心中生出一个可怕的念头，生怕狗会跑出来，但我记得托尔特尔那天晚上喝醉了，而且我知道他是家里唯一一个对野蛮人有影响力的人，或者敢于放走他的。
I slipped in in safety and lay awake half the night in my joy at the thought of seeing you.
我安全地溜进了房间，躺在床上，在想到见到你时的喜悦中彻夜难眠。

I had no difficulty in getting leave to come into Winchester this morning, but I must be back before three o’clock, for Mr. and Mrs. Rucastle are going on a visit, and will be away all the evening, so that I must look after the child.
我今天早上没有困难就能得到进入温彻斯特的许可，但必须在三点前回来，因为鲁卡斯特夫妇要去旅行，晚上会离开，所以我必须照顾孩子。
Now I have told you all my adventures, Mr. Holmes, and I should be very glad if you could tell me what it all means, and, above all, what I should do.”
现在我把我的冒险故事都告诉了你，先生·霍尔姆斯，我很乐意知道这一切的含义，尤其是我应该做什么。
Holmes and I had listened spellbound to this extraordinary story.
霍尔姆斯和我全神贯注地听这个非凡的故事。
My friend rose now and paced up and down the room, his hands in his pockets, and an expression of the most profound gravity upon his face.
我的朋友现在站起来，在房间里来回踱步，双手插在口袋里，脸上露出最深沉的严肃。
“Is Toller still drunk?” he asked.
“托尔特尔还喝醉了吗？”他问道。
“Yes.
“是的。
I heard his wife tell Mrs. Rucastle that she could do nothing with him.”
我听到妻子告诉鲁卡斯特夫人，她无法控制他。
“That is well.
那是很好。
And the Rucastles go out to-night?”
并且鲁卡斯特家今晚出去吧？
“Yes.”
是。
“Is there a cellar with a good strong lock?”
是否有带好锁的地下室？
“Yes, the wine-cellar.”
是的，酒窖。
“You seem to me to have acted all through this matter like a very brave and sensible girl, Miss Hunter.
你在我看来在整个这件事情上都像是一个非常勇敢而又理智的女孩，亨特小姐。
Do you think that you could perform one more feat?
你认为你能再做一件 feats?
I should not ask it of you if I did not think you a quite exceptional woman.”
如果你不是我非常exceptional的女人，我不应该向你提出这个要求。
“I will try.
我会试试。
What is it?”
“We shall be at the Copper Beeches by seven o’clock, my friend and I. The Rucastles will be gone by that time, and Toller will, we hope, be incapable.
我们将七点钟到达铜蜂角庄园，我的朋友。鲁卡斯庄园到那时已经离开，托勒庄园，我们希望，已经无法动弹。
There only remains Mrs. Toller, who might give the alarm.
只余托勒太太一人，她或许会报警。
If you could send her into the cellar on some errand, and then turn the key upon her, you would facilitate matters immensely.”
如果你可以让她去 cellar 做点事，然后锁上她的门，那就会大大方便事情了。
“I will do it.”
我要做。
“Excellent!
非常好！
We shall then look thoroughly into the affair.
我们将仔细调查此事。
Of course there is only one feasible explanation.
当然只有一个可行的解释。
You have been brought there to personate someone, and the real person is imprisoned in this chamber.
你被带到这里，是为了扮演一个人，而真正的那个人被关在这个房间里。
That is obvious.
显而易见。
As to who this prisoner is, I have no doubt that it is the daughter, Miss Alice Rucastle, if I remember right, who was said to have gone to America.
关于这个囚犯是谁，我肯定她就是鲁斯卡特小姐，我记得她曾经去美国。
You were chosen, doubtless, as resembling her in height, figure, and the colour of your hair.
你被选出来，很可能是因为你的身高、体型和头发的颜色与她相似。
Hers had been cut off, very possibly in some illness through which she has passed, and so, of course, yours had to be sacrificed also.
她的头发被剪掉了，很可能是由于她曾经生病，所以你的头发也必须被剪掉。
By a curious chance you came upon her tresses.
由于一个偶然的机会，你碰到了她的头发。
